A. 5, 92: vulnera, not mortal, curable, Plin. 10, 37, 52, § 109: saltus, free from noxious animals, id. 3, 5, 6, § 41: iter, secure, Tac. H. 4, 20: hinc vel illinc appellere indiscretum et innoxium est, id. ib. 3, 47 fin.— That does harm to none, not guilty, blameless, innocent: decet innocentem servum atque innoxium,
innoxius.short: in-noxĭus, a, um, adj., harmless, innoxious.

innubilo.full: in-nūbĭlo, 1, v. a., to cloud over, to overcast, make gloomy. Lit., Sol. 53, 24. — Trop.: serenitatem gaudii, Aug. Ep. 238.

innubilus.full: in-nūbĭlus, a, um, adj., unclouded, cloudless: aether, Lucr. 3, 21.
innubilus.short: in-nūbĭlus, a, um, adj., unclouded, cloudless: aether, Lucr.

innubis.full: innūbis, e, adj. 2. in-nubes, cloudless: dies, Sen. Herc. Oet. 238.

innubo.full: in-nūbo, psi, ptum, 3, v. n., to marry into. Lit.: quae haud facile iis, in quibus nata erat, humiliora sineret ea, quae innupsisset, into which she had married, Liv. 1, 34, 4: nostris thalamis, Ov. M. 7, 856. — Transf., to pass over, Lucil. ap. Non. 125, 10.

innubus.full: innŭbus, a, um, adj. 2. in-nubo, unmarried. Lit., Ov. M. 10, 567; 14, 142: Pallas, Aus. Epigr. 106; Val. Fl. 1, 87: diva, id. 4, 605.— Transf., of the laurel (because Daphne, who was never married, was changed into it): innuba laurus, Ov. M. 10, 92.

innucleatus.full: innū^clĕātus, a, um, adj. 2. in-nucleo, not stoned, from which the kernels are not taken out: uvae passae, Plin. Val. 1, 7.

innumerabilis.full: in-nŭmĕrābĭlis, e, adj., countless, innumerable (class.): mundi, Cic. Ac. 2, 17, 55; 1, 10, 25: atomi, id. N. D. 1, 20, 54: homines, id. de Or. 2, 38, 142: pecunia, id. Quint. 11, 37: series annorum, Hor. C. 3, 30, 4: numerus annorum, Gell. 14, 1, 18.— Absol.: reperiam multos vel innumerabiles potius quibus, etc., Cic. Fin. 2, 9, 28; Quint. 12, 2, 30; cf. innumerabilia, id. 3, 4, 2; 12, 1, 45.—Adv.: innŭmĕrābĭlĭter, innumerably, Lucr. 5, 274; Cic. de Or. 3, 52, 201; id. Div. 1, 14 fin.
innumerabilis.short: in-nŭmĕrābĭlis, e, adj., countless, innumerable (class.): mundi, Cic.

innumerabilitas.full: innŭmĕrābĭlĭtas, ātis, f. innumerabilis, countless number, innumerableness: mundorum, Cic. N. D. 1, 26, 73: atomorum, id. ib. 1, 39, 109; Arn. 3, p. 132 Herald.

innumeralis.full: in-nŭmĕrālis, e, adj., numberless, innumerable: numerus, Lucr. 2, 1086.
innumeralis.short: in-nŭmĕrālis, e, adj., numberless, innumerable: numerus, Lucr.

innumeratus.full: in-nŭmĕrātus, a, um, adj. 2. in-numero, unnumbered (late Lat.): miracula, Tert. adv. Marc. Carm. 2, 17.

innumerosus.full: in-nŭmĕrōsus, a, um, adj., countless (late Lat.): manus, Coripp. Joann. 5, 662: domini, Hilar. in Psa. 122, 6.
innumerosus.short: in-nŭmĕrōsus, a, um, adj., countless (late Lat.): manus, Coripp.

innumerus.full: in-nŭmĕrus, a, um, adj., countless, innumerable, numberless. In gen. (poet. and in post-Aug. prose; false reading instead of meri, Cic. de Or. 2, 22, 94; v. Orell. and Klotz): numerus, Lucr. 2, 1054: scaena est deserta, dein Risus, Ludu' jocusque, et numeri innumeri simul omnes collacrumarunt, verses without number, Plaut. or Varr. ap. Gell. 1, 24, 3: pecunia, Tac. A. 14, 53: innumeras adversariorum copias superare, Suet. Caes. 68 med.; id. Galb. 6: turba, id. Calig. 26: post proelii innumeras c
innumerus.short: in-nŭmĕrus, a, um, adj., countless, innumerable, numberless.

innuo.full: in-nŭo, ŭi, ūtum, 3, v. n., to give a nod, to nod to; to give a sign, to intimate, hint. With dat.: ubi ego innuero vobis, Plaut. Rud. 3, 4, 26: abiens innuit mihi, Ter. Eun. 4, 5, 9: stabat innuebat digito similis vocanti, Plin. Ep. 7, 27, 9.— Absol.: ne mora sit, si innuerim, quin pugnus in mala haereat, Ter. Ad. 2, 1, 17: ubi innuerint, Liv. 8, 4, 2: coram licet innuat atque Rescribat, Juv. 6, 140: aqua innuetur his signis esse tenus, Vitr. 8, 5 ext.— To mean, intimate, signify, = significo,

innuptus.full: in-nuptus, a, um, adj. 2. in-nubo, unmarried. Lit. Adj.: pueri innuptaeque puellae, Verg. G. 4, 476: Minerva, virginal, virgin-, id. A. 2, 31: manus, the Amazons, Sil. 2, 75.— Subst.: innupta, ae, f., an unmarried woman, a virgin, Cat. 62, 6; 12; 36; 64, 78; Prop. 3, 19, 25; Verg. A. 12, 24: praegnans, Arn. in Luc. 2, 2.— Transf.: innuptae nuptiae (γάμος ἄγαμος), a marriage that is no marriage, an unhappy marriage, Poëta ap. Cic. de Or. 3, 58, 219 (Trag. Fragm. Inc. v. 80 Rib.).

innutribilis.full: in-nūtrībĭlis, e, adj., not nourishing: juscellum, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 9, 55.
innutribilis.short: in-nūtrībĭlis, e, adj., not nourishing: juscellum, Cael.

innutrio.full: in-nūtrĭo, īvi, ītum, 4, v. a., to nourish or bring up in any thing (post-Aug.): ne castris innutriretur et armis, Sil. 2, 286.— Part. perf.: indigenae atque ipsius provinciae finibus innutriti, Cod. Th. 7, 13, 6, § 1: mari innutritus, Plin. Ep. 9, 33, 6: amplis opibus, Suet. Aug. 3: bellicis laudibus, Plin. Pan. 16, 1: caelestium praeceptorum disciplinis, Vell. 2, 94, 1: liberalibus disciplinis, Sen. Cons. ad Polyb. 21 fin.: certis ingeniis innutriri oportet, id. Ep. 2.

innutritus1.full: innūtrītus, a, um, Part., from innutrio.
innutritus1.short: innūtrītus, a, um, Part., from innutrio.

innutritus2.full: in-nūtrītus, a, um, adj. 2. in-nutrio, not nourished, without nourishment, Cael. Aur. Acut. 17, 1, 17, § 177.

ino.full: īnō, ūs, f. (Ino, ōnis, Hyg. Fab. 2), daughter of Cadmus and Harmonia, sister of Semele, wife of Athamas king of Thebes, nurse of Bacchus, mother of Learchus and Melicerta, and step-mother of Phrixus and Helle. Being pursued by Athamas, who had become raving mad, she threw herself with Melicerta into the sea, whereupon they were both changed into sea-deities. Ino, as such, was called Matuta (Gr. Leucothea), and Melicerta Palaemon or Portumnus, Cic. Tusc. 1, 12, 28; Ov. M. 4, 416 sq.; id. F. 6, 4

inobjurgatus.full: ĭn-objurgātus, a, um, adj., not scolded, not blamed, Charis. p. 41 P.
inobjurgatus.short: ĭn-objurgātus, a, um, adj., not scolded, not blamed, Charis.

inoblector.full: ĭn-oblector, āri, v. dep., to take delight in any thing (late Lat.): in filiis hominum, Tert. adv. Hermog. 18.

inobliteratus.full: ĭn-oblītĕrātus, a, um, adj., not obliterated, unforgotten: scientia, Tert. Anim. 24.
inobliteratus.short: ĭn-oblītĕrātus, a, um, adj., not obliterated, unforgotten: scientia, Tert.

inoblitus.full: ĭn-oblītus, a, um, adj., not forgetful, mindful, Ov. P. 4, 15, 37.
inoblitus.short: ĭn-oblītus, a, um, adj., not forgetful, mindful, Ov.

inoboediens.full: ĭnŏboedĭens and ĭnŏboedĭenter, v. inoboedio fin.

inoboedientia.full: ĭn-ŏboedĭentĭa, ae, f., disobedience (late Lat.), Aug. Civ. Dei, 14, 17; Hier. Quaest. Hebr. ad Reg. 2, 1.—In the form ĭnŏbaudĭentĭa, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 17 fin.
inoboedientia.short: ĭn-ŏboedĭentĭa, ae, f., disobedience (late Lat.), Aug.

inoboedio.full: ĭn-ŏboedĭo (or ĭnŏbaudĭo, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 16), īre, v. n., to disobey, be disobedient, Ambros. Serm. Epiph. 1. — Hence, ĭnŏboedĭens, entis, P. a., disobedient, Vulg. Interp. Deut. 8, 20; ib. Tit. 1, 10. — Adv.: ĭnŏboedĭenter, disobediently, Aug. Civ. Dei, 14, 17.

inoboedus.full: ĭnŏboedus, a, um, adj. inoboedio, disobedient: cessatio (al. in obeundo), Arn. 7, 248.

inobrutus.full: ĭn-obrŭtus, a, um, adj., not overwhelmed, Ov. M. 7, 356.
inobrutus.short: ĭn-obrŭtus, a, um, adj., not overwhelmed, Ov.

inobsaeptus.full: ĭn-obsaeptus, a, um, adj. in-obsaepio, not hedged up, not closed, open: foramina aurium, Lact. Opif. D. 8, 7.

inobscurabilis.full: ĭn-obscūrābĭlis, e, adj., that cannot be obscured (late Lat.): regula, Tert. Anim. 3.
inobscurabilis.short: ĭn-obscūrābĭlis, e, adj., that cannot be obscured (late Lat.): regula, Tert.

inobscuro.full: ĭn-obscūro, āre, a false read. in Cic. Phil. 9, 5, 10, instead of obscurabit.

inobsequens.full: ĭn-obsĕquens, entis, adj., not yielding, uncomplying, disobedient, Sen. praef. Q. N. fin.: equi frenis, id. Hippol. 1068.— Absol.: contumaces et inobsequentes, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 17 fin.
inobsequens.short: ĭn-obsĕquens, entis, adj., not yielding, uncomplying, disobedient, Sen.

inobsequentia.full: ĭn-obsĕquentĭa, ae, f., disobedience, Jul. Valer. Res Gest. Alex. M. 2, 21 Mai.

inobservabilis.full: ĭn-observābĭlis, e. adj., that cannot be observed, unobservable: cursus, Plin. 2, 17, 15, § 77: error, Cat. 64, 115.

inobservans.full: ĭn-observans, antis, adj., unobservant: homines, Pall. 1, 35, 12.
inobservans.short: ĭn-observans, antis, adj., unobservant: homines, Pall.

inobservantia.full: ĭnobservantĭa, ae, f. inobservans, inattention, negligence, irregularity: quae ne fecisse inobservantia quadam videatur, Quint. 4, 2, 107; Suet. Aug. 76.

inobservatus.full: ĭn-observātus, a, um, adj., unobserved, unperceived, Ov. M. 2, 544; 4, 341: et incertum tempus, Sen. Q. N. 3, 26 med.: sidera, Ov. F. 3, 111: columba, Mart. 8, 32, 3.
inobservatus.short: ĭn-observātus, a, um, adj., unobserved, unperceived, Ov.

inobsoletus.full: ĭn-obsŏlētus, a, um, adj., not grown old: vestimenta, Tert. Res. Carn. 58.
inobsoletus.short: ĭn-obsŏlētus, a, um, adj., not grown old: vestimenta, Tert.

inocciduus.full: ĭn-occĭdŭus, a, um, adj., never setting. Lit.: axis, the north pole, Luc. 8, 175.— Transf.: visus, ever open eyes, Stat. Th. 6, 277: ignes, inextinguishable, Claud. Rapt. Pros. 3, 400: vita continua et inoccidua, Arn. 2, 68.
inocciduus.short: ĭn-occĭdŭus, a, um, adj., never setting.

inocco.full: ĭn-occo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a., to harrow in: semen inoccatum, Col. 2, 8, 4; 11, 2, 82: pastinatio inoccata, id. 3, 15, 1.

inoccultus.full: ĭn-occultus, a, um, adj., not secret, Quint. 7, 9, 5 dub. (al. incultus).
inoccultus.short: ĭn-occultus, a, um, adj., not secret, Quint.

inoculatio.full: ĭnŏcŭlātĭo, ōnis, f. inoculo, an inoculating, ingrafting, Col. 5, 11, 1; 11, 2, 54; Pall. 7, 5. (An earlier method of inoculating is described in Plin. 17, 14, 23, § 100; cf. id. 17, 16, 26, § 118.)

inoculator.full: ĭnŏcŭlātor, ōris, m. id., an inoculator, ingrafter, Plin. 18, 33, 76, § 329.

inoculo.full: ĭn-ŏcŭlo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a., to inoculate, i. e. to ingraft an eye or bud of one tree into another (post-Aug.). Lit.: arbores ficorum, Col. 11, 2, 59.— Transf. To implant: justitiae affectum pectoribus, Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 1.— To adorn: bullis aureis inoculatus, App. M. 6, p. 185, 21.

inodiatus.full: ĭnŏdĭātus, a, um, adj. 2. in-odium, not hated: odiosus, inodiatus, Not. Tir. p. 77.

inodoro.full: ĭn-ŏdōro, 1, v. a., to scent, cause to smell: mandentium halitus, Col. 11, 3, 22.

inodoror.full: ĭn-ŏdōror, ātus sum, 1, formerly regarded as v. dep., to smell out, trace out: mirabiliter inodoratus est, Cic. Att. 2, 25, 1, where Orell., B. and K., al. now read moratus.
inodoror.short: ĭn-ŏdōror, ātus sum, 1, formerly regarded as v.

inodorus.full: ĭn-ŏdōrus, a, um, adj. Without smell, inodorous: ossa, unperfumed, Pers. 6, 35: flos, App. M. 4, p. 143, 16.— Without the sense of smell: animalia, Gell. 7, 6 (also ap. Non. 129, 11).

inoffensus.full: ĭn-offensus, a, um, adj., not struck; without stumbling, without hinderance, unobstructed, uninjured (poet. and in postAug. prose). Lit.: cogit inoffensae currus accedere metae, untouched, not grazed, Luc. 8, 201: voluptatis regionisque abundantiam inoffensa transmitteres, Plin. Ep. 6, 4, 2: inoffensum pedem referre, not stumbling, Tib. 1, 7, 62.— Transf., that goes on without hinderance, without obstacle, unhindered, uninterrupted: lumen oculorum, Pall. 1, 3: inoffensae metam tangere vitae, pla
inoffensus.short: ĭn-offensus, a, um, adj., not struck;

inofficiositas.full: ĭnoffĭcĭōsĭtas, ātis, f. inofficiosus, disobligingness, Salv. Ep. 3: Ruricius, Ep. 2, 15.

inofficiosus.full: ĭn-offĭcĭōsus, a, um, adj., undutiful, inofficious. In gen. Not observant of his duty, undutiful: humana gens inofficiosa dei, Tert. Apol. 40: libertus inofficiosus patrono, Dig. 37, 14, 1.— Contrary to one's duty: testamentum, i. e. one in which nothing is left to one's nearest relatives, children, etc., Cic. Verr. 1, 42, 107; cf. Dig. 5, 2.— In partic., not obliging, disobliging: in aliquem, Cic. Att. 13, 27, 1.
inofficiosus.short: ĭn-offĭcĭōsus, a, um, adj., undutiful, inofficious.

inolens.full: ĭn-ŏlens, entis, adj., without smell, inodorous: olivum, Lucr. 2, 850.
inolens.short: ĭn-ŏlens, entis, adj., without smell, inodorous: olivum, Lucr.

inolesco.full: ĭn-ŏlesco, lēvi, ŏlĭtum, 3, v. n. and a. (inolesti, Aus. Grat. Act. § 36). Neutr., to grow in, on, or to any thing. Lit.: udo libro, Verg. G. 2, 77: necesse est multa diu concreta modis inolescere miris, id. A. 6, 738; Sil. 8, 583: tradux a materno sustinetur ubere dum inolescat, Col. 4, 29, 14.— Trop.: assidua veterum scriptorum tractatione inoleverat linguae illius vox, i. e. had remained fixed in his mind, Gell. 5, 21, 3: quae nosti, meditando velis inolescere menti, Aus. Ep. 141.— Act., to i

inominalis.full: ĭn-ōmĭnālis, e, adj., unlucky, illomened, inauspicious: dies, Gell. 5, 17, 3; Macr. S. 1, 16, § 26.
inominalis.short: ĭn-ōmĭnālis, e, adj., unlucky, illomened, inauspicious: dies, Gell.

inominatus.full: ĭn-ōmĭnātus, a, um, adj., ill-omened, inauspicious: cubilia, Hor. Epod. 16, 38.
inominatus.short: ĭn-ōmĭnātus, a, um, adj., ill-omened, inauspicious: cubilia, Hor.

inopaco.full: ĭn-ŏpāco, 1, v. a., to overshadow, Col. 8, 15, 4.

inopacus.full: ĭn-ŏpācus, a, um, adj., not shady: inopacus, ἄσκιος, Gloss. Philox.
inopacus.short: ĭn-ŏpācus, a, um, adj., not shady: inopacus, ἄσκιος, Gloss.

inoperatus.full: ĭn-ŏpĕrātus, a, um, adj., unoccupied, inactive: bonitas, Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 11.— Not wrought, Ambros. de Fid. 3, 14, 113.
inoperatus.short: ĭn-ŏpĕrātus, a, um, adj., unoccupied, inactive: bonitas, Tert.

inopero.full: ĭn-ŏpĕro, āre, v. a., to effect, produce (eccl. Lat.): hoc inoperatur per Deum Patrem, Rufin. Orig. de Principp. 1, 3, 7.

inoperor.full: ĭn-ŏpĕror, āri, v. dep., to effect, operate, produce (eccl. Lat.): ille inoperatus est in Christum valentiam suam, Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 17 (ex adv. Ephes. 1).

inopertus.full: ĭn-ŏpertus, a, um, adj., uncovered, bare. Lit.: corpora, Prud. Cath. 3, 117: capite inoperto, Sen. Vit. Beat. 13.— Trop., naked: ac confessa veritas, Sen. Ot. Sap. 30.
inopertus.short: ĭn-ŏpertus, a, um, adj., uncovered, bare.

inopia.full: ĭn-ŏpĭa, ae, f. inops, want, lack, scarcity. In gen.: argenti, Plaut. Curc. 2, 3, 55: summa rerum omnium, Caes. B. G. 5, 2: frumenti commeatusque, id. ib. 3, 6: frumenti, Sall. J. 91, 1; cf.: frumentaria, Caes. B. G. 5, 24: et amore pereo et inopia argentaria, Plaut. Ps. 1, 3, 66: loci, Liv. 1, 33, 6: advocatorum, Tac. A. 11, 7: consilii, Cic. Att. 6, 3, 2: criminum, id. Rosc. Am. 16, 48: occasionis, Suet. Cal. 56: remedii, Tac. A. 13, 57: veri, id. H. 1, 35 al.— In partic., a want, esp. of nece

inopinabilis.full: ĭn-ŏpīnābĭlis, e, adj., not to be supposed or expected, inconceivable: latebra, Gell. 17, 9, 18: id (dictum), id. 11, 18, 11: res, Aur. Vict. Caes. 39.— Esp., rhet. t. t., surprising, paradoxical: infames materias, sive quis mavult dicere inopinabiles, quas Graeci ἀδόξους ὑποθέσεις appellant, veteres adorti sunt, Gell. 17, 12, 1.—Adv.: inŏpīnābĭlĭter, unexpectedly, Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 1, 3; 8, 1.
inopinabilis.short: ĭn-ŏpīnābĭlis, e, adj., not to be supposed or expected, inconceivable: latebra, Gell.

inopinans.full: ĭn-ŏpīnans, antis, adj., not expecting, unaware (freq. in the historians; not in Cic.): inscios inopinantesque Menapios oppresserunt, Caes. B. G. 4, 4: impeditos et inopinantes aggressus, id. ib. 1, 12: imprudente atque inopinante Curione, id. B. C. 2, 3: rex in potestatem inopinanti (ei) venerat, Nep. Dat. 3, 4: suis inopinantibus, Liv. 27, 48, 14.— Hence, adv.: ĭnŏpīnanter, unexpectedly, Suet. Tib. 60.
inopinans.short: ĭn-ŏpīnans, antis, adj., not expecting, unaware (freq.

inopinate.full: ĭnŏpīnātē and ĭnŏpīnātō, advv., v. inopinatus fin.

inopinatus.full: ĭn-ŏpīnātus, a, um, not expected, unexpected (class.). Adj.: cum hoc illi improvisum atque inopinatum accidisset, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 28, § 69: nova tibi haec sunt et inopinata? id. ib. 2, 2, 8, § 24: neque novum neque inopinatum mihi sit, Liv. 6, 40, 3: nec hoc tam re est, quam dictu inopinatum atque mirabile, Cic. Par. 5, 1, § 35: malum, Caes. B. C. 2, 12: finis vitae, Suet. Caes. 87: fraus, Sil. 7, 133: id quoque scriptum est, quod volgo inopinatum est, contrary to the common belief, Gell. 11, 1
inopinatus.short: ĭn-ŏpīnātus, a, um, not expected, unexpected (class.).

inopinor.full: ĭn-ŏpīnor, ātus sum, 1, v. dep., to suppose, think, opine: Alexander facilius inopinatus, Val. Res Gest. Alex. M. 1, 52 Mai. (but a false read. for opinor, Gell. 18, 7, 5).

inopinus.full: ĭn-ŏpīnus, a, um, adj., unexpected (poet. and in post-Aug. prose = in-opinatus, insperatus): quies, Verg. A. 5, 857: nova inopinave facies laborum, id. ib. 6, 104: fors, id. ib. 8, 476: visus, Ov. M. 4, 232: siccitas, Plin. Pan. 30, 2; Tac. A. 1, 68.

inopiosus.full: ĭnŏpĭōsus, a, um, adj. inops, in want of something: res inopiosae consilii, Plaut. Poen. 1, 1, 2.

inoppidatus.full: ĭn-oppĭdātus, a, um, adj., that has no town, not dwelling in a town (late Lat.): Gabalitani sparsi, inoppidati, Sid. Ep. 5, 13; cf.: inoppidatus ἀοίκητος, Gloss. Philox.
inoppidatus.short: ĭn-oppĭdātus, a, um, adj., that has no town, not dwelling in a town (late Lat.): Gabalitani sparsi, inoppidati, Sid.

inopportunus.full: ĭn-opportūnus, unfitting (late Lat.), Oros. c. Pelag. p. 618 (also a false reading in two places for importunus, Cic. de Or. 2, 5, 20; 3, 5, 18). — Hence, ĭnopportūnē, adv., unsuitably, untimely, Aug. c. Faust. 22, 72.

inops.full: ĭnops, ŏpis, adj. 2. in-opis, without resources, helpless, weak (class.). In gen.: ab ope inops, qui ejus indiget, Varr. L. L. 5, § 92 Müll.: inopes relicti a duce, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 34: nihil cum potentiore juris humani relinquitur inopi, Liv. 9, 1, 8: solare inopem et succurre relictae, Verg. A. 9, 290.— With ab: sic inopes et ab amicis, et ab existimatione sunt, Cic. Att. 1, 1, 2. — With inf.: inopes laudis conscendere carmen, unable, Prop. 2, 10, 23 (3, 1, 23 Müll.).— In partic., helpless thr

inoptabilis.full: ĭn-optābĭlis, e, adj., undesirable, unpleasant: officinae disciplina, App. M. 9, p. 222, 24.
inoptabilis.short: ĭn-optābĭlis, e, adj., undesirable, unpleasant: officinae disciplina, App.

inoptatus.full: ĭn-optātus, a, um, adj., undesired, unpleasant: res, Sen. Exc. Contr. 8, 6, § 5.
inoptatus.short: ĭn-optātus, a, um, adj., undesired, unpleasant: res, Sen.

inopus.full: Īnōpus, i, m. Ἰνωπός, a fountain and river in the island of Delos, where Latona brought forth Apollo and Diana. It is said to have risen and fallen at the same time with the Nile, and hence was supposed to be connected with it by a subterraneous channel, Plin. 2, 103, 166, § 229; Val. Fl. 5, 105.

inorabilis.full: ĭnōrābĭlis, e, false reading for evocabili, Att. ap. Non. 487, 15; v. Att. Trag. Fragm. v. 158 Rib.
inorabilis.short: ĭnōrābĭlis, e, false reading for evocabili, Att.

inoratus.full: ĭn-ōrātus, a, um, adj., not pleaded: incertā re atque inoratā, i. e. without obtaining a hearing, Enn. ap. Non. 166, 23 (Trag. v. 12 Vahl.): legati Ameriam re inorata reverterunt, Cic. Rosc. Am. 9, 26.
inoratus.short: ĭn-ōrātus, a, um, adj., not pleaded: incertā re atque inoratā, i.

inordinaliter.full: ĭnordĭnālĭter, adv. 2. in-ordinalis, irregularly: scarificandum, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 4, 36.

inordinate.full: ĭnordĭnātē and ĭnordĭnātim, advv., v. inordinatus fin.

inordinatio.full: ĭn-ordĭnātĭo, ōnis, f., disorder, App. Trism. p. 92, 1; Cod. Just. 3, 43, 3.

inordinatus.full: ĭn-ordĭnātus, a, um, adj., not arranged, disordered, irregular: inordinati et incompositi milites, Liv. 22, 50, 8: hostes, id. 35, 29, 5: inordinati in proelium ruunt, id. 23, 27, 5: ordo, App. M. p. 292 Oud. — Sup.: inordinatissimi pili, Plin. 22, 22, 45, § 91.—In neutr. absol.: idque ex inordinato in ordinem adduxit, disorder, Cic. Univ. 3, 7; Quint. 1, 10, 46; 8, 2, 23; 10, 4, 1.—Adv. in two forms. ĭnordĭnātē, irregularly: febres redire, Cels. 3, 3; so 1, 4. — ĭnordĭnātim, irregularly: acies
inordinatus.short: ĭn-ordĭnātus, a, um, adj., not arranged, disordered, irregular: inordinati et incompositi milites, Liv.

inordino.full: ĭn-ordĭno, 1, v. a., to arrange, bring into order: inordinandi soli duo sunt tempora, Col. 11, 3, 9 dub. (al. ordinandi).

inorior.full: ĭn-ŏrĭor, false reading for oreretur, Tac. A. 11, 23.
inorior.short: ĭn-ŏrĭor, false reading for oreretur, Tac.

inoris.full: ĭn-ōris, e, adj. ōs, without a mouth, Paul. ex Fest. p. 114 Müll. N. cr.

inormis.full: ĭnormis, e, adj. 2. in-norma, immoderate, enormous, Spart. Anton. Get. 6, 2; Ael. Ver. 1, 3 acc. to Salmas (al. enormis).

inornatus.full: ĭn-ornātus, a, um, adj., unadorned (syn. incomptus): mulieres, Cic. Or. 23, 78; cf. capilli, Ov. M. 1, 497; 5, 472; and, crines, id. ib. 9, 3: Lysias tenuis atque inornatus, Cic. Or. 9, 29; so Quint. 4, 2, 46; 8, 3, 50; 59 al.: nomina et verba, plain, common, Hor. A. P. 234: non ego te meis Chartis inornatum silebo, uncelebrated, id. C. 4, 9, 31.— Adv.: ĭnornātē, without ornament, inelegantly: dicere, Auct. Her. 4, 31, 42.—Comp.: inornatius scribere, Fronto ad Verum Imp. ep. 1 med. Mai.

inorno.full: ĭn-orno, 1, v. a., to adorn (late Lat.): flosculi inornantur, Tert. Anim. 19; id. adv. Val. 12.

inoro.full: ĭn-ōro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a., to crown the brim of a drinking-vessel: calix de coronis quoque potatoris inorabitur (al. inornabitur), Tert. Res. Carn. 16.

inorus.full: ĭnōrus, a, um, adj. 2. in-os, without a mouth: ostreae, Turp. ap. Non. 216, 8 (Com. Rel. v. 23 Rib.; cf. Müll. ad Fest. p. 114).

inotiosus.full: ĭn-ōtĭōsus, a, um, adj., not idle, busy (ἄσχολος): actio, Quint. 11, 3, 183.
inotiosus.short: ĭn-ōtĭōsus, a, um, adj., not idle, busy (ἄσχολος): actio, Quint.

inous.full: Īnōüs, a, um, adj., v. Ino fin.

inquaesitus.full: in-quaesītus, a, um, adj., i. q. inquisitus, sought for, Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 3.

inquam.full: inquam (the foll. forms are found: inquam and inquit very freq.; v. infra; first pers., inquio, found in late writers: si igitur, inquio, Jul. ap. Aug. c. Saec. Resp. Jul. 4, 9, is not in good use, but mentioned by Vel. Long. ap. Cassiod. Orthogr. p. 2287; Prisc. 8, 11, 62; cf. inquo, Eutych. 2, 12, p. 2182: inquis, Cic. Caecin. 13, 37; id. Fam. 2, 12, 3; 9, 26, 1; id. Att. 2, 5, 8; Hor. S. 2, 1, 5; Mart. 2, 93, 1 saep.: inquĭmus, Hor. S. 1, 3, 66: inquitis, Arn. 2, 44; Tert. Apol. 9 al.: inquiu

inquassatus.full: in-quassātus, a, um, adj., unbroken: inquassatus, ἄθραυστος, Gloss. Philox.
inquassatus.short: in-quassātus, a, um, adj., unbroken: inquassatus, ἄθραυστος, Gloss.

inquies1.full: in-quĭes, ētis, f., restlessness, unquietness: nocturna, Plin. 14, 22, 28, § 142: vigiliarum, Gell. 19, 9, 5: infantis (in utero), Tert. Anim. 25.
inquies1.short: in-quĭes, ētis, f., restlessness, unquietness: nocturna, Plin.

inquies2.full: in-quĭes, ētis, adj. (abl. inquieti, App. M. 9, 42), restless, unquiet: homo, Sall. Fragm. ap. Prisc. p. 704 P.: vir, Vell. 2, 68: animus, Plin. prooem. § 16 (al. in quiete): inquies atque indomitum ingenium, Sall. H. Fragm. 1, 7 Dietsch: Germanus spe, cupidine, Tac. A. 1, 68: animo, id. ib. 16, 14: animus, Vell. 2, 77, 2: ad libidinem, App. M. 2, p. 122 fin.

inquiescens.full: inquĭescens, false reading for increscente, App. M. 9, p. 218.
inquiescens.short: inquĭescens, false reading for increscente, App.

inquietatio.full: inquĭētātĭo, ōnis, f. inquieto, disturbance, agitation, Sen. Suas. 2; Marc. Emp. 8, 1 (but false reading for irrita quassatio, Liv. 22, 17, 3).

inquietator.full: inquĭētātor, ōris, m. id., a disturber: animarum, Tert. Spect. 23; Cod. Th. 6, 10, 1.

inquieto.full: in-quĭēto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a., to disquiet, disturb (syn. sollicitare): nares digito, Quint. 11, 3, 80: mentem, Sen. Vit. Beat. 12: nullis rumoribus inquietari, Plin. Ep. 1, 9, 5: tam multis libellis et tam querulis inquietor, id. ib. 9, 15, 1: num alio genere furiarum declamatores inquietantur, Petr. init.: victoriam, Tac. H. 3, 84: aliquem litibus, Suet. Ner. 34: matrimonium quiescens, by an accusation of adultery, Dig. 48, 5, 26: inquietatus fremitu, Suet. Calig. 26.

inquietudo.full: inquĭētūdo, ĭnis, f. inquieto, restlessness, disquietude. In gen.: de aliqua re sustinere, Cod. 7, 14, 5.— In partic., feverishness, Marc. Emp. 20 med.: capitis inquietudo, Sol. 1.

inquietus.full: in-quĭētus, a, um, adj., restless, unquiet (not in Cic. or Cæs.; freq. in Liv.): animus, Liv. 1, 46, 2: ingenia, id. 22, 21, 2: lux deinde noctem inquieta insecuta est, id. 5, 52, 6: praecordia, Hor. Epod. 5, 95: inquieta urbs auctionibus, Tac. H. 1, 20: vita oratorum, id. Or. 13 init.: tempora, id. ib. 37: Marius, Vell. 2, 11, 2: noctes, Val. Max. 8, 14, ext. 1: littora saeviente fluctu inquieta, Sen. Suas. 1, 2: infantes, Plin. 28, 19, 78, § 259: Adria, Hor. C. 3, 3, 5: inertia. busy idleness,
inquietus.short: in-quĭētus, a, um, adj., restless, unquiet (not in Cic.

inquilinatus.full: inquĭlīnātus, ūs, m. inquilinus, an inhabiting of a place which is not one's own, sojourning: inquilinatūs tempus, Tert. Anim. 38 fin.; Sid. Ep. 5, 19.

inquilino.full: inquĭlīno, 1, v. a. id., to be an inhabitant or sojourner: inquilino, ἐνοικέω, Gloss. Philox.

inquilinus1.full: inquĭlīnus, a, m. and f. incolinus, colo, an inhabitant of a place which is not his own, a sojourner, tenant, lodger (cf. incola). Lit. Padi, Plin. 21, 12, 43, § 73: Massilienses, qui nunc inquilini videantur, quandoque dominos regionum futuros, Just. 43, 4: fabrum inquilinum et ferrarium vicinum, Sen. Ep. 56, 4: te inquilino (non enim domino) personabat omnia, Cic. Phil. 2, 41, 105: inquilini privatarum aedium atque insularum, Suet. Ner. 44.— An inmate or lodger: inquilinus, qui eundem colit fo

inquilinus2.full: inquĭlīnus, a, um, adj., of foreign birth: civis urbis Romae, Sall. C. 31, 7.
inquilinus2.short: inquĭlīnus, a, um, adj., of foreign birth: civis urbis Romae, Sall.

inquinabulum.full: inquĭnābŭlum, i, n. inquino, filth: inquinabulum, μόλυμμα, Gloss. Philox.

inquinamentum.full: inquĭnāmentum, i, n. id., filth, Vitr 8, 5; Gell. 2, 6, 25.

inquinatio.full: inquĭnātio, ōnis, f. inquino, a defiling: animarum, Vulg. Sap. 14, 26.

inquinatus.full: inquĭnātus, a, um, P. a., from inquino.

inquino.full: inquĭno, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. cunire, acc. to Paul. ex Fest. p. 50 Müll., to befoul, stain, pollute, defile (syn.: polluo, contamino, conspurco). Lit.: vestem, Plaut. Capt. 2, 2, 17: mentior at si quid, merdis caput inquiner albis Corvorum, Hor. S. 1, 8, 37: ruris opes niteant: inquinet arma situs, Ov. F. 4, 928: (gurgitem) venenis, id. M. 14, 56: segetem injecto lolio, Dig. 9, 2, 27. — Trop., to pollute, defile, corrupt, contaminate: saepe unus puer petulans atque impurus inquinat gregem pueroru

inquiro.full: inquīro, sīvi, sītum, 3, v. a. in-quaero, to seek after, search for, inquire into any thing (cf. anquirere). Lit.: vera illa honestas, quam natura maxime inquirit, Cic. Tusc. 3, 2, 3: omnia ordine, Liv. 22, 7, 11: sedes, Just. 3, 4: inquire in ea quae memoriae sunt prodita, Cic. Leg. 1, 1, 4: de opere, Quint. 3, 11, 21: verborum originem, id. 1, 6, 28: aliquibus inquirenda quaedam mandare, id. 10, 1, 128: vitia (alicujus), Hor. S. 1, 3, 28: quid sit furere, id. ib. 2, 3, 41.— Trop. Jurid., to se

inquisitio.full: inquīsītĭo, ōnis, f. inquiro, a seeking or searching for. Lit.: tu cave inquisitioni mihi sis, be at hand, don't let me have to look for you, Plaut. Cas. 3, 1 fin.: novorum militum, Curt. 4, 6: corporum, Plin. 8. 30, 44, § 106.— Transf., a searching or inquiring into, an examination. In gen.: veri inquisitio atque investigatio, Cic. Off. 1, 4, 13: opinionum, Quint. 3, 1, 2: nova inquisitione addiscere, Plin. 2, 46, 45, § 117. — In partic., a seeking for proofs or grounds in support of an accusat

inquisitor.full: inquīsītor, ōris, m. id., a searcher. Lit., one who searches for a suspected person, an inquisitor, tracker, detective, spy: scrutatur vestigia (canis) atque persequitur, comitantem ad feram inquisitorem loro trahens, the hunter, Plin. 8, 40, 61, § 147: se ab inquisitoribus pecunia redimere, Suet. Caes. 1: inquisitores algae, they who search the very sea-weed, Juv. 4, 49.— Transf., an examiner, investigator. In gen.: rerum inquisitorem decet esse sapientem, Cic. Fragm. Ac. ap. Aug. cont. Ac. 2,

inquisitus1.full: inquīsītus, a, um, v. inquiro fin.

inquisitus2.full: inquīsītus, a, um, adj. 2. in-quaero, not searched or inquired into (Plautin.): res, Plaut. Am. 2, 2, 217: quaestio, id. ib. 4, 1, 9.

inr.full: inr-. For words beginning thus, v. irr-.

inrectus.full: in-rectus, a, um, adj., not straight, crooked: vulpinari dictum ab inrecto, seu intorto vulpium cursu, Non. 46, 24.
inrectus.short: in-rectus, a, um, adj., not straight, crooked: vulpinari dictum ab inrecto, seu intorto vulpium cursu, Non.

insaepio.full: in-saepĭo, īre, saeptus, 4, v. a., to hedge in, enclose: ingenti muro, Sen. Ben. 4, 19, 1.

insaeptio.full: insaeptio, ōnis, f. insaepio, a defined surface, facet, Sen. Q. N. 1, 7, 3.

insaeptus2.full: in-saeptus, a, um, adj., not hedged in, not enclosed, Paul. ex Fest. 95, 111 Müll.
insaeptus2.short: in-saeptus, a, um, adj., not hedged in, not enclosed, Paul.

insaevio.full: in-saevĭo, īre, 4, v. n., to fall into a passion, Ambros. de Jos. Patr. 3, 11; Cassiod. Var. 1, 37.

insalubris.full: in-sălūbris, e, adj., unwholesome. Unhealthy, insalubrious: fundus, Plin. 18, 5, 6, § 27: in medicina alia salubria, alia insalubria, Quint. 3, 2, 3.—Comp.: insalubrius, Gell. 19, 5, 7. — Sup.: vinum insaluberrimum, Plin. 23, 1, 22, § 40.— Unseruiceable, unprofitable, useless: meridiem vineas spectare colono insalubre est, Plin. 17, 2, 2, § 20. — Adv.: insălūbrĭter, unwholesomely, unserviceably, unprofitably, Salv. ap. Avar. 3, p. 90: indulgere naturae, id. ib. p. 92.

insalutaris.full: in-sălūtāris, e, adj., not healthful; plur.: cogitationes, Hilar. in Psa. 118, 13, 14 (also a false read. for salutare, App. M. 2, p. 117, 25).

insalutatus.full: in-sălūtātus, a, um, adj., ungreeted, unsaluted: annis jam multis insalutatus, Sid. Ep. 4, 10; 9, 9; Hier. Ep. 3, 1; in tmesis: inque salutatam linquo, Verg. A. 9, 288.
insalutatus.short: in-sălūtātus, a, um, adj., ungreeted, unsaluted: annis jam multis insalutatus, Sid.

insanabilis.full: in-sānābĭlis, e, adj., that cannot be cured or healed, incurable (class.). Lit.: morbus, Cic. Tusc. 5, 1, 3: vulnus, Col. 7, 5, 13: venenum, Plin. 7, 15, 13, § 64.— Trop., irretrievable, without remedy, hopeless: contumeliae, Cic. Or. 26, 89: ingenium, Liv. 1, 28, 9: nihil insanabilius, id. 28, 25, 7: insanabili leto perire, Plin. 24, 17, 100, § 157: dolor, Quint. 6 prooem. § 6: caput insanabile tribus Anticyris, Hor. A. P. 300: scribendi cacoethes, Juv. 7, 51.—Adv.: insānābĭlĭter, incurably, Ca
insanabilis.short: in-sānābĭlis, e, adj., that cannot be cured or healed, incurable (class.).

insanctus.full: in-sanctus, a, um, adj., unholy: insanctus, ο μὴ ἅγιος, Gloss. Gr. Lat.
insanctus.short: in-sanctus, a, um, adj., unholy: insanctus, ο μὴ ἅγιος, Gloss.

insania.full: insānĭa, ae, f. insanus, unsoundness of mind. As a disease, madness, insanity, Cels. 3, 18, 2 sqq.— As a personal quality, madness, frenzy, folly, senselessness: nomen insaniae significat mentis aegrotationem et morbum, Cic. Tusc. 3, 4, 8: sanitatem animorum positam in tranquillitate quadam constantiaque censebant: his rebus mentem vacuam appellarunt insaniam, id. ib. 3, 4, 9: furorem esse rati sunt, mentis ad omnia caecitatem: quod cum majus esse videatur, quam insania, tamen ejusmodi est, ut f

insanibilis.full: insānībĭlis, e, adj. insanio, insane, raging: furor, Lact. 4, 19 dub.

insanio.full: insānĭo, īvi and ĭi, ītum (imperf.: insanibat, Ter. Phorm. 4, 3, 37), 4, v. n. insanus, to be of unsound mind (syn.: furo, deliro, desipio). Lit. As a medic. t. t., to be mad, insane, of men, Cels. 3, 18, 66; 2, 7, 69 al.; of animals, Plin. 27, 11, 76, § 101.— To be senseless, without reason, mad, insane: insanire ex amore, Plaut. Merc. 2, 2, 53: homo insanibat (for insaniebat), Ter. Phorm. 4, 3, 37: usque eo est commotus, ut insanire omnibus ac furere videretur, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 18, § 39: insan
insanio.short: insānĭo, īvi and ĭi, ītum (imperf.: insanibat, Ter.

insanitas.full: insānĭtas, ātis, f. insanus, unsoundness, unhealthiness, disease: nomen insaniae significat mentis aegrotationem et morbum, id est insanitatem et aegrotum animum, Cic. Tusc. 3, 4, 8: sapientia sanitas sit animi, insipientia autem quasi insanitas quaedam, id. ib. 3, 5, 10; cf. Varr. ap. Non. 122, 28.

insanus.full: in-sānus, a, um, adj., unsound in mind. Lit., mad, insane (syn.: furiosus, fanaticus): quod idem contigit insanis, Cic. Ac. 2, 17, 52: si fecisset Juno maritum insanum, Juv. 6, 620. — Transf., that acts like a madman, raging, raving, foolish, frantic. Ex stultis insanos facere, Ter. Eun. 2, 2, 23: acrior et insanior cupiditas, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 18, § 39: insanissima concio, id. Mil. 17, 45: homo insanissimus, id. Rosc. Am. 12, 33: uter est insanior horum? Hor. S. 2, 3, 102.— Transf., of inanim. a
insanus.short: in-sānus, a, um, adj., unsound in mind.

insani montes.full: Insāni montes, the insane mountains ( = τὰ μαινόμενα ὄρη), i. e. absurdly high, Weissenb. (acc. to others, the raging or stormy mountains), a range in the western part of Sardinia, Liv. 30, 39, 2; cf.: Sardiniam Gracchus arripuit. Nihil illi gentium feritas, Insanorumque, nam sic vocantur, immanitas montium profuere, Flor. 2, 6, 35; Claud. B. Gild. 513.
insani montes.short: Insāni montes, the insane mountains ( = τὰ μαινόμενα ὄρη), i.

insarcio.full: in-sarcĭo, īre, 4, v. a., to stuff in (late Lat.): nummos in calceos sibi, Porphyr. ad Hor. S. 1, 8, 39.

insatiabilis.full: in-sătĭābĭlis, e, adj. That cannot be satisfied, insatiable: cupiditas, Cic. Tusc. 1, 19, 44: gaudium, id. ib. 5, 25, 70: crudelitas, id. Phil. 1, 3, 8: humanus animus, Liv. 4, 13, 4: acquirendi votum, Juv. 14, 125. — With gen.: sanguinis, Just. 1, 8, 13: laudis, Val. Max. 8, 14. 3: spectaculi, Sen. Cons. ad Helv. 9, 1.— That cannot cloy or sate, that never produces satiety: varietas, Cic. N. D. 2, 39, 38: nulla est insatiabilior species, id. ib. 2, 62, 155.— Adv.: insătĭābĭlĭter, insatiably: de

insatiabilitas.full: insătĭābĭlĭtas, ātis, f. insatiabilis, insatiableness, Amm. 31, 4, 11.

insatiatus.full: in-sătĭātus, a, um, adj., unsatisfied, insatiate: ardor eundi, Stat. Th. 6, 305; Prud. Psych. 478.
insatiatus.short: in-sătĭātus, a, um, adj., unsatisfied, insatiate: ardor eundi, Stat.

insatietas.full: in-sătĭĕtas, ātis, f., insatiateness, greedy disposition: quorum animis avidis atque insatietatibus neque lex est, etc., Plaut. Aul. 3, 5, 13.
insatietas.short: in-sătĭĕtas, ātis, f., insatiateness, greedy disposition: quorum animis avidis atque insatietatibus neque lex est, etc., Plaut.

insativus.full: in-sătīvus, false reading for in sativis, Plin. 19, 12, 60, § 183.
insativus.short: in-sătīvus, false reading for in sativis, Plin.

insaturabilis.full: in-sătŭrābĭlis, e, adj., insatiable: abdomen, Cic. Sest. 51, 110; with gen.: sanguinis humani, Oros. 3, 18 fin.—Adv.: in-sătŭrābĭlĭter, insatiably: annis praeteritis expleri, Cic. N. D. 2, 25, 64.
insaturabilis.short: in-sătŭrābĭlis, e, adj., insatiable: abdomen, Cic.

insaturatus.full: in-sătŭrātus, a, um, adj., unsatisfied, insatiate: noverca insaturata odiis, Avien. Phaen. Arat. 183.
insaturatus.short: in-sătŭrātus, a, um, adj., unsatisfied, insatiate: noverca insaturata odiis, Avien.

insaturus.full: in-sătŭrus, a, um, adj., insatiable, Coripp. Joann. 3, 368.
insaturus.short: in-sătŭrus, a, um, adj., insatiable, Coripp.

insauciatus.full: in-saucĭātus, a, um, adj., not wounded, Ambros. Dign. Sacerd. 5.
insauciatus.short: in-saucĭātus, a, um, adj., not wounded, Ambros.

inscendo.full: inscendo, scendi, scensum, 3, v. n. and a. [in-scando], to step into or upon, to climb up, mount, ascend. Lit.: cum inscenderet in rogum ardentem, Cic. Div. 1, 23, 47: supra pilam inscendat, Cato, R. R. 127, 2: quadrigas Jovis, Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 294: in arborem, id. Aul. 4, 6, 12: in currum, id. Men. 5, 2, 10: equum, Suet. Ner. 48: haud se inscendi ab alio (Bucephalus) nisi a rege passus est, Gell. 5, 2, 3: grabatulo inscenso, App. M. 2, p. 122, 16.—Absol.: ubi amicam avectam scio, Inscendo, I go

inscensio.full: inscensĭo, ōnis, f. inscendo, a mounting, ascending: in navem inscensio, an embarking, Plaut. Rud. 2, 6, 19.

inscensus1.full: inscensus, a, um, Part., v. inscendo.

inscensus2.full: inscensus, ūs, m. inscendo, a mounting, i. e. covering: equarum, App. M. 7, p. 194, 17.

insciens.full: in-scĭens, entis, adj., unknowing. Without knowledge, unaware: si peccavi, insciens feci, Ter. Heaut. 4, 1, 19: nihil me insciente esse factum, without my knowing it, Cic. Fam. 5, 2, 3: saepe jam Plus insciens quis fecit quam prudens boni, Plaut. Capt. prol. 45; cf. sq.: me apsente atque insciente, id. Trin. 1, 2, 130: utrum inscientem vultis contra foedera fecisse, an scientem? Cic. Balb. 5, 13.— With de and abl.: de eorum verbis, Plaut. Trin. 1, 2, 178 al.— Ignorant, stupid, silly: abi, sis, i

inscientia.full: in-scĭentĭa, ae, f. Want of knowledge, ignorance, inexperience (cf. inscitia init.): in tantis tenebris erroris et inscientiae, Cic. Sull. 14, 40: mea, id. de Or. 1, 46, 203: alicujus, id. ib. 3, 35, 142; id. Ac. 2, 47, 146.—With gen. Subj.: vulgi, Caes. B. G. 7, 43, 3: hostium, id. ib. 3, 19, 3: temeritas et inscientia ducum, Liv. 22, 25, 12.— Obj.: locorum, Caes. B. G. 3, 9, 3: belli, Nep. Epam. 7: dicendi, Cic. de Or. 1, 54, 233.— Ignorance, philosophically speaking; opp. fundamental knowledg

inscitia.full: inscītĭa, ae, f. inscitus, ignorance, inexperience, unskilfulness, awkwardness, stupidity, stolidity in any thing (usu. with suggestion of blame; while inscientia is simply the absence of knowledge; but the distinction is neglected by Tacitus; v. infra).—With gen., rarely with erga (class.): rerum, Cic. de Or. 1, 22, 49: temporis, id. Off. 1, 40, 144: belli, Nep. Epam. 7, 4: rei publicae ut alienae, Tac. H. 1, 1: rerum verborumque, Quint. 5, 13, 38: veri, Hor. S. 2, 3, 43: artis, Suet. Ner. 41:

inscitulus.full: inscītŭlus, a, um, adj. dim. [inscitus], ignorant, awkward, unmannerly: ancillula, Afran. ap. Non. 12, 21 (Com. Fragm. v. 386 Rib.).

inscitus.full: in-scītus, a, um, adj. Ignorant, inexperienced, unskilful, silly, simple, stupid; freq. coupled with stultus (rare in Cic.; a favorite word of Plaut.), Plaut. Most. 1, 3, 51: inscita atque stulta mulier, id. ib. 2, 3, 85; id. Mil. 3, 1, 141.—Of inanim. and abstr. things: mirum atque inscitum somniavi somnium, Plaut. Rud. 3, 1, 5.—Comp.: quid est inscitius, Cic. N. D. 2, 13. 36; id. Div. 2, 62.—Sup.: inscitissimus, Plaut. Most. 5, 2, 14.— * Pass., unknown: nescio quid aliud indictum inscitumque d

inscius.full: in-scĭus, a, um, adj., not knowing, ignorant of a thing (not used by Plaut. or Ter.; v. Ritschl, Proleg. p. 64 sq.; and cf. insciens); constr., absol., with gen., rarely with de, an acc., an inf., or a rel. clause (class.). Absol.: distinguere artificem ab inscio, Cic. Ac. 2, 7, 22: is, quem vos ad mortem inscii misistis, ignorantly, id. Planc. 16, 40: inscios inopinantesque Menapios oppresserunt, Caes. B. G. 4, 4: omnibus insciis, neque suspicantibus, Hirt. B. Afr. 37.— With gen.: omnium rerum,
inscius.short: in-scĭus, a, um, adj., not knowing, ignorant of a thing (not used by Plaut.

inscribo.full: in-scrībo, psi, ptum, 3, v. a., to write in or upon any thing, to inscribe (class.). Lit.: aliquid in basi tropaeorum, Cic. Pis. 38, 92: in statua inscripsit, Parenti optime merito, id. Fam. 12, 3, 1: nomen suum monumentis, id. Har. Resp. 27: ea inscribam brevi, quae, etc., id. Att. 4, 1, 4: sit inscriptum in fronte unius cujusque civis, quid de re publica sentiat, id. Cat. 1, 13, 32: orationes in animo, id. de Or. 2, 87, 355: ut, si quae essent incisae aut inscriptae litterae, tollerentur, id.

inscriptilis.full: in-scriptĭlis, e, adj., that cannot be written, Diom. p. 413 P.
inscriptilis.short: in-scriptĭlis, e, adj., that cannot be written, Diom.

inscriptio.full: inscriptĭo, ōnis, f. inscribo, a writing upon, inscribing; an inscription, title (class.): nominis inscriptio, Cic. Dom. 20, 51: quod de inscriptione quaeris, non dubito, quin καθῆκον officium sit; sed inscriptio plenior, de officiis, id. Att. 16, 11, 4.—An inscription on monuments: hinc illa infelicis monumenti inscriptio, turba se medicorum periisse, Plin. 29, 1, 5, § 11: frontis, a branding on the forehead, Petr. 106; 103; so plur., Sen. de Ira, 3, 3, 6: servi, quibus stigmata inscripta sint,

inscriptum.full: inscriptum, v. inscribo, I. B. fin.

inscriptura.full: inscriptūra, ae, f. inscribo, an inscription (al. in scriptura), Tert. adv. Val. 30.

inscriptus1.full: inscriptus, a, um, Part., from inscribo.
inscriptus1.short: inscriptus, a, um, Part., from inscribo.

inscriptus2.full: in-scriptus, a, um, adj. Unwritten: unde et illa divisio est, alia esse scripta, alia inscripta, Quint. 3, 6, 36; 7, 4, 36.— Not marked or entered at the custom-house, contraband: inscriptum pecus, Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 16.— Concerning which nothing is written (in the statutes): maleficium, Sen. praef. 3 Excerpt. Controv.

inscrutabilis.full: in-scrūtābĭlis, e, adj. 2. in-scrutor, inscrutable (eccl. Lat.): Dei judicia, Aug. Ep. 106, 4; Hilar. Trin. 8, 38.

inscrutor.full: in-scrūtor, āri, v. dep., to search or examine into: si Homeri latentem prudentiam inscruteris altius (al. scruteris), Macr. S. 7, 1.

insculpo.full: in-sculpo (inscalp-), psi, ptum, 3, v. a., to cut or carve in or upon, to engrave. Lit. With dat. (poet. and in postAug. prose): summam patrimonii saxo (shortly before, incidere), Hor. S. 2, 3, 90: litteras tabellae, Quint. 1, 1, 27: elogium tumulo, Suet. Claud. 1: incisa et insculpta sunt publicis aeternisque monumentis praetoria ornamenta Pallantis, Plin. Ep. 8, 6, 14: usus luxuriantis aetatis signaturas pretiosis gemmis coepit insculpere, Macr. S. 7, 13, 11.— With abl. (very rare): columna ae

insculptio.full: insculptĭo, ōnis, f. insculpo, a cutting, carving (late Lat.), Jul. Val. 2, 28.

insculptus.full: insculptus, a, um, Part., from insculpo.
insculptus.short: insculptus, a, um, Part., from insculpo.

insecabilis.full: in-sĕcābĭlis, e, adj., that cannot be cut up or divided, inseparable, indivisible (post-Aug.), Sen. Ep. 118: corpora, i. e. atoms, Quint. 2, 17, 38; 3, 3, 13.
insecabilis.short: in-sĕcābĭlis, e, adj., that cannot be cut up or divided, inseparable, indivisible (post-Aug.), Sen.

inseco1.full: in-sĕco, cŭi, ctum, 1, v. a., to cut into, cut up (class.): aliquid dentibus, Auct. Her. 4, 49, 62: olivam acuta harundine, Col. 12, 47: corpora mortuorum ad scrutandos morbos, to dissect, Plin. 19, 5, 26, § 86: insecandi sunt favi, Col. 9, 15, 9: quod (subtemen) insecti pectine dentes, cut in, notched, Ov. M. 6, 58.—Hence, insectum, i, n. (sc. animale), an insect; plur., Plin. 11, 1, 1, § 1; 11, 28, 33, § 96 al.

inseco2.full: insĕco or insĕquo, insexi, old form for insĕquor, to pursue the narration, to proceed, relate, declare; so imper.: insece, Musa, Enn. ap. Gell. 18, 9, 3 (Ann. v. 332 Vahl.): virum mihi, Camena, insece versutum, Liv. Andr. ap. Gell. 18, 9, 5; perf. subj.: insexit, dixerit, Enn. ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 111 Müll.; gerund.: insecenda, Cato ap. Gell. 1. 1.
inseco2.short: insĕco or insĕquo, insexi, old form for insĕquor, to pursue the narration, to proceed, relate, declare;

insectanter.full: insectanter, adv. insector, harshly, bitterly (with graviter): vituperari, Gell. 19, 3, 1.

insectatio.full: in-sectātĭo, ōnis, f. id., a pursuing, pursuit (class., but not in Cic. or Cæs.). Lit.: hostis, Liv. 21, 47, 2.— Trop., a pursuing with words, a censuring, railing at, deriding, insulting: tanta est hominum insolentia et nostri insectatio, Brut. ap. Ep. Cic. Fam. 11, 1, 2: principum, Liv. 22, 34, 2: studiorum et morum alicujus, Suet. Gramm. 19: insectationibus petere aliquem, Tac. A. 2, 55: fortunae, Quint. 6, 3, 28; 11, 1, 86: quod insectationis genus, id. 5, 7, 6.

insectator.full: in-sectātor, ōris, m. id., a persecutor (very rare; not in Cic. or Cæs.). Lit.: plebis, Liv. 3, 33, 7.— Trop., a censurer: vitiorum, Quint. 10, 1, 129.

insectio.full: insectĭo, ōnis, f. 2. inseco, a narration, i. q. narratio, acc. to a remark of Gell. 18, 9, 4; 11.

insecto.full: insecto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a., a rare form for insector, to pursue (ante- and postclass.): nos insectabit lapidibus, Plaut. Capt. 3, 4, 61.— Hence, pass.: insectatus, pursued, Auct. B. Afr. 71, 4.

insector.full: insector, ātus, 1, v. dep. a. freq. [insequor], to pursue (class.). Lit.: impios agitant insectanturque furiae, Cic. Leg. 1, 14, 40; cf. id. Div. 2, 70, 144: aliquem hastis, Plaut. Capt. 3, 4, 17: aliquem verberibus, to pursue with blows, Tac. A. 1, 20.— Transf.: assiduis herbam insectabere rastris, pursue the weeds with diligent hoes, i. e. diligently extirpate them, Verg. G. 1, 155.— Trop., to pursue with words, to censure, blame, rail at, inveigh against, speak ill of (with exagitare): indice

insectum.full: insectum, i, n., v. 1. inseco fin.

insectura.full: in-sectūra, ae, f. [1. inseco), an incision, Sen. Q. N. 1, 7.

insectus1.full: insectus, a, um, Part., from 1. inseco.

insectus2.full: in-sectus, a, um, adj. 2. in-seco, for non sectus, Paul. ex Fest. p. 111 Müll.

insecundus.full: in-sĕcundus, a, um, adj., not following, unyielding, uncomplying: secundus, insecundus, Not. Tir. 95.
insecundus.short: in-sĕcundus, a, um, adj., not following, unyielding, uncomplying: secundus, insecundus, Not.

insecutio.full: insĕcūtĭo, ōnis, f. insequor, a pursuing: incerta, App. M. 8, p. 208, 23.

insecutor.full: insĕcūtor, ōris, m. id., a pursuer, persecutor (post-class.), Tert. Mag. 5: frustratis insecutoribus, App. M. 7 init.

insedabilis.full: in-sēdābĭlis, e, adj. 2. in-sedo, that cannot be stayed or stilled, incessant: insedabilis, ἀκατάπαυστος, Gloss. Philox.— * Adv.: insēdābĭlĭter, unquenchably, incessantly: sitis arida, Lucr. 6, 1175.

inseducibilis.full: insēdūcĭbĭlis, e, adj. 2. in-seduco, not to be drawn away (eccl. Lat.), Anon. (Hilar.) in Job, 2, p. 188.

insedulus.full: in-sēdŭlus, a, um, adj., not zealous: insedulus, ασπούδαστος, Gloss. Philox.
insedulus.short: in-sēdŭlus, a, um, adj., not zealous: insedulus, ασπούδαστος, Gloss.

insegnis.full: in-segnis, e, adj., inactive, indolent: insegnis, ἀδρανής, Gloss. Philox.
insegnis.short: in-segnis, e, adj., inactive, indolent: insegnis, ἀδρανής, Gloss.

insemel.full: in-sĕmĕl, adv., at once, Flor. prooem. § 3; id. 2, 20, 1; Dig. 18, 1, 35, § 7.

insemino.full: in-sēmĭno, 1, v. a., to sow or plant in, to implant (post-Aug.): tabem et morbos visceribus, Gell. 19, 5, 3: terra ex caelestium imbrium conceptionibus inseminata, impregnated, fertilized, Vitr. 8 praef. init.: ex conventu Jovis inseminati et nati sunt, Arn. 2, 93; Macr. S. 1, 17, 35; 68.

insemitatio.full: insēmĭtātĭo, ōnis, f. (2. in-semita], pathlessness, impassableness: insemitatio, ἀνοδία, Gloss. Philox.

insenescibilis.full: insĕnescĭbĭlis, e, adj. 2. in-senesco, not growing old, undecaying: insenescibilis, ἀγήραος, ἀγήρατος, Gloss. Philox.

insenesco.full: in-sĕnesco, nui, 3, v. inch. n., to grow old in or at a thing; constr. with dat. (poet. and post-Aug. prose): insenuit Libris et curis, Hor. Ep. 2, 2, 82: malis, Ov. P. 1, 4, 48: singulis actionum partibus, Quint. 10, 3, 11: iisdem negotiis, Tac. A. 4, 6.

insensatus.full: in-sensātus, a, um, adj., irrational (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 43 al.—Adv.: insensātē, foolishly, Vulg. Sap. Sir. 12, 23.

insensibilis.full: in-sensĭbĭlis, e, adj., that cannot be felt, insensible, imperceptible (post-class.). Pass.: morbus, Ser. Samm. 3, 2. — As subst.: insensĭbĭlĭa, ium, n., things of no account, Lact. 2, 2, 17; 2, 5, 1.— Things imperceptible, Apul. Asclep. 19, p. 87. — Trop., incomprehensible: inenarrabile esse ait, et propemodum insensibile, Gell. 17, 10, 17.— Act., that cannot feel, insensible, senseless: simulacra, Lact. 6, 13 fin.: deus, id. 7, 3, 7; 4, 1, 2 al.—Adv.: insensĭbĭlĭter, insensibly, Cassiod.
insensibilis.short: in-sensĭbĭlis, e, adj., that cannot be felt, insensible, imperceptible (post-class.).

insensibilitas.full: insensĭbĭlĭtas, ātis, f. insensibilis, insensibility, Claud. Mam. Stat. An. 1, 3; Ambros. de Bono Mort. 7, 26.

insensilis.full: in-sensĭlis, e, adj., insensible, imperceptible, = insensibilis: principia, Lucr. 2, 866; 888.
insensilis.short: in-sensĭlis, e, adj., insensible, imperceptible, = insensibilis: principia, Lucr.

insensualis.full: in-sensŭālis, e, adj., insensible: res, Cassiod. Var. 2, 40.
insensualis.short: in-sensŭālis, e, adj., insensible: res, Cassiod.

insensualitas.full: insensŭālĭtas, ātis, f. insensualis, insensibility (eccl. Lat.), Aug. contr. Faust. 15, 4.

inseparabilis.full: in-sēpărābĭlis, e, adj., that cannot be separated, inseparable (post-Aug.): quaedam inter se, Sen. Ep. 118, 85: societas, Gell. 1, 9, 12.—Comp.: trinitas inseparabilior, Aug. Trin. 15, 23.—Adv.: insēpărā-bĭlĭter, inseparably (post-class.), Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 22: conexa, Lact. 3, 11.
inseparabilis.short: in-sēpărābĭlis, e, adj., that cannot be separated, inseparable (post-Aug.): quaedam inter se, Sen.

inseparabilitas.full: insēpărābĭlĭtas, ātis, f. inseparabilis, inseparableness, inseparability (eccl. Lat.), Aug. Trin. 15, 23: virtutum, id. Ep. 29, 2.

inseparatus.full: in-sēpărātus, a, um, adj., not separate (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Prax. 9.
inseparatus.short: in-sēpărātus, a, um, adj., not separate (eccl.

insepultus.full: in-sĕpultus, a, um, adj. 2. in-sepultus, unburied (class.): acervi civium, Cic. Cat. 4, 6, 11: membra, Hor. Epod. 5, 99: insepultos projecit, Liv. 29, 9, 10. — Transf., without burial: mors, Sen. Tranq. 14: sepultura, a burial without the customary funeral rites, and therefore undeserving the name of a burial (imitation of the Gr. τάφος ἄταφος), Cic. Phil. 1, 2, 5 (but sepulta is the true reading, id. ib. 14, 12, 33 B. and K.).

insequens.full: insĕquens, entis, Part. and P. a., from insequor.

insequenter1.full: insĕquenter, adv., v. insequor, P. a. fin.

insequenter2.full: in-sĕquenter, adv. 2. in-sequor, not in the proper order of succession, without connection, unconnectedly: particula posita, Gell. 10, 29, 4.

insequor.full: in-sĕquor, cūtus (quūtus), 3, v. dep. n. and a., to follow, to follow after or upon a person or thing (class.). Lit. In gen.: proximus huic, longo sed proximus intervallo Insequitur Salius, Verg. A. 5, 321: fugientem lumine pinum, with her eyes follows the flying ship, Ov. M. 11, 468.— In partic., to pursue, follow up, press upon: gens eadem quae te bello Insequitur, Verg. A. 8, 146: hostem, Curt. 4, 9, 13; 7, 9, 13; Suet. Claud. 1: ad hostem insequendum, Liv. 26, 6, 7: reliquias Troiae cineres

inserabiliter.full: in-sĕrābĭlĭter, adv. 2. in-sera, so as not to be unlocked: obstruere, Auct. Itin. Alex. M. 100 Mai.

inserenus.full: in-sĕrēnus, a, um, adj., not clear or serene, overcast: Hyas, Stat. S. 1, 6, 21.
inserenus.short: in-sĕrēnus, a, um, adj., not clear or serene, overcast: Hyas, Stat.

insero1.full: in-sĕro, sēvi, sĭtum, 3, v. a. in-, 1. sero, to sow or plant in; to ingraft (class.). Lit.: frumentum, Col. 5, 7, 3: pirum bonam in pirum silvaticam, to ingraft, graft, Varr. R. R. 1, 40, 5: vitem, Col. Arb. 8, 2: fissā modo cortice virgam Inserit, Ov. M. 14, 631; Hor. Epod. 2, 12: inseritur et nucis arbutus horrida fetu, Verg. G. 2, 69 Forbig. ad loc.; so, cum Vergilius insitam nucibus arbutum dicat, Plin. 15, 15, 17, § 57. — Trop., to implant: num qua tibi vitiorum inseverit olim Natura, Hor.

insero2.full: in-sĕro, sĕrŭi, sertum, 3, v. a. in-, 2. sero, to put, bring, or introduce into, to insert (class.); constr. with in and acc., or with dat. Lit. In gen.: collum in laqueum, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 17, § 37; id. de Or. 2, 39, 162: oculos in pectora, Ov. M. 2, 94: caput in tentoria, Liv. 8, 36, 6: gemmas aureis soleis, Curt. 9, 1, 29: falces longuriis, Caes. B. G. 3, 14: subtegmen radiis, Ov. M. 6, 56: in avium nidis aliquid, Plin. 24, 19, 113, § 174.— In partic., to ingraft: quidquid inserueris, vimine

inserpo.full: in-serpo, psi, ptum, 3, v. n., to crcep on or over any thing; only trop.; constr. with dat. (poet. and post-class.): jam somnus avaris Inserpit curis, Stat. Th. 1, 340: ei lanugo malis inserpebat, covered over his cheeks, App. M. 7, p. 189 fin.

inserta.full: inserta, ae, f. 2. insero, an ornament (very rare): frugalitas inserta est rumoris boni, Macr. S. 2, 7.

insertatio.full: insertātĭo, ōnis, f. inserto, an inserting, Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 1, 43.

inserticius.full: insertīcĭus, a, um, adj. 2. insero, that can be inserted: inserticius, ἐγκεντρήσιμος, ἐντάξιμος, Gloss. Philox.

insertim.full: insertim, false read. for inserti, Lucr. 2, 115.

insertio.full: insertĭo, ōnis, f. 2. insero, a putting in, ingrafting, grafting (post-class.), Isid. Orig. 17, 6, 2: oleastri, Aug. Ep. 120, 20: surculorum, Macr. S. 1, 7, 25.

insertivus.full: insertīvus, a, um, adj. id., inserted, ingrafted; only trop. (very rare): stirps, i. e. an illegitimate posterity, Calp. Decl. 24: liberi, Phaedr. 3, 3, 10.

inserto.full: inserto, 1, v. a. freq. [id.], to put into, insert; with dat. (poet. and post - Aug.): clipeoque sinistram Insertabam aptans, Verg. A. 2, 672: dextras catenis, Stat. Th. 12, 460: insertans commissuris secures, Petr. 97.

insertus.full: insertus, a, um, Part., from 2. insero.

inservio.full: in-servĭo, īvi or ĭi, ītum, 4 (archaic forms, inservibas, Plaut. Most. 1, 3, 59: inservibat, Sil. 7, 341), v. n. and (rarely) a., to be serviceable, to be devoted or attached to, to be submissive to, to serve (syn.: deservio, ministro); with dat., rarely with acc. (class.). With dat.: filium meum amico suo video inservire, Ter. Heaut. 3, 1, 9: a quo plurimum sperant, ei potissimum inserviunt, Cic. Off. 1, 15, 49: plebi, cui ad eam diem summa ope inservitum erat, who had been treated with the utm
inservio.short: in-servĭo, īvi or ĭi, ītum, 4 (archaic forms, inservibas, Plaut.

inservo.full: in-servo, 1, v. a. To attend to, observe (a favorite word of Statius): gemit, inservante noverca, Liber, Stat. Th. 10, 886: volucres, id. ib. 8, 194: fata, id. ib. 6, 935.— To keep: sagittae volitantes vires integras inservabant, Amm. 31, 15, 11.

insessio.full: insessĭo, ōnis, f. insideo, a sitting down (late Lat.): hostium insessio, id est hostilis circundatio, Cassiod. in Psa. 21, 12.

insessor.full: insessor, ōris, m. id., a besetter, occupant (very rare); of a ship, Jul. Val. Res Gest. Alex. 1, 1: viarum, a waylayer, Symm. Ep. 2, 48; cf.: insessores, latrones, Paul. ex Fest. p. 111 Müll.: quod circa vias insidientur sedentes.

insessus1.full: insessus, a, um, Part., from insideo.
insessus1.short: insessus, a, um, Part., from insideo.

insessus2.full: in-sessus, a, um, adj. 2. in-sedeo, unsettled, without a permanent dwelling: gentes, Sic. Fl. de Cond. Agr. p. 3.

insibilator.full: insībĭlātor, m. insibilo, one that breathes in by hissing (late Lat.): venenorum insibilator serpens, Aug. in Joh. 8, 6.

insibilo.full: in-sībĭlo, 1, v. n. and a., to hiss, whistle, or rustle in (poet.): Eurus, Ov. M. 15, 603: ignis membris, Sil. 12, 616: Erinys atros insibilat ore tumores, hisses in, breathes in, with a hissing noise, id. 2, 626.

insiccabilis.full: in-siccābĭlis, e, adj., that cannot be dried, Sid. Ep. 9, 16.
insiccabilis.short: in-siccābĭlis, e, adj., that cannot be dried, Sid.

insiccatus.full: in-siccātus, a, um, adj., undried, not dried up (only in Statius): vulnera cruore, Stat. Th. 3, 364: cruor, id. ib. 8, 246.
insiccatus.short: in-siccātus, a, um, adj., undried, not dried up (only in Statius): vulnera cruore, Stat.

insicia.full: insĭcĭa, ae, f., and insĭcĭum (īsĭc-), ĭi, n. inseco, stuffing, force-meat, a dish of minced meat (very rare). Form insicia, Varr. L. L. 5, § 110 Müll.— Form insicium, Macr. S. 7, 8; Arn. 2, 92.
insicia.short: insĭcĭa, ae, f., and insĭcĭum (īsĭc-), ĭi, n.

insiciarius.full: insĭcĭārĭus, ĭi, m. insicia, a forcemeat-maker, Hier. in Ruf. 1, 4.

insiciatus.full: insĭcĭātus or isĭcĭātus, a, um, adj. id., stuffed with force-meat: pullus, Apic. 8, 7.
insiciatus.short: insĭcĭātus or isĭcĭātus, a, um, adj.

insiciolum.full: insĭcĭŏlum or isĭcĭŏlum, i, n. dim. insicium, a little force-meat (post-class.): porcina, Apic. 2, 2; 5, 3.

insideo.full: insĭdĕo, sēdi, sessum, 2, v. n. and a. [in-sedeo], to sit in or upon any thing; mostly with dat. (class.). Neutr. Lit.: equo, Liv. 7, 6, 5: curru insidens, Sen. Med. 29: solo, Suet. Aug. 82.— To settle: ubi Lydia quondam jugis insedit Etruscis, Verg. A. 8, 479.— Trop., to be seated, fixed, or stamped in, to adhere to: cum in locis semen insedit, Cic. N. D. 2, 51, 128: longus morbus, cum penitus insedit, when it has become deeply seated, Cels. 3, 1: insidens capulo manus, i. e. keeping firm hold

insidiae.full: insĭdĭae, ārum, f. plur. (in sing. insidia prima, Sall. Fragm. ap. Charis. p. 75 P.) [insideo], an ambush, ambuscade (class.). Lit Of persons: qui sustinuerant primos impetus insidiarum, Hirt. B. G. 8, 19: equites procedere longius jussi, donec insidiae coorirentur, Tac. H. 2, 24.— Of place: si forte in insidias devenero, Plaut. As. 1, 1, 92: signa aenea in insidiis ponere, Cic. Deiot. 7, 21: milites in insidiis collocare, Caes. B. G. 3, 20: intrare insidias, id. B. C. 3, 38.—Particular phrases.

insidianter.full: insĭdĭanter, adv. insidior, craftily, artfully, insidiously: insidianter speculati (al. insidiantes), Just. 6, 6.

insidiator.full: insĭdĭātor, ōris, m. id., a soldier lying in ambush, Hirt. B. G. 8, 18.— Transf., one who lies in wait, a lurker, waylayer (rare but class.): viae, Cic. Cat. 2, 12, 27: in foro collocatur, id. Mil. 7, 19: imperii, Nep. Reg. 2.

insidiatrix.full: insĭdĭātrix, īcis, f. adj. insidiator, that lies in wait: manus, Amm. 24, 4.

insidio.full: insĭdĭo, āvi, 1, v. the foll. art.

insidior.full: insĭdĭor, ātus, 1, v. dep. (act. form insidiaverint for insidiati erunt, Dig. 48, 19, 28, § 11) [insidiae], to lie in ambush, lie in wait for; constr. with dat. Lit.: quam diu mihi, Catilina, insidiatus es, Cic. Cat. 1, 5, 11: apris, Mart. 12, 14, 10: in legatis insidiandis, Cic. Cael. 21, 51.— Trop.: somno maritorum, Cic. Cat. 1, 10, 26: tempori, to watch for, seize upon the favorable moment, Liv. 23, 35, 15: temporibus, to watch the changes of the times, to turn them to one's own advantage, Ve

insidiosus.full: insĭdĭōsus, a, um, adj. insidiae, cunning, artful, deceitful, dangerous, insidious (class.). Of persons: quis insidiosior unquam fuit? Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 78, § 192. — Of inanim. and abstr. things: Capraria insidiosa naufragiis, Plin. 3, 5, 11, § 78: pocula Circes, Ov. M. 14, 294: verba, id. H. 20, 212: clementia, Cic. Att. 8, 16, 2. — Sup., Plin. 29, 1, 8, § 28. — Adv.: insĭdĭōsē, cunningly, deceitfully, insidiously: in gratiam rediit cum illo, Cic. Rab. Post. 12, 33: me insidiosissime tractavit,

insido.full: in-sīdo, sēdi (perf. insidi, Amm. 28, 6, 4), sessum, 3, v. n. and a., to sit down in or on, to settle on; constr. with dat. (poet. and post-Aug.). Lit. In gen.: apes floribus insidunt, Verg. A. 6, 708: inscia Dido, Insidat quantus miserae deus, id. ib. 1, 719; volucres metuunt insidere ramis, Luc. 3, 407. — With acc.: locum, Stat. Th. 2, 151: apex insiditur astris, id. ib. 2, 36: littera "i" sibi insidit, coniicit enim est ab illo jacit, coalesces, Quint. 1, 4, 11: digitos membris, sink into, Ov

insigne.full: insigne, is, n. insignis, a mark, sign, signal; a distinctive mark, a badge of office (class.). Lit.: quod erat insigne, eum facere, etc., Cic. de Or. 3, 33, 133: Minerva singulare est insigne ejus gymnasii, id. Att. 1, 4, 3: bos in Aegypto etiam numinis vice colitur: Apim vocant. Insigne ei in dextro latere candicans macula, Plin. 8, 46, 71, § 184.—Plur.: sibi haberent honores ... sibi triumphos, sibi alia praeclarae laudis insignia, Cic. Pis. 9, 26.— A sign or badge of office or honor, a decor

insigniarius.full: insignĭārĭus, ĭi, m. insigne, a keeper of insignia: insigniarius, ὁπλοπάροχος, Gloss. Philox.

insignificativus.full: in-signĭfĭcātīvus, i, m. (sc. modus) [2. in-significo], the insignificative, a name given by some grammarians to the infinitive, Diom. p. 331 P.

insignio.full: insignĭo, īvi or ĭi, ītum, 4 (imperf. insignibat, Verg. A. 7, 790; Stat. Th. 7, 56), v. a. insignis, to put a mark upon, to mark; to distinguish (mostly post-Aug.): pueri insigniti, marked with some bodily defect, Plaut. Fragm. ap. Fest. p. 375, 19 (id. Mil. 3, 1, 127 Weise): clipeum auro, Verg. A. 7, 790: mulli insigniuntur barba gemina inferiori labro, Plin. 9, 17, 30, § 64: oratorem fucatis et meretriciis vestibus, Tac. Or. 26: nec insigniri, nec misceri omnibus, to distinguish one's self, Se

insignis.full: insignis, e, adj. in-signum, distinguished by a mark; remarkable, noted, eminent, distinguished, prominent, extraordinary (class.): insignes appellantur boves, qui in femine et in pede album habent, quasi insigniti, Paul. ex Fest. p. 114 Müll.: maculis insignis et albo, i. e. maculis albis, Verg. G. 3, 56: insigni eum veste adornavit, Liv. 1, 20, 2: officinae, Plin. 35, 12, 46, § 161: virtus, Cic. Lael. 27, 102: vis, id. N. D. 2, 31, 80; id. de Or. 2, 22, 90: ad deformitatem puer, id. Leg. 3, 8,

insignite.full: insignītē, adv., v. insignio, P. a. fin.

insignitor.full: insignītor, ōris, m. insignio, an engraver (late Lat.), Aug. Civ. Dei, 21, 4.

insignitus.full: insignītus, Part. and P. a., from insignio.

insigno.full: in-signo, 1, v. a., to engrave: insigno, ἐγχαράσσω, Gloss. Philox.

insilia.full: insĭlĭa, ĭum, n. plur. [insilio], the treadle of a weaver's loom, Lucr. 5, 1353.

insilio.full: insĭlĭo, ŭi (insilivi, Liv. 8, 9, 9: insilii, Claud. ap. Ruf. 1, 349; imperf. insilibat, Gell. 9, 11, 7), 4, v. n. in-salio, to leap into or upon, to spring at; constr. with in and acc., with the simple acc., with dat., or absol. (class., but not in Cic.). Lit. With in and acc.: e navi in scapham, Plaut. Rud. 2, 3, 36: in equum, Liv. 6, 7, 3: milites qui in phalangas insilirent, Caes. B. G. 1, 52, 5.— With the simple acc.: equum, Sall. H. Fragm. 5, 3 Dietsch: puppim, Luc. 3, 626: undas, Ov. M. 8

insimul.full: in-sĭmul, adv., at the same time (postAug.; first in Statius), Stat. S. 1, 6, 36 (in Flor. 2, 20, 1, read insemel).
insimul.short: in-sĭmul, adv., at the same time (postAug.;

insimulatio.full: insĭmŭlātĭo (insĭmĭl-), ōnis, f. insimulo, a charge against one, an accusation (class.): in falsam atque iniquam probrorum insimulationem vocabatur, Cic. Font. 13, 29: criminis, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 9, § 23: falsae, App. M. 10, p. 253, 19.

insimulator.full: insĭmŭlātor (insĭmĭl-), ōris, m. id., an accuser (post-class.), App. Mag. p. 293, 37; Pacat. Pan. Theod. 43.

insimulatus.full: insĭmŭlātus, a, um, adj. 2. in-simulo, undisguised, unfeigned (eccl. Lat.), Vulg. Sap. 18, 16.

insimulo.full: in-sĭmŭlo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a., to make a plausible charge (true or false) against a person before a tribunal; to make suspected, charge, accuse, blame, esp. falsely; to invent a charge or bear false witness against (syn.: accuso, incuso, arguo). With acc. of person: si non facit tu male facis, quae insontem insimules, Plaut. Men. 5, 2, 55: hic tu me etiam insimulas, Cic. Fam. 7, 13, 1: non possum quemquam insimulare falso, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 41, § 107: hic tu me etiam insimulas, id. Fam. 7, 13, 1

insincerus.full: in-sincērus, a, um, adj., not genuine, not pure, adulterated, spoiled; not honest or candid, insincere (poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit.: cruor, Verg. G. 4, 285: acies, imperfect, Prud. Ham. 4.— Trop.: philosophus, Gell. 5, 3, 7: oblatio, Ambros. de Cain et Abel, 2, 6, § 18; id. in Psa. 118, Serm. 11, § 20.
insincerus.short: in-sincērus, a, um, adj., not genuine, not pure, adulterated, spoiled;

insinuatio.full: insĭnŭātĭo, ōnis, f. insinuo, an entrance through a narrow or crooked way. Lit.: Ponti, Avien. Perieg. 397.— Trop. An insinuating or ingratiating one's self into the favor of others: exordium in duas partes dividitur, in principium et insinuationem.... Insinuatio est oratio, quadam dissimulatione et circuitione obscure subiens auditoris animum, Cic. Inv. 1, 15, 20.— A notification, publication, Cod. Just. 8, 54, 32.

insinuator.full: insĭnŭātor, ōris, m. id., an introducer (eccl. Lat.): deorum, Tert. ad Nat. 2, 1.

insinuatrix.full: insĭnŭātrix, īcis, f. insinuator, she that introduces or makes known (eccl. Lat.): rei novae, Aug. Ep. 110, 1.

insinuo.full: in-sĭnŭo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n. Act. Lit., to put, place, or thrust into the bosom (post-class.): sicine vacuus et otiosus insinuatis manibus ambulabis, with folded arms, App. M. 9, p. 219, 23: manum in sinum, Tert. Res. Carn. 28.— To bring in by windings or turnings, to insinuate into; to cause a person or thing to get to a place by windings or turnings; and, in gen., to cause to arrive at or get to a place. In gen.: ratem terris, to land, Avien. Arat. 312: suum aestum per saepta domorum,

insipidus.full: in-sĭpĭdus, a, um, adj. 2. in-sapidus, tasteless, insipid (late Lat.): sapor, Firm. Math. 2, 12; Paul. Nol. Ep. 39, 4.

insipiens.full: in-sĭpĭens (insăp-, Schol. Bob. ad Cic. Sest. 53; p. 304, 16 Bait.), entis, adj. 2. in-sapiens, unwise, senseless, foolish (class.): sed ego insipiens nova nunc facio, Plaut. Cas. 5, 2, 4: insipiens fortunatus, Cic. Lael. 15, 54: sermo insipientium (opp. sapiens), id. Fin. 2, 15, 50. — Comp.: quis homost me insipientior, qui, etc., Plaut. Trin. 4, 2, 84: ego insipientior quam illi ipsi, id. Div. 2, 23, 51.—Sup.: insipientissimus, Sen. Q. N. 2, 59.—Adv.: insĭpĭen-ter, unwisely, foolishly: a me fa

insipientia.full: insĭpĭentĭa, ae, f. insipiens, want of wisdom, senselessness, folly (class.): ita fit, ut sapientia sanitas sit animi, insipientia autem quasi insanitas quaedam, quae est insania eademque dementia, Cic. Tusc. 3, 5, 10; 3, 28, 68; Plaut. Am. prol. 36; id. Mil. 3, 3, 5; id. Poen. 5, 2, 130.

insipo.full: insĭpo, ŭi (pres. pass. insipitur, Varr. L. L. 5, § 105 Müll.), 3, v. a., to throw in (ante-class.), Cato, R. R. 85: ligna, Pompon. ap. Non. 10, n. 3 (Com. Fragm. v. 50, 86 Rib.).

insisto.full: in-sisto, stĭti, 3, v. n., to set foot upon, to stand, tread, or press upon; constr. mostly with dat., also with in and abl. or acc., or the simple acc. (class.). Lit. In gen. With dat.: nec desunt villae quae secutae fluminis amoenitatem margini insistunt, Plin. Ep. 8, 8, 6: ut proximi jacentibus insisterent, stepped upon them, Caes. B. G. 2, 27: alternis pedibus, Quint. 11, 3, 128: volucres metuunt insistere ramis, Luc. 3, 407: vestigiis, Liv. 25, 33 fin.: huic (saxo) institerat frustra, Ov. F

insiticius.full: insĭtīcĭus, a, um, adj. insitio, that is inserted, ingrafted (ante-class. and postAug.); hence, trop.: somnus, that is inserted between the occupations of the day, a noon-day nap, siesta, Varr. R. R. 1, 2, 5: muli, produced from two species of animals, qs. ingrafted, id. ib. 2, 8, 1; App. M. 6, p. 186: (with inductus) sermo, i. e. foreign, Plin. Ep. 4, 3, 5.

insitio.full: insĭtĭo, ōnis, f. 1. insero. An ingrafting, grafting: nec consitiones modo delectant, sed etiam insitiones, Cic. de Sen. 15, 54; Col. 3, 9, 6.— That which is ingrafted: insitionem nutrire, Pall. 5, 2; Col. Arb. 8, 3.— The time of grafting, Ov. R. Am. 195.

insitium.full: insĭtĭum, ĭi, n. id., a putting in, insertion: insitium, ἔνθεσις, Gloss. Philox.

insitivus.full: insĭtīvus, a, um, adj. id., ingrafted, grafted (poet. and post - Aug.). Lit.: pira, Hor. Epod. 2, 19.— Trop., substituted, spurious: liberi, Phaedr. 3, 3, 10: heres, adopted, Sen. Contr. 2, 8: alimentum lactis, of another person than the mother, Gell. 12, 1, 17.—Plur. n. as subst.: insitiva virtutum, Ambros. Ep. 2, 8.

insitor1.full: insĭtor, ōris, m. id., an ingrafter, grafter, Prop. 4 (5), 2, 17; Plin. 18, 33, 76, § 329.

insitor2.full: Insĭtor, ōris, m., the god that presides over grafting, Serv. ad Verg. G. 1, 21.
insitor2.short: Insĭtor, ōris, m., the god that presides over grafting, Serv.

insitum.full: insĭtum, i, n., v. 1. insero fin.

insitus1.full: insĭtus, a, um, P. a., v. 1. insero fin.

insitus2.full: insĭtus, ūs (only in the abl. sing.), m. 1. insero, an ingrafting, Plin. 15, 14, 15, § 52.

insochi.full: Insochi, ōrum, m., a people of Armenia, Tac. A. 13, 37 (dub.; al. Moschi).
insochi.short: Insochi, ōrum, m., a people of Armenia, Tac.

insociabilis.full: in-sŏcĭābĭlis, e, adj., that cannot be joined together, unsociable, incompatible (mostly post-Aug.): gens, Liv. 37, 1: diversae, insociabilesque naturae arborum, Plin. 17, 19, 30, § 137: anum insociabilem nurui efficiebat, Tac. A. 4, 12 fin.: regnum (with discordiae), id. ib. 13, 17; 15, 68.
insociabilis.short: in-sŏcĭābĭlis, e, adj., that cannot be joined together, unsociable, incompatible (mostly post-Aug.): gens, Liv.

insocialis.full: in-sŏcĭālis, e, adj., for insociabilis, unsociable (late Lat.): inconcinna, insocialis, Porphyr. ad Hor. Ep. 1, 18, 6.
insocialis.short: in-sŏcĭālis, e, adj., for insociabilis, unsociable (late Lat.): inconcinna, insocialis, Porphyr.

insolabiliter.full: in-sōlābĭlĭter, adv. 2. in-solor, inconsolably: dolere, Hor. Ep. 1, 14, 8.

insolatio.full: insōlātĭo, ōnis, f. insolo, a setting or placing in the sun: cerae, Plin. 21, 14, 49, § 84.

insolatus.full: insōlātus, Part. and P. a. of insolo.

insolens.full: in-sŏlens, ntis, adj. 2. in-soleo. In gen., i. q. insuetus, contrary to custom, unaccustomed to a thing; unusual, not in use (class.); constr. absol., or with gen.: quid tu Athenas insolens? Ter. And. 5, 4, 4: mutatos deos flebit et aspera aequora emirabitur insolens (= antea insuetus tam celeris immutationis), Hor. C. 1, 5, 8: verbum, i. q. insuetum, insolitum, Cic. Or. 8, 25; Quint. 4, 1, 58; Gell. 11, 7, 1; cf. in sup.: insolentissimum nomen, Quint. prooem. § 14.—With gen.: infamiae, Cic. Att

insolentia.full: in-sŏlentĭa, ae, f. insolens. A being unaccustomed to a thing, unusualness, novelty; with gen. (class.). In gen.: fori, judiciorumque, Cic. Rosc. Am. 31, 88: itineris, Sall. J. 94, 2: loci, Cic. Deiot. 2, 5: voluptatum, id. Cael. 31, 75: disputationis, id. de Or. 1, 22.— Rhet., unusualness, novelty, strangeness, affectedness in the choice of words: orationis, Cic. Brut. 82, 284: verborum, id. de Or. 3, 13: peregrina, id. ib. 12.—In plur.: insolentias verborum a veteribus dictorum respuere, Gell.

insoleo.full: in-sŏleo, 2, v. n., to be wont, i. q. soleo, Caecil. ap. Gell. 3, 16, 4 dub. (perh. solet).

insolesco.full: insŏlesco, ĕre, v. inch. n. [insolens], to become unusual or strange. Lit., of the voice, to begin to change, to become manly: coepit Caelo vox insolescere, Tert. ad Nat. 2, 12; of the womb: uterus insolescens, i. e. swelling up, Hier. in Helv. 18.— Trop., to grow haughty or insolent, to become elated (mostly post-Aug.): ad superbiam, Cato ap. Gell. 7, 3, 15: per licentiam animus humanus insolescit, Sall. C. 6, 7: rebus secundis, Tac. H. 2, 7; Just. 31, 8, 7.

insolidus.full: in-sŏlĭdus, a, um, adj., not solid, soft, tender: herba, Ov. M. 15, 203.
insolidus.short: in-sŏlĭdus, a, um, adj., not solid, soft, tender: herba, Ov.

insolite.full: insŏlĭtē, adv., v. insolitus, a, um, fin.

insolitus.full: in-sŏlĭtus, a, um, adj., unaccustomed, unusual (class.). Act., unaccustomed to a thing; constr. absol., with ad or with gen. Absol.: cur pudentissimas feminas in tantum virorum conventum insolitas, invitasque prodire cogis? Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 37: phocae, not accustomed to rivers, Verg. G. 3, 543.— With ad: insolitus ad laborem, Caes. B. C. 3, 85.— With gen.: civitas insolita rerum bellicarum, Sall. J. 39, 1: genus serviti insolitum, id. H. 2, 81 Dietsch. — Pass., unusual, uncommon: insolita mihi l
insolitus.short: in-sŏlĭtus, a, um, adj., unaccustomed, unusual (class.).

insollicitus.full: in-sollĭcĭtus, a, um, adj., unconcerned, careless: insollicitus dies, ἀμνήμονος ἡμέρα (dub.; perh. ἀμέριμνος), Gloss. Philox.
insollicitus.short: in-sollĭcĭtus, a, um, adj., unconcerned, careless: insollicitus dies, ἀμνήμονος ἡμέρα (dub.;

insolo.full: in-sōlo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. in-sol, to place in the sun, i. e. expose to the sun, in order to warm, dry, etc. (a favorite word with Columella): uvas, Col. 12, 39, 2: insolati dies, sunny, sunshiny days, id. 11, 3, 51: humus insolatur, becomes warmed, id. 4, 17, 8.

insolubilis.full: in-sŏlūbĭlis, e, adj., that cannot be loosed, indissoluble (post-Aug.). Lit.: vinculum, Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 6, § 24: colligatio, id. ib. § 28.— Trop. That cannot be paid: beneticium, creditum insolubile est, Sen. Ben. 4, 12, 1.— That cannot be refuted, incontestable: signum, Quint. 5, 9, 3.— That cannot be destroyed: aeternitas, App. Asclep. p. 100, 37.— Adv.: insŏlūbĭlĭter, indissolubly: vinciri, Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 6; Aug. Civ. Dei, 21, 10.
insolubilis.short: in-sŏlūbĭlis, e, adj., that cannot be loosed, indissoluble (post-Aug.).

insolubilitas.full: in-sŏlūbĭlĭtas, ātis, f. insolubilis, insolubility: quaestionum, Sid. Ep. 4, 11.

insolutus.full: in-sŏlūtus, a, um, adj., not solved: quaestio, Aug. Civ. Dei, 15, 23, 1.
insolutus.short: in-sŏlūtus, a, um, adj., not solved: quaestio, Aug.

insomnia.full: insomnĭa, ae, f. (plur. insomnia, n., Plin. 20, 9, 33, § 82; Prop. 2, 25, 47; Val. Fl. 1, 329; 7, 6; 2, 140) [insomnis], sleeplessness, want of sleep (class.): consequitur comes insomnia, Caecil. ap. Non. 209, 15: aut mox noctu te adiget horsum insomnia, Ter. Eun. 2, 1, 13 Fleck. (Umpfenbach, adigent, v. insomnium): incitabatur insomnia, Suet. Cal. 50.—In plur.: neque insomniis, neque labore fatigari, Sall. C. 27, 2: insomniis carere, Cic. de Sen. 13, 44.

insomnietas.full: insomnĭĕtas, ātis, f. id., for insomnia, sleeplessness (late Lat.), Theod. Prisc. 2, 1; Plin. Val. 1, 35.

insomniosus.full: insomnĭōsus, a, um, adj. insomnia, sleepless, troubled with want of sleep, Cato, R. R. 157, 8.

insomnis.full: in-somnis, e, adj. 2. in-somnus, sleepless (poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Of living beings, Hor. C. 3, 7, 8: juventus, Pers. 3, 54: insomnes magis, quam pervigiles, Tac. A. 1, 65: draco, Ov. M. 9, 190.— Of things: oculi, Stat. Th. 3, 328: dens, i. e. of the dragon, from which armed men sprung, Luc. 4, 552: nox, Verg. A. 9, 167: cura, Luc. 2, 239.

insomnium1.full: insomnĭum, ĭi, n. in-somnus, a dream (mostly in plur.). In sing.: illud haud ambigitur, qualicumque insomnio ipsi fratrique perniciem allatam, Tac. A. 11, 4: per insomnium dicere, in a dream, Arn. 7, 244: ipsa insomnii verba, Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 3.— In plur., Ter. Eun. 2, 1, 13 Umpfenbach; Tib. 3, 4, 1; Verg. A. 4, 9; 6, 896; Sil. 10, 358; 11, 102; Plin. 18, 12, 30, § 118.

insono.full: in-sŏno, ŭi, 1, v. n., to make a noise in or on, to sound, sound loudly, resound (mostly poet.): Boreae cum spiritus alto Insonat Aegaeo, roars on the Ægean Sea, Verg. A. 12, 366: insonuere cavernae, id. ib. 2, 53: caeli delapsa per auras Insonuit, resounded flying through the air, id. ib. 11, 596; cf. pennis, Ov. M. 13, 608: calamis, to play upon, id. ib. 11, 161: insonuitque flagello, cracked his whip, Verg. A. 5, 579; cf. poet. with acc.: verbera insonuit, id. ib. 7, 451: quasi faucibus aliqu

insons.full: in-sons, ntis, adj. Guiltless, innocent; constr. with gen. or absol. (class., but not in Cic. or Cæs.): insontem probri accusare, Plaut. Am. 3, 1, 9: aliquem falso atque insontem arguere, id. Bacch. 3, 3, 10: publici consilii, Liv. 34, 32, 8: culpae, id. 22, 49.— With abl. (rare): si regni crimine insons fuerit, Liv. 4, 15, 1.—Absol.: purus et insons ... si vivo, Hor. S. 1, 6, 69; Sen. Hipp. 486: amicus, Verg. A. 2, 93; 5, 350. — Esp., as subst.: insontes, um, m., the innocent (opp. sontes): cir

insonus.full: in-sŏnus a, um, adj., without sound, noiseless, silent (post-class.). Lit.: passus, Amm. 27, 12; cf. gressus, id. 29, 5: vestigium, App. M. 3, p. 138, 22.— Transf.: litterae, i. e. mutae, App. de Mundo, p. 66, 29.
insonus.short: in-sŏnus a, um, adj., without sound, noiseless, silent (post-class.).

insopibilis.full: in-sōpībĭlis, e, adj. 2. in-sopio, that cannot be lulled to sleep (post-class.): flamma, i. e. inextinguishable, Mart. Cap. 1, § 7: ignis, id. 9, § 910.

insopitus.full: in-sōpītus, a, um, adj., not lulled to sleep, sleepless, wakeful (poet.): draco, Ov. M. 7, 36; Luc. 9, 357: ignis, inextinguishable, Claud. Rapt. Pros. 3, 401.
insopitus.short: in-sōpītus, a, um, adj., not lulled to sleep, sleepless, wakeful (poet.): draco, Ov.

insordesco.full: in-sordesco, dŭi, 3, v. inch. n., to become dirty or foul (post-class.), Sid. Ep. 5, 13.— Esp., to become gloomy, to darken, Sid. Ep. 2, 2; Rutil. Itin. 1, 617.

insortitus.full: in-sortītus, a, um, adj., not allotted: spicula insortita (al. specula in sortitu), Plaut. Cas. 2, 4, 27.
insortitus.short: in-sortītus, a, um, adj., not allotted: spicula insortita (al.

inspatior.full: in-spătĭor, āri, v. dep. n., to walk about in a place: inspatiantem (al. exspatiantem), Prud. Apoth. 130.

inspeciatus.full: in-spĕcĭātus, a, um, adj., unshapen: substantia informis et inspeciata (late Lat.), Tert. adv. Val. 10 fin.
inspeciatus.short: in-spĕcĭātus, a, um, adj., unshapen: substantia informis et inspeciata (late Lat.), Tert.

inspeciosus.full: in-spĕcĭōsus, a, um, adj., unshapely, ugly: puer, Petr. Fragm. Trag. 74, 8 Burm.
inspeciosus.short: in-spĕcĭōsus, a, um, adj., unshapely, ugly: puer, Petr.

inspectabilis.full: inspectābĭlis, e, adj. inspecto, worth looking at, glorious: victoria, Gell. 4, 18, 2.

inspectatio.full: inspectātĭo, ōnis, f. inspecto, a looking into, considering (post-Aug.).— Lit.: Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 17; 4, 35 (in Sen. Q. N. 1, 7, 3, read inseptiones).

inspectator.full: inspectātor, ōris, m., id., for inspector, an overseer (late Lat.), Symm. Ep. 6, 9.
inspectator.short: inspectātor, ōris, m., id., for inspector, an overseer (late Lat.), Symm.

inspectio.full: inspectĭo, ōnis, f. inspicio, a looking into, inspection (post-Aug.). Lit. In gen.: ager prima inspectione neque vitia, neque virtutes abditas ostendit, Col. 1, 4, 1: speculi non tam possessio culpatur quam inspectio, App. Mag. 13, p. 282, 4.— In partic., a looking through, examination: tabularum, Quint. 5, 5, 2; Dig. 29, 3, 2, § 5: rationum, Trajan. ap. Plin. Ep. 10, 57, 1.— Trop., consideration, investigation, contemplation; hence theory, in opposition to practice, Quint. 2, 18, 3; 2, 17, 42;

inspectivus.full: inspectīvus, a, um, adj. inspectio, considering, reflecting, contemplative (postclass.): pars rationis philosophiae (opp. actualis), Isid. Orig. 2, 24.

inspecto.full: inspecto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. freq. a. inspicio, to look at, observe, view (class. only in part. pres.): aliquid, Plaut. Poen. 3, 3, 69: nescio quis inspectavit per impluvium, id. Mil. 2, 2, 18: me inspectante, before my eyes, Cic. Fam. 1, 9, 19; cf.: inspectante exercitu, id. ib. 6, 18, 2: inspectantibus nobis, Caes. B. G. 7, 25; and: astante et inspectante ipso, in his presence and before his eyes, id. B. C. 2, 20.

inspector.full: inspector, ōris, m. id.. A viewer, observer (post-Aug.), Sen. Ben. 1, 9, 3.— An inspector, examiner (late Lat.), Dig. 13, 6, 10; Cod. Th. 11, 1, 31; Mos. et Rom. Leg. Coll. 15, 1, 2 al.

inspectrix.full: inspectrix, īcis, f. inspector, she that inspects or examines (late Lat.), Ambros. Ep. 5.

inspectus1.full: inspectus, a, um, Part., from inspicio.
inspectus1.short: inspectus, a, um, Part., from inspicio.

inspectus2.full: inspectus, ūs, m. inspicio. A looking at, inspection, an examination (postAug.): jecoris, Amm. 22, 1, 25.— Contemplation: animus liber ad inspectum, oculis inspectu minacibus, App. M. 10, p. 254, 26: universi, Sen. Ep. 92, 6.

insperabilis.full: in-spērābĭlis, e, adj., that cannot be hoped for (post-class.): pax, Gell. 4, 18, 3: nuntius, Amm. 15, 5, 17.
insperabilis.short: in-spērābĭlis, e, adj., that cannot be hoped for (post-class.): pax, Gell.

insperans.full: in-spērans, ntis, adj.
