sugillo.full: sūgillo (suggillo, oited ap. Victorin. p. 2465 P.), āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. etym. dub.; perh. akin with sugo, to beat black-andblue (mostly post-Aug.). Lit.: oculi ex ictu suffusi cruore et sugillati, Plin. 31, 9, 45, § 100: athleta, qui numquam sugillatus est, Sen. Ep. 13, 2: oculos patri, perh. to knock out, Varr. ap. Non. 171, 13. — Part. perf. as subst.: sūgillāta, ōrum, n. (sc. loca), black-and-blue spots, bruises: allium sugillata aut liventia ad colorem reducit, black-and-blue spots, Plin. 20

sugo.full: sūgo, xi, ctum, 3, v. a. root svag-; cf. sucus, to suck (class.). Lit.: (animalium) alia sugunt, alia carpunt, Cic. N. D. 2, 47, 122: (agni) matris sugunt mammam, Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 20: porca frequentiore numero sucta deficiet, exhausted, Pall. Febr. 26, 5: terram, to exhaust, Varr. R. R. 1, 44, 3. — Trop.: cum lacte nutricis errorem suxisse, to have sucked, imbibed, Cic. Tusc. 3, 1, 2.

sui.full: sŭi (gen.), dat. sĭbī^, acc. and abl. sē or sēsē, sing. and plur. (old dat. sĭbei, C. I. L. 1, 38; 1, 1056; 1, 1180 et saep.: sibe, ib. 1, 1267; 5, 300; cf. Quint. 1, 7, 24; and v. Neue, Formenl. 2, p. 180 sq.; on the quantity of the final i, v. Ritschl, Opusc. 2, p. 632 sqq.; old acc. sed, C. I. L. 1, 196, 13 sq.; 1, 197, 21; strengthened acc. sepse = se ipse, Cic. Rep. 3, 8, 12; cf. Sen. Ep. 108, 32: semet, Hor. S. 1, 6, 78; Liv. 2, 12, 7; 2, 44, 8 al.), pron. of 3d pers. in recipr. and reflex

suifico.full: sŭĭfĭco, āre, 1, v. a., to make his own (eccl. Lat.), Rustic. c. Aceph. p. 1245.

suile.full: sŭīle, is, n. sus, a hog-sty, Col. 7, 9, 14.

suillates.full: Sŭillātes, ĭum, m., a people of Umbria, Plin. 3, 14, 19, § 114.
suillates.short: Sŭillātes, ĭum, m., a people of Umbria, Plin.

suillus.full: sŭillus, a, um, adj. sus, of or belonging to swine. Adj.: pecus, Varr. R. R. 2, 4, 1; Col. 7, 9, 14: grex, Liv. 22, 10: genus, Plin. 8, 52, 78, § 212: rostrum, id. 8, 33, 51, § 121: caro, swine's flesh, pork, Varr. R. R. 2, 4, 8: lac, Plin. 28, 8, 29, § 116: fungi, an inferior kind of mushroom, black hogmushrooms, id. 22, 23, 47, § 96; Mart. 3, 60, 5. — Subst.: sŭilla, ae, f. (sc. caro), pork, Cels. 3, 9; 5, 26, 30; Plin. 30, 5, 12, § 38.

suinus.full: sŭīnus, a, um, adj. id., of or belonging to swine, swine-, Prisc. 594 P.: caro, Varr. R. R. 2, 4, 8 (MSS.; Gesn. and Schneid. suilla): sevum, Theod. Prisc. 4, 1.

suiones.full: Suĭŏnes, um, m., a northern Germanic people of Scandinavia, in the mod. Sweden, Tac. G. 44 and 45.
suiones.short: Suĭŏnes, um, m., a northern Germanic people of Scandinavia, in the mod.

suismontium.full: Suismontium, i, n., a mountain of Liguria, Liv. 39, 2; 40, 41.
suismontium.short: Suismontium, i, n., a mountain of Liguria, Liv.

sulca.full: Sulca, ae, m., a Roman surname: Q. Baetius Sulca, Liv. 42, 6.
sulca.short: Sulca, ae, m., a Roman surname: Q.

sulcamen.full: sulcāmen, ĭnis, n. sulco, a furrow, = sulcus, App. M. 6, p. 174, 9.

sulcator.full: sulcātor, ōris, m. id., one who draws furrows, a furrower, plougher (in postAug. poets). Lit.: Leontini campi, Prud. adv. Symm. 2, 939: patuli agri, Avien. Perieg. 587.— Transf., one who sails over, traverses, etc.: sulcator navita ponti, Sil. 7, 363: pigri Averni, i. e. Charon, Stat. Th. 11, 588; cf. undae, id. ib. 8, 18: Bagrada sulcator harenae, Luc. 4, 588.— A render, tearer, lacerator: lateris sulcator (vultur), Claud. Rapt. Pros. 2, 340.

sulcatorius.full: sulcātōrĭus, a, um, adj., sailing over; only in subst.: sulcātōrĭa, ae, f. (late Lat.), a ship, a barge, Cassiod. Var. 2, 20.
sulcatorius.short: sulcātōrĭus, a, um, adj., sailing over;

sulci.full: Sulci, ōrum, m., an ancient maritime city on the southern coast of Sardinia, founded by Carthage, now the ruins of Palma de Solo near Sulci, Mel. 2, 7, 19.— Hence, Sulcensis, e, of Sulci: promuntorium, Plin. 3, 7, 13, § 84; Mart. Cap. 6, § 645.— Sulcĭtāni, ōrum, m., the inhabitants of Sulci, Auct. B. Afr. 98, 1; Plin. 3, 7, 13, § 85.
sulci.short: Sulci, ōrum, m., an ancient maritime city on the southern coast of Sardinia, founded by Carthage, now the ruins of Palma de Solo near Sulci, Mel.

sulco.full: sulco, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. sulcus, to furrow, cut furrows through, to plough (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; not in Cic. or Cæs.). Lit., in agriculture: agros, Tib. 2, 3, 85: (rura) sulcata Camilli Vomere, Luc. 1, 168: vomere humum, Ov. Tr. 3, 10, 68: campos vomere, Sil. 9, 191. — Absol.: recto plenoque sulcare, Col. 2, 2, 25.— Transf. Ingen., to furrow, plough; poet., to sail over, traverse, pass through, etc.: sulcant fossas, quo pluvia aqua delabatur, Varr. R. R. 1, 29, 2: (anguis) hare

sulcus1.full: sulcus, a, um, adj., only ficus sulca, an unknown species of fig-tree, Col. 5, 10, 11.
sulcus1.short: sulcus, a, um, adj., only ficus sulca, an unknown species of fig-tree, Col.

sulcus2.full: sulcus, i, m. Gr. ὁλκός, from ἕλκω, a furrow made by the plough (cf.: lira, porca): sulci appellantur, quā aratrum ducitur, vel sationis faciendae causā vel urbis condendae, vel fossura rectis lateribus, ubi arbores serantur: quod vocabulum quidam ex Graeco fictum, quia illi dicant ὁλκόν, Fest. p. 302 Müll.: quā aratrum vomere lacunam striam facit, sulcus vocatur: quod est inter duos sulcos elata terra, dicitur porca, Varr. R. R. 1, 29, 3: sulco vario ne ares, Cato, R. R. 61, 1: cum sulcus altiu

sulfur.full: sulfur (in MSS. also sulphur and sulpur), ŭris, n. (masc., Tert. adv. Prax. 16; Veg. Vet. 1, 38 med.), brimstone, sulphur. Lit., Plin. 35, 15, 50, § 174; Cato, R. R. 39, 1; Col. 8, 5, 11: vivum, Liv. 39, 13, 12; Ov. F. 4, 739; Lucr. 6, 221; 6, 748; 6, 807; Tib. 1, 5, 11; Prop. 4 (5), 8, 86; Ov. M. 5, 405 et saep.—Plur.: viva, Verg. G. 3, 449: vivacia, Ov. M. 3, 374: lurida, id. ib. 14, 791; 15, 351; Quint. 12, 10, 76 Spald. N. cr.; used as a cement, Juv. 5, 48.— Transf., poet., lightning (so cal

sulfurans.full: sulfŭrans (sulph-), antis, adj. sulfur; cf. sulfuratus, containing sulphur, sulphurous: aquae, Tert. adv. Val. 15.

sulfuraria.full: sulfŭrārĭa (sulph-), ae, f. sulfur, a sulphur pit or mine: in calcariam vel sulfurariam damnari, Dig. 48, 19, 8, § 10; 47, 2, 53, § 10.

sulfuratio.full: sulfŭrātĭo (sulph-), ōnis, f. id., a vein of sulphur in the earth, Sen. Q. N. 3, 15, 5.

sulfuratus.full: sulfŭrātus (sulph-), a, um, adj. id., impregnated with sulphur, sulphurated. Adj.: fontes, Vitr. 8, 3: aqua, Plin. 31, 6, 32, § 59: ramentum, Mart. 10, 3, 3: merx, id. 12, 57, 14: lana, Cels. 4, 5.—Comp.: gehenna, Tert. adv. Marc. 1, 28.— Subst.: sul-fŭrāta, ōrum, n. (Sc. fila.) Brimstone-matches, Mart. 1, 42, 4.— (Sc. loca.) Veins of sulphur, Plin. 31, 3, 28, § 49.

sulfureus.full: sulfŭrĕus (sulph-), a, um, adj. id., of or like sulphur, sulphurous, sulphureous: fornaces, Ov. M. 15, 340: aqua, Verg. A. 7, 517: lux fulminum, Plin. 35, 15, 50, § 177: color, id. 35, 6, 25, § 41: odor, id. 36, 19, 34, § 141.

sulfurosus.full: sulfŭrōsus (sulph-), a, um, adj. id., full of sulphur, sulphureous: fontes, Vitr. 8, 3 med.: plurima sulfurosa, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 7.

suliviae.full: Sŭlĭvĭae, ārum, f. a lengthened form for Silviae, a kind of wood-goddesses, Inscr. Orell. 2051. — Also in the form SVLEVIAE, Inscr. Orell. 2099 sq.

sulla.full: Sulla (less correctly Sylla), ae, m., a surname in the gens Cornelia. So, esp., L. Cornelius Sulla Felix, the celebrated Roman dictator, Cic. Div. 1, 33, 72; Sall. J. 100, 2; Flor. 3, 21, 5; Vell. 2, 17, 1.—Hence, Sullānus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to Sulla: tempus, Cic. Par. 6, 2, 46: ager, id. Agr. 2, 26, 70: assignationes, id. ib. 3, 1, 3: proscriptio, Sen. Ira, 2, 34, 3: saeculum, id. ib. 1, 20, 4: partes, Nep. Att. 2: tempora, Plin. 9, 35, 59, § 123. — Subst.: Sullāni, ōrum, m., partisa
sulla.short: Sulla (less correctly Sylla), ae, m., a surname in the gens Cornelia.

sullaturio.full: sullātŭrĭo, īre, v. desid. n. [Sulla], to imitate or play the part of Sulla: ita sullaturit animus ejus et proscripturit, Cic. Att. 9, 10, 6; cf. Quint. 8, 3, 32; 8, 6, 32.

sulmo.full: Sulmo, ōnis, m. A town in the territory of the Peligni, near Corfinium, the birthplace of Ovid, now Sulmona: aquosus, Ov. Am. 3, 15, 11: gelidus, id. F. 4, 81; Sil. 9, 76; 8, 511; Ov. Tr. 4, 10, 3; Cic. Att. 8, 4, 3; 8, 12, A, 1; Flor. 3, 21, 28.—Hence, Sulmōnensis, e, adj., of or belonging to Sulmo: ager, Plin. 17, 26, 41, § 250.—Plur.: Sulmōnenses, ĭum, m., the inhabitants of Sulmo, Caes. B. C. 1, 18, 1; Plin. 3, 12, 17, § 106.—Sing. fem., Juv. 6, 187 —* Sul-montīnus, a, um, adj., of Sulmo: co

sulphur.full: sulphur, and its derivv., v. sulfur.

sulpicilla.full: Sulpĭcilla, ae, f. dim. Sulpicia, i. e. the poetess Sulpicia, Fulg. Myth. praef. 1 pr.; v. Sulpicius, VII.

sulpicius.full: Sulpĭcĭus, i, m.; Sulpĭcĭa, ae, f., the name of a Roman gens; e. g. Ser. Sulpicius Galba, consul 610 A.U.C., and an able orator, Cic. de Or. 1, 10, 39; id. Brut. 22, 86.— C. Sulpicius Gallus, a connoisseur in Greek literature, and a good orator, Cic. Brut. 20, 78; id. Off. 1, 6, 19; id. Lael. 27, 101.— Ser. Sulpicius Rufus, a very celebrated jurist, a contemporary and correspondent of Cicero; v. Cic. Fam. 4, 1 sqq.; Gell. 2, 10, 1; Dig. 1, 2, 2, § 42 sq.— C. Sulpicius Apollinaris, a grammarian,

sultis.full: sultis = si vultis, v. volo init.

sum1.full: sum, fŭi, esse (2d pers. ĕs, but usu. ēs in Plaut and Ter; old forms, indic. pres. esum for sum, acc. to Varr. L. L. 9, § 100 Müll.: essis for es, Att. ap. Non. 200, 30, or Trag. Rel. p. 283 Rib.: simus for sumus, used by Augustus, acc. to Suet. Aug. 87; fut. escit for erit, XII. Tab. ap. Gell. 20, 1, 25: esit, XII. Tab. ap. Fest. s. v. nec, p. 162 Müll.: escunt for erunt, Cic. Leg. 2, 24, 60, 3, 3, 9; Lucr. 1, 619; perf. fūvimus for fuimus, Enn. ap. Cic. de Or. 3, 42, 168: FVVEIT, C. I. L. 1, 1

sum2.full: sum = eum, Enn. ap. Fest., v. is.

sum3.full: sum- in composition, for sub before m; v. sub fin.
sum3.short: sum- in composition, for sub before m;

sumen.full: sūmen, inis, n. contr. from sugimen, sugmen, from sugo, a breast, of women (syn.: uber, mamma). Lit. In gen.: manus lactanti in sumine sidat, Lucil. ap. Non. 458, 7.— In partic., a sow's udder, the paps of a sow (esteemed a delicacy by the Romans): pernam, abdomen, sumen, suis glandium, Plaut. Curc. 2, 3, 44; id. Ps. 1, 2, 33; id. Capt. 4, 3, 4; Plin. 11, 37, 84, § 211; Mart. 13, 44, 1.—* Meton., a sow, a hog, Juv. 12, 73. — Transf., the fat part, the richest portion: (Caesar Vopiscus) campos Ro

suminatus.full: sūmĭnātus, a, um, adj. sumen, of or belonging to a sow's udder, that has the paps on (post-class.): caro, i. e. the paps or udder of a sow, Arn. 2, 73. sus, i. e. a sow, Lampr. Alex. Sev 22.

summa.full: summa, ae, f. (sc. res; old gen. summai, Lucr. 1, 984; 6, 679) [summus, v. superus]. Lit., that which is highest in any thing, the top, summit, surface (postAug. and very rare): testudines evectae in summā pelagi, Plin. 9, 10, 12, § 35 (cf. summus, I. s. v. superus).— Transf., that which is most important or prominent in any thing, the main thing, chief point, principal matter; the sum, height, substance, summit, completion, perfection In gen.: leges a me edentur non perfectae ... sed ipsae summ

summaestus.full: sum-maestus (subm-), a, um. adj., somewhat sorrowful, Amm. 30, 1, 2.

summalis.full: summālis, e, adj. summa, containing a sum, whole (post-class.), Tert. adv. Herm. 31.—Hence, summālĭter, adv., wholly, perfectly, Primas. in Coloss. 1.

summanans.full: sum-mānans (subm-), antis, Part. [mano], flowing beneath: aqua sub terrā, Vitr. 3, 1 med.

summanes.full: Summānes (Subm-), ĭum, m., a kind of inferior deities, Mart. Cap. 2, § 164.
summanes.short: Summānes (Subm-), ĭum, m., a kind of inferior deities, Mart.

summano.full: summāno (subm-), āre, v. a. and n [sub-mano]. Neutr., to glide or trickle under, Vitr. 8, 1, 2.— Act., to wet somewhat: vestimenta mea, ubi obdormivi ebrius, Summano (with a play on the name Summanus, i. e. Pluto), Plaut. Curc. 3, 46 (v. the passage in connection).

summanus.full: Summānus (Subm-), i, m., a Roman deity to whom nocturnal lightnings were asscribed, but whose precise nature was unknown even to Ovid; acc. to Mart. Cap. i. q. Pluto, Ov. F. 6, 731; Mart. Cap. 2, § 161; Plaut. Bacch. 4, 8, 54; id. Curc. 3, 43; Liv. 32, 29; Cic. Div. 1, 10, 16; Plin. 2, 52, 53, § 138; 29, 4, 14, § 57; Arn. 3, 44; 5, 37; 6, 3 Orell.; Aug. Civ. Dei, 4, 23; Inscr. Orell. 1466; v. Merkel ad Ov. F. p. ccviii.—Hence: Summanalia liba farinacea in modum rotae ficta, Fest. pp. 348 and 349
summanus.short: Summānus (Subm-), i, m., a Roman deity to whom nocturnal lightnings were asscribed, but whose precise nature was unknown even to Ovid;

summara.full: Summara, ae, f., a town in Ethiopia, Plin. 6, 30, 35, § 193.
summara.short: Summara, ae, f., a town in Ethiopia, Plin.

summarium.full: summārĭum, ĭi, n. summa, a summary, epitome, abstract: oratio, quae nunc vulgo breviarium dicitur, olim, cum Latine loqueremur, summarium, vocabatur, Sen. Ep. 39, 1.

summas.full: summas, ātis, comm. id., of high or noble birth, high-born, noble, eminent, distinguished (ante- and post-class.): vir, Plaut. Ps. 1, 2, 90; id. Stich. 3, 2, 36; Amm. 14, 6, 12; Sid. Ep. 3, 11: matronae, Plaut. Cist. 1, 1, 27: dea, App. M. 11, p. 267, 38: virgo, id. ib. 4, p. 153, 9: puella, Sid. Ep. 9, 6.

summatim.full: summātim, adv. id., on the surface, on the outside, slightly. Lit. (post-Aug. and very rare): radicem summatim eradere, Col. 12, 48, 1: eruere radices, id. Arb. 6, 2: ablaqueare vitem, id. ib. 10, 5.— Trop., slightly, summarily, cursorily, briefly, compendiously, etc. (class.): summatim rescribere paucis, Lucil. ap. Non. 296, 5: de re pecuariā breviter ac summatim percurram, Varr. R. R. 2, praef. § 7: aliquid summatim perscribere, Cic. Att. 5, 16, 1: aliquid cognoscere, id. Fam. 10, 28, 3: summa

summatus.full: summātus, ūs, m. id., chief rule, supremacy, sovereignty, = principatus: imperium ac summatum petere, Lucr. 5, 1142.

summedius.full: sum-mĕdĭus (subm-), a, um, adj., middle, mean positura, Diom. p. 432 P.
summedius.short: sum-mĕdĭus (subm-), a, um, adj., middle, mean positura, Diom.

summejo.full: sum-mējo (subm-), ĕre, v. a., to make water under a thing, se, Marc. Emp. 8, 5 med.

summejulus.full: summējŭlus (subm-), i, m. summejo, one who makes water under himself, who wets his bed, Marc. Emp. 26 fin.

summergo.full: sum-mergo (subm-), si, sum, 3, v. a., to dip or plunge under, to sink, overwhelm, submerge, submerse. Lit. (class.; most freq. pass.): summersus equus voraginibus, Cic. Div. 1, 33, 73: genera summersarum beluarum, id. N. D. 2, 39, 100: salgama semper jure summersa, Col. 12, 4, 5: navis summersa, * Caes. B. C. 3, 39: ferrum summersum in undā, Ov M. 12, 279: ipsos potuit summergere ponto, Verg. A. 1, 40: quod (saxum) tumidis submersum tunditur olim Fluctibus, id. ib. 5, 125: aliquot procellis summ

summersio.full: summersĭo (subm-), ōnis, f. summergo, a sinking, drowning, submersion (late Lat.), Arn. 5, 182; Firm. Math. 1, 2 fin.

summerso.full: summerso, āre, 1, v. freq. a. id., to plunge repeatedly or thoroughly, Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. 3, 26.

summersus1.full: summersus (subm-), a, um, Part. of summergo.

summersus2.full: summersus (subm-), ūs, m. summergo, a plunging under water, sinking (post-class.), Tert. Anim. 32 med.

summerus.full: sum-mĕrus (subm-), a, um, adj., rather pure: vinum, Plaut. Stich. 1, 3, 116.
summerus.short: sum-mĕrus (subm-), a, um, adj., rather pure: vinum, Plaut.

summigratio.full: sum-mī^grātĭo (subm-), ōnis, f., an emigration (late Lat.): e patriā, Amm. 25, 9, 1.
summigratio.short: sum-mī^grātĭo (subm-), ōnis, f., an emigration (late Lat.): e patriā, Amm.

summinia.full: summĭnĭa (subm-), ae, f. sub-minium, a kind of garment for women, Plaut. Ep. 2, 2, 50.

sumministratio.full: summĭnistrātĭo (subm-), ōnis, f. sumministro, a giving, furnishing, supplying, subministration (post-class.): divina incorruptibilitatis, Tert. Apol. 48 fin.

sumministrator.full: summĭnistrātor (subm-), ōris, m. id., one who aids or assists; trop., an abettor, promoter (post- Aug.): libidinum testisque, Sen. Ep. 114, 23.

sumministratus.full: summĭnistrātus (subm-), ūs, m. id., a furnishing, supplying: exiguus cibi, Macr. S. 7, 12, § 20.

sumministro.full: sum-mĭnistro (subm-), āvi, ātum, 1, v. a., to aid by giving; to give, furnish, afford, supply (class.). Lit.: pecuniam alicui, Cic. Deiot. 9, 25: tela clam, id. Cael. 9, 20: tela ad manum, Quint. 5, 7, 8: tela agentibus, id. 12, 3, 4: lapides telaque, Caes. B. G. 3, 25: frumentum, id. ib. 1, 40: auxilia hostibus nostris, id. ib. 4, 20: sauciis ac defatigatis integros equites, Auct. B. Afr. 78: puteus, qui CCC. pondo argenti Hannibali sumministravit in dies, Plin. 33, 6, 31, § 97: aquam radicibus

summisse.full: summissē, adv., v. summitto, P. a. fin.

summissim.full: summissim (subm-), adv. summissus, in a low voice, gently, softly (post-Aug. and very rare): fabulantes, Suet. Aug. 74: ridere (with sensim), Gell. 17, 8, 7.

summissio.full: summissĭo (subm-), ōnis, f. summitto, a letting down, lowering, dropping, sinking (Ciceron.): ex contentione vocis et summissione, Cic. Off. 1, 41, 146: (iterationes) erunt ab hac summissione orationis alienae, id. Or. 25, 85: nec elatio nec summissio, i. e. depression, id. Top. 18, 71.

summissus1.full: summissus (subm-), a, um, Part. and P. a. of summitto.

summissus2.full: summissus (subm-), ūs, m. summitto, a sending to or in, introduction: ex summissu erroris ulciscitur, Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 16 med.

summitas.full: summĭtas, ātis, f. summus, the highest part, height, top, summit (post-class.): placidioribus locis septem pedibus summitas vitis insurgit, Pall. 1, 6, 10; Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 6 med.: terrae, Censor. de Die Nat. 13: deum summitatem omnium summorum obtinentem, Arn. 1, 13; App. Dogm. Plat. 2, p. 15, 7; Amm. 15, 10, 6 (not Plin. 37, 9, 37, § 118, where Jan. reads imitata).

summitto.full: sum-mitto (subm-), mīsi, missum, 3, v. a. With the force of sub predominating (mostly poet. and in post- Aug. prose; cf. subicio). In gen. To set, put, or place under or below: singuli agni binis nutricibus submittuntur: nec quicquam subtrahi submissis expedit, Col. 7, 4, 3: vaccas tauris (for breeding), Pall. Jul. 4: vaccas in feturam, id. ib. 4, 1: equas alternis annis, id. Mart. 13, 6: canterium vitibus, Col. 4, 14, 1.— To send or put forth below, or from below, to cause to spring forth, to s

summoenium.full: Summoenĭum (Subm-), ii, n. submoenia, a place in Rome, probably near the walls, the resort of vile characters, Mart. 1, 35, 6.— Hence, Summoenĭānus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to Summœnium: uxores, Mart. 3, 82, 2; cf. buccae, id. 11, 61, 2.

summolestus.full: sum-mŏlestus (subm-), a, um, adj., somewhat troublesome or vexatious (very rare): illud est mihi submolestum, quod, etc., Cic. Att. 16, 4, 4.—Adv.: summŏle-stē, with some vexation: aliquid ferre, Cic. Att. 5, 21, 1.
summolestus.short: sum-mŏlestus (subm-), a, um, adj., somewhat troublesome or vexatious (very rare): illud est mihi submolestum, quod, etc., Cic.

summoneo.full: sum-mŏnĕo (subm-), ŭi, 2, v. n., to remind privily, give a hint (very rare): summonuit me Parmeno, quod, etc., Ter. Eun. 3, 5, 22: patres salutavit nominatim singulos, nullo summonente, Suet. Aug. 53.

summonstro.full: sum-monstro (subm-), āre, v. a., to show privately: responsa, Arn. 3, 143 (al. subministrat).

summorosus.full: sum-mōrōsus (subm-), a, um, adj., somewhat peerish or morose: me illa valde movent stomachosa et quasi summorosa ridicula, Cic. de Or. 2, 69, 279.
summorosus.short: sum-mōrōsus (subm-), a, um, adj., somewhat peerish or morose: me illa valde movent stomachosa et quasi summorosa ridicula, Cic.

summotenus.full: summō-tĕnus, adv., up to the top: summotenus florescentibus floribus, App. Herb. 75.
summotenus.short: summō-tĕnus, adv., up to the top: summotenus florescentibus floribus, App.

summotor.full: summōtor (subm-), ōris, m. summoveo, one who puts aside or removes (in order to make room), a clearer of a space: summotor aditūs, praeco, accensus, i. e. the lictor, Liv. 45, 29, 2.

summotus.full: summōtus (subm-), a, um, Part. of summoveo.

summoveo.full: sum-mŏvĕo (subm-), mōvi, mōtum, 2 (sync. form of the pluperf. subj. summosses, Hor. S. 1, 9, 48), v. a., to send or drive off or away, to remove (freq. and class.; cf.: repello, amolior). Lit. In gen.: hostes a portā, Caes. B. G. 7, 50: hostes ex muro ac turribus, id. B. C. 2, 11: hostes ex agro Romano trans Anienem, Liv. 4, 17, 11: hostium lembos statione, id. 45, 10, 2: recusantes advocatos, Cic. Quint. 8, 31: quam (Academiam) summovere non audeo, id. Leg. 1, 13, 39: summotā contione, id. Fl.

summula.full: summŭla, ae, f. dim. summa, a small sum: summulas minutas distribuit servis, Sen. Ep. 77, 8; App. M. 11, p. 271, 32; Prud. στεφ. 2, 131.

summultiplex.full: sum-multĭplex (subm-), plĭcis, adj., contained many times in another number, Boëth. Inst. Arithm. 1, 22.
summultiplex.short: sum-multĭplex (subm-), plĭcis, adj., contained many times in another number, Boëth.

summurmuro.full: sum-murmŭro (subm-), āvi, 1, v. a., to murmur a little or in secrēt (late Lat.), Aug. Conf. 6, 9; 8, 11.

summus.full: summus, a, um, adj., v. superus.

summussi.full: summussi = murmuratores (murmurers). Naevius: odi, inquit, summussos; proinde aperte dice, quid sit, Fest. pp. 298 and 299 Müll. (Trag. Rel. p. 12 Rib.) [submusso].

summuto.full: sum-mūto (subm-), āre, v. a., to change, interchange, substitute one thing for another: hanc ὑπαλλαγὴν rhetores, quia quasi summutantur verba pro verbis, μετωνυμίαν grammatici vocant, quod nomina transferuntur, Cic. Or. 27, 93.

sumo.full: sūmo, sumpsi, sumptum, 3 (sync. form of the inf. perf. sumpse, Naev. ap. Gell. 2, 19, 6 (Com. Rel. v. 97 Rib.; suremit for sumpsit, surempsit for sumpserit, Paul. Diac. 299, 2; Fest. 298, 9), v. a. contr. for subimo, from sub-emo, to take, take up, lay hold of, assume (syn. capio). In gen.: auferere, non abibis, si ego fustem sumpsero, Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 202: laciniam, id. Merc. 1, 2, 16: si hoc digitulis duobus sumebas primoribus, id. Bacch. 4, 4, 24: si mutuas non potero, certum'st sumam foenore

sumptifacio.full: sumptĭ-făcĭo, fēci, 3, v. a. 2. sumptus, to lay out, spend, expend: restim, Plaut. Cas. 2, 7, 2.

sumptio.full: sumptio (collat. form sumpsio, Cato, R. R. 145, 2), ōnis, f. sumo, a taking. Lit., Vitr. 1, 2, 2.— Trop., in logic, a premise taken for granted, an assumption: demus tibi istas duas sumptiones, ea quae λήμματα appellant dialectici; sed nos Latine loqui malumus, Cic. Div. 2, 53, 108.

sumptito.full: sumptĭto, āvi, 1, v. freq. a. id., to take much of or in strong doses: saepius helleborum, Plin. 25, 5, 21, § 51.

sumptuarius.full: sumptŭārĭus, a, um, adj. 2. sumptus, of or relating to expense, sumptuary: rationes nostrae, Cic. Att. 13, 47, 1: lex, id. ib. 13, 7, 1; cf. id. Fam. 7, 26, 2; Suet. Caes. 43; id. Aug. 34; Gell. 2, 24.

sumptuatus.full: sumptŭātus, a, um, Part., well furnished (late Lat.); cf. Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. M. 2, 18.
sumptuatus.short: sumptŭātus, a, um, Part., well furnished (late Lat.);

sumptuositas.full: sumptŭōsĭtas, ātis, f. sumptuosus, great expense, costliness, expensiveness, Sid. Ep. 9, 6.

sumptuosus.full: sumptŭōsus, a, um, adj. 2. sumptus, very expensive or costly. Of things, that costs much, dear, expensive, sumptuous: ager, Cato, R. R. 1, 6: cenae, Cic. Fam. 9, 23 fin.: hostia, Hor. C. 3, 23, 18: bellum, Liv. 45, 3: tutela, Plin. Ep. 2, 17, 4: dignitas, id. ib. 2, 4, 3: substructiones, id. ib.— Comp.: ludi sumptuosiores, Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 8, 6: cicercula, Col. 7, 3, 22.—Sup.: portum operis sumptuosissimi fecit, Suet. Ner. 9 fin.— Of persons, spending much, lavish, wasteful, extravagant, Plaut. Me

sumptus1.full: sumptus, a, um, Part. of sumo.

sumptus2.full: sumptus,, ūs (gen. sumpti, Cato, R. R. 22, 3; Lucil., Turp., Caecil., and Varr. ap. Non. 484, 30 sq.; Turp. ib. 132, 16; Plaut. Trin. 2, 1, 21; id. Cas. 2, 7, 2), m. sumo, II. D., expense, cost, charge (class.; used alike in sing. and plur.; cf. impendium): at tibi tanto sumptui esse mihi molestum'st, Plaut. Mil. 3, 1, 78: quor tu his rebus sumptum suggeris, Ter. Ad. 1, 1, 37; 3, 3, 16; 5, 3, 21: sine sumptu tuo, id. Eun. 5, 8, 46: perpetuos sumptus suppeditare, nec solum necessarios, sed etiam

sunamitis.full: Sunamītis, ĭdis, f., a Shunamite: puella, Hier Ep. 52, 2.
sunamitis.short: Sunamītis, ĭdis, f., a Shunamite: puella, Hier Ep.

sunium.full: Sūnĭum or Sūnĭon, ii, n., = Σούνιον, a promontory and town of Attica, now Capo Colonna, Mel. 2, 2, 8; 2, 3, 6; Cic. Att. 13, 10, 3; 7, 3, 10; Plin. 4, 7, 11, § 24; Ter. Phorm. 5, 5, 9; id. Eun. 3, 3, 13; Liv. 28, 8; 31, 22; 32, 17.—Form Sunion, Ov. F. 4, 563; Stat. Th. 12, 625.
sunium.short: Sūnĭum or Sūnĭon, ii, n., = Σούνιον, a promontory and town of Attica, now Capo Colonna, Mel.

sunuci.full: Sunuci, ōrum, m., a Belgic people, Tac. H. 4, 66; Plin. 4, 17, 31, § 106.
sunuci.short: Sunuci, ōrum, m., a Belgic people, Tac.

suo.full: sŭo, sŭi, sūtum, 3, v. a. Sanscr. siv-, sivjāmi, sew; Gr. κασσύω, to stitch, cobble, to sew or stitch, to sew, join, or tack together (rare but class.). Lit.: quod (foramen) nisi permagnā vi sui non potest, Cels. 7, 4, 3: tegumenta corporum vel texta vel suta, Cic. N. D. 2, 60, 150: unius os sutum, Flor. 4, 12, 36: pellibus et sutis arcent male frigora bracis, Ov. Tr. 3, 10, 19: hi plerasque naves loris suebant, Varr. ap. Gell. 17, 3, 4: navis suta lino et sparteis serilibus, Pac. ap. Fest. s. v

suovetaurilia.full: sŭŏvĕtaurīlĭa, or sōlĭtaurīlĭa, ĭum, n. sus-ovis-taurus; cf. Quint. 1, 5, 67 Spald.; Fest. p. 293 Müll., or sollus-taurus, a sacrifice consisting of a swine, a sheep, and a bull, offered esp. at lustrations: solitaurilia hostiarum trium diversi generis immolationem significant, tauri, arietis, verris, quod omnes eae solidi integrique sint corporis, etc., Fest. p. 293: Mars pater lustri faciendi ergo macte hisce suovetaurilibus lactentibus esto, an old formula of prayer, Cato, R. R. 141, 3 sq.; c

supellecticarius.full: sŭpellectĭcārĭus, a, um, adj. supellex, of or relating to household stuff or furniture: servi, that have the care of it, Dig. 33, 7, 12, § 31.

supellex.full: sŭpellex (nom. supellectilis, Eutr. 3, 23; Salv. Gub. Dei, 3, 2), lectĭlis (abl. -li or -le; v. Neue, Formenl. 1, 240), f. superlego, household utensils, stuff, furniture, or goods (class.; only in sing.; cf.: vasa, utensilia, instrumenta), Dig. 33, 10 (De supellectile legata), 1; 33, 10, 3; 33, 10, 7; Cato ap. Prisc. p. 782 P.; Varr. R. R. 1, 22, 6; Plaut. Aul. 2, 5, 17; id. Pers. 4, 8, 2; Ter. Phorm. 4, 3, 61; Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 34, § 83; 2, 4, 17, § 37; id. Agr. 2, 13, 32; 2, 15, 38; id. Par. 1

super2.full: sŭper, adv. and prep. Sanscr. upari; Gr. ὑπέρ; Goth. ufar, above, over (often confounded in MSS. and edd. with supra, q. v.). Adv., above, on top, thereupon, upon, etc. (rare but class.). Lit., of place: Anien infraque superque Saxeus, Stat. S. 1, 3, 20: eo super tigna bipedalia, iniciunt, Caes. B. C. 2, 10: haec super e vallo prospectant Troes, Verg. A. 9, 168: implenturque super puppes, from above, i. e. by rain, id. ib. 5, 697: purpureas super vestes ... Coniciunt, id. ib. 6, 221; cf. id. ib.

superabilis.full: sŭpĕrābĭlis, e, adj. supero, that may be got over or surmounted. * Lit.: murus, Liv. 25, 23, 12.— Trop., that may be overcome or subdued, conquerable, superable (very rare): non est per vim superabilis ulli, Ov. Tr. 5, 8, 27: invictos et nullis casibus superabiles Romanos praedicabant, Tac. A. 2, 25: an talis caecitas ac debilitas ope humanā superabiles forent, i. e. curable, id. H. 4, 81.

superabluo.full: sŭpĕr-ablŭo, ĕre, 3, v. a., to wash off above, Avien. Perieg. 881.

superabundantia.full: sŭpĕrăbundantĭa, ae, f. superabundo, superabunaance (late Lat.), Hier. in Ezech. 6, 18, 6; Vulg. Lev. 25, 37.

superabundo.full: sŭpĕr-ăbundo, āvi, 1, v. n., to be very abundant, to superabound (post-class.): ubi delictum abundaverit, illic gratiam superabundasse, Tert. Res. Carn. 34; 47; Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 14; Lact. Ep. 6, 13; Dig. 27, 1, 6.—Hence, sŭpĕrăbundanter, adv., very abundantly: facere omnia, Vulg. Eph. 3, 20.

superaccommodo.full: sŭpĕr-accommŏdo, āre, v. a., to fit on above, put on: ferulas, Cels. 8, 10, 1 fin.

superacervo.full: sŭpĕr-ăcervo, āre, v. a., to heap on, pile up, Tert. ad Nat. 1, 15.

superaddo.full: sŭpĕr-addo, no perf., dĭtum, 3, v. a., to add over and above, to superadd (poet.; now usu. written separately): tumulo superaddite carmen, Verg. E. 5, 42: laurus superaddita busto, Prop. 2, 13, 33 (3, 5, 17): vitis, Verg. E. 3, 38.

superadicio.full: sŭpĕr-ādĭcĭo, jēci, 3, v. a., to put in or add besides, to superadd (post-class.): quartam partem vini, Pall. Oct. 14, 15: piper his, Apic. 7, 4: decem dies observationi veteri, Macr. S. 1, 14.

superadmiro.full: sŭpĕradmīro, āre, 1, v. a., to admire or wonder at exceedingly (late Lat.), Facund. Defens. 2, 2.

superadornatus.full: sŭpĕr-ădornātus, a, um, Part. [adorno], further adorned, additionally ornamented: materia, Sen. Q. N. 4, 2, 18.

superadultus.full: sŭpĕr-ădultus, a, um, Part. [adulesco], fully mature, past the first period of maturity: virgo, Vulg. 1 Cor. 7, 36.

superaedificatio.full: sŭpĕraedĭfĭcātĭo, ōnis, f. superaedifico, a building upon, Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 6 fin.

superaedificium.full: sŭpĕr-aedĭfĭcĭum, ii, n., the upper building, Ambros. in Ep. ad Cor. 1, 3.
superaedificium.short: sŭpĕr-aedĭfĭcĭum, ii, n., the upper building, Ambros.

superaedifico.full: sŭpĕr-aedĭfĭco, āre, v. a., to build upon or over, Vulg. 1 Cor. 3, 12: operationem, Paul. Nol. Ep. 28; Ennod. Dict. 2; Aug. Civ. Dei, 21, 21; 21, 26.—Absol.: alius superaedificat, Vulg. 1 Cor. 3, 10.

superaggero.full: sŭpĕr-aggĕro, āre, v. a., to heap over with any thing: scrobem, Col. 12, 46, 4.

superalluo.full: sŭpĕr-allŭo (-adl-), ĕre, 3, v. a., to wash over, flow over, Prisc. Perieg. 881.

superambulo.full: sŭpĕr-ambŭlo, āre, v. a., to walk upon or over: calcatas undas (Dominus), Sedul. Carm. 3, 226.

superamentum.full: sŭpĕrāmentum, i, n. supero, a remainder, remnant: superamenta materiarum, Dig. 32, 1, 55, § 4.

superans.full: sŭpĕrans, antis, Part. and P. a., v. supero.

superantia.full: sŭpĕrantĭa, ae, f. supero, excess, predominance (late Lat.), Cael. Aur. Signif. Diaet. Pass. 9.

superappareo.full: sŭpĕr-appārĕo, ēre, 2, v. n., to appear above, Fulg. Myth. 2, 16.

superapparitio.full: sŭpĕrappārĭtĭo, ōnis, f. superappareo, an appearance above, Fulg. Myth. 2, 16.

superargumentans.full: sŭpĕr-argūmentans, antis, Part. [argumentor], arguing over and above, proving besides, Tert. adv. Herm. 37.

superaspergo.full: sŭpĕr-aspergo, ĕre, v. a., to scatter upon or over (late Lat.): farinam, Veg. Vet. 3, 3 med.: piperis pulverem, Apic. 4, 2; Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 1, 14: pardus albis maculis superadspersus, Isid. 12, 2, 19.

superasto.full: sŭpĕr-asto (-adsto), āre, 1, v. n., to stand over: superadstantium manibus adtollitur, Sall. H. Fragm. 1, 74 Dietsch.

superatio.full: sŭpĕrātĭo, ōnis, f. supero, an overcoming, conquering, Vitr. 3 praef. med.— An excess: fervoris, Theod. Prisc. 4, 2.

superator.full: sŭpĕrātor, ōris, m. supero, an overcomer, conqueror (Ovidian): populi Etrusci, Ov. F. 1, 641: Gorgonis (Perseus), id. M. 4, 699.

superatrix.full: sŭpĕrātrix, īcis, f. superator, she that conquers: CASTARVM, Inscr. Fabr. p. 383.

superaugmentum.full: sŭpĕr-augmentum, i, n., an additional or further increase, Isid. Orig. 6, 17, 23.
superaugmentum.short: sŭpĕr-augmentum, i, n., an additional or further increase, Isid.

superbia.full: sŭperbĭa, ae, f. superbus. In a bad sense, loftiness, haughtiness, pride, arrogance (syn.: arrogantia, insolentia, fastidium, fastus): num sibi aut stultitia accessit aut superat superbia? Plaut. Am. 2, 2, 77: magnitudinem animi superbia (imitatur) in animis extollendis, Cic. Part. Or. 23, 81: divitiae dedecoris plenae sunt et insolentis superbiae, id. Rep. 1, 34, 51: abicio superbiam, Plaut. Merc. 5, 2, 10: in rebus prosperis superbiam magno opere, fastidium arrogantiamque fugiamus, id. Off. 1,

superbibo.full: sŭper-bĭbo, ĕre, v. n., to drink upon or after, Plin. 23, 1, 23, § 42; Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 14, 110.

superbificus.full: sŭperbĭfĭcus, a, um, adj. superbusfacio, proud-making, that renders proud: manus, Sen. Herc. Fur. 58.

superbiloquentia.full: sŭperbĭlŏquentĭa, ae, f. superbusloquor, haughty or proud speaking, Poët. ap. Cic. Tusc. 4, 16, 35.

superbio.full: sŭperbĭo, īre, 4, v. n. superbus, to be haughty or proud, to take pride in a thing (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit.: si habes quod liqueat, neque respondes, superbis, * Cic. Ac. 2, 29, 94 Orell. (dub.; B. and K. and Halm, superbe): ut nostris tumefacta superbiat Umbria libris, Prop. 4 (5), 1, 63. avi nomine, Ov. M. 11, 218: patriis actis, id. H. 8, 43: formā multa superbit avis, id. Med. Fac. 34: formā, id. A. A. 3, 103: nimis triumviratu suo, Plin. 9, 35, 59, § 122: honore, Phaedr. 5

superbus.full: sŭperbus, a, um, adj. super; cf. Gr. ὑπέρβιος. In a bad sense, that thinks himself above others, haughty, proud, arrogant, insolent, discourteous, uncivil, rude, supercilious, domineering (cf.: arrogans, insolens, fastidiosus, vanus, elatus): reges odisse superbos, Poët. ap. Cic. Att. 6, 3, 7: reges, Lucr. 5, 1222: domini, id. 2, 1091; Verg. A. 12, 236: juvenis, id. ib. 3, 326; 10, 514: victor, id. G. 3, 226: non decet superbum esse hominem servom, Plaut. As. 2, 4, 64: freti virtute et viribus s

supercado.full: sŭper-cădo, cĕcĭdi, 3, v. n., to fall upon or over, Vulg. Psa. 57, 9; Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 3, 70.

supercaelestis.full: sŭper-caelestis, e, adj., that is above the heavens, super-celestial (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Anim. 23; id. Res. Carn. 49.
supercaelestis.short: sŭper-caelestis, e, adj., that is above the heavens, super-celestial (eccl.

supercalco.full: sŭper-calco, āre, v. a., to tread or stand upon: tabulatum, Col. 12, 39, 3.

supercerno.full: sŭper-cerno, ĕre, v. n., to sift upon or over: terram cribris, Plin. 17, 10, 14, § 74 (better superincerno).

supercerto.full: sŭper-certo, āre, 1, v. n., to fight over, to fight therefor, Vulg. Ep. Jud. 1, 3.

superciliosus.full: sŭpercĭlĭōsus, a, um, adj. supercilium, haughty, disdainful, supercilious; censorious, severe (post-Aug. and very rare), Sen. Ep. 123, 11; Arn. 1, 8; Mart. Cap. 8, § 809.

supercilium.full: sŭper-cĭlĭum, ii, n. super and root kal-; Gr. καλύπτω; Lat. celāre, to hide, cover; cf. Gr. κύλον, ἐπικύλιον, eyelid; cf. also, Ang.-Sax. hlid; Engl. lid; Germ. Augenlid: cilium est folliculus, quo oculus tegitur, unde fit supercilium, Fest. p. 43 Müll.; Plin. 11, 37, 57, § 157. Lit., the eye-brow (good prose; more freq. in the plur.). Plur.: ex superciliorum aut remissione aut contractione facile judicabimus, etc., Cic. Off. 1, 41, 146: supercilia abrasa, id. Rosc. Com. 7, 20: superiora superci

supercingo.full: sŭper-cingo, ĕre, 3, v. a., to cover over or in addition (late Lat.), Aug. Quaest. in Heptat. 2, 177, 3.

superclaudo.full: sŭper-claudo, ĕre, 3, v. a., to cover or close up (late Lat.), Adaman. Locc. Sanct. 1, 15.

supercompono.full: sŭper-compōno, ĕre, v. a., to place together upon or on the top: pisces, Apic. 4, 2 med.

superconcido.full: sŭper-concīdo, ĕre, v. a., to cut in pieces over: coliculorum minutias, Apic. 5, 5 fin.

supercontego.full: sŭper-contĕgo, xi, 3, v. a., to cover over: lapsos (herbida pondera), Sil. 16, 42: renes tunicis, Cels. 4, 1, 19.

supercorruo.full: sŭper-corrŭo, ĕre, v. n., to fall down thereon, Val. Max. 5, 6, 5.

supercreatus.full: sŭper-crĕātus, a, um, Part. [creo], grown on, adventitious: infusio umoris, Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 8, 125; Hilar. Trin. 6, 5.

supercresco.full: sŭper-cresco, crēvi, 3, v. n. and a. Neutr. Lit., To grow up, over, or upon: carcinoma, Cels. 5, 28, 2 fin.: caro, id. 5, 28, 22 init.—With dat., Serv. Verg. A. 3, 15.— Trop.: fortuna quod supercresceret caritati, i. e., might join, be added to, Quint. Decl. 5 14 fin.— Act., to excel, outdo: municipalem habitum, August. c. Acad. 1, 2.

supercubo.full: sŭper-cŭbo, āvi, 1, v. n., to lie or sleep upon, Col. 7, 4, 5; App. M. 6, p. 185, 34.

supercurro.full: sŭper-curro, ēre, v. n. Lit., to run over or beyond: baltei, Sid. Ep. 4, 20.— Trop., to surpass, exceed: large vectigali (ager), Plin. Ep. 7, 18, 3; Alcim. Ep. 18.

superdatus.full: sŭperdătus, a, um, Part., v. superdo.

superdeligo.full: sŭper-dēlĭgo (also separate, sŭper dēl-), āre, v. a., to bind upon or over: spongiam, Cels. 7, 7, 8 fin.
superdeligo.short: sŭper-dēlĭgo (also separate, sŭper dēl-), āre, v.

superdestillo.full: sŭper-destillo, āre, 1, v. n., to drop or trickle upon, Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 1, 18.

superdico.full: sŭper-dīco, ĕre, 3, v. n., to say in addition, Dig. 12, 2, 13 fin.

superdimidius.full: sŭper-dīmĭdĭus, a, um, adj.; of a number, half as much more (i. e. that bears to another the ratio of 3 to 2), Mart. Cap. 7, § 761 sqq.

superdo.full: sŭper-do, dĕdi, dătum, 1, v. a., to put or lay over (post-Aug.), Cels. 5, 28, 3 fin.; 5, 8, 7; Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 7 med.

super3.full: sŭper-dūco, xi, ctum, 3, v. a. (postclass.), to lead or draw over: pampinum, Sid. Ep. 5, 17 med.: novercam tot liberis, to bring or put over, Capitol. M. Aur. fin.: novercam filio, Quint. Decl. 38.— To add, subjoin, Tert. Anim. 36; id. Cor. Mil. 11.

superductio.full: sŭper-ductĭo, ōnis, f. super-duco, a drawing over, erasure, Dig. 28, 4, 1, § 1.

superedo.full: sŭpĕr-ĕdo, ĕre, v. a., to eat besides or after a thing: betae radicem, Plin. 19, 6, 34, § 113.

supereffero.full: sŭpĕr-effĕro, ef-ferre, v. irreg. a., to exalt, extol (late Lat.), Aug. in Psa. 49, 30.

super4.full: sŭpĕr-efflŭo, ĕre, v. n., to superabound, be superfluous (late Lat.), Ambros. in Psa. 118, Serm. 14, § 9: mensura, Vulg. Luc. 6, 38: quicquid, Paul. Nol. Carm. 35, 511: PECVNIA, Inscr. Murat. 1772, 8.— To be abundantly exalted above: legi supereffluit doctrina Christi, Ambros. in Luc. 5, 34.

super5.full: sŭpĕr-effulgĕo, ēre, 2, v. n., to be more than effulgent (late Lat.), Rustic. c. Aceph. p. 1250.

superegredior.full: sŭpĕr-ēgrĕdĭor, ĕdi, 3, v. a., to surmount (late Lat.): plebeias opiniones, Ambros. Ep. 6.

superelevo.full: sŭpĕr-ēlĕvo, āre, v. a., to raise above (late Lat.): se (iniquitates), Vulg. Esd. 4, 16, 77.

superemico.full: sŭpĕr-ēmĭco, āre, v. a., to spring or burst forth over a thing: terram (unda), Sid. Carm. 15, 75.

supereminentia.full: sŭpĕrēmĭnentĭa, ae, f. super-emineo, supereminence (late Lat.): dei, Aug. Serm. 40; id. Gest. Pelag. 30, 55; Ambros. Parad. 2, 8: laudis, Hilar. Trin. 11, 4.

super6.full: sŭpĕr-ēmĭnĕo, ēre, v. a. and n., to overtop, to appear or be above, to rise above (poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Act.: victor viros supereminet omnes, Verg. A. 6, 857: umero undas, id. ib. 10, 765: fluctus omnes, Ov. Tr. 1, 2, 49: quas omnes aspis supereminens, Amm. 22, 15, 27.— Neutr.: ut olivae premantur et jus superemineat, Col. 12, 49, 1; Sen. Q. N. 5, 15, 1: herba paulum supereminens extra aquam, Plin. 26, 8, 33, § 50 (al. semper eminens).—Hence, sŭpĕrēmĭnens, entis, P. a., rising above, p

superemorior.full: sŭpĕr-ēmŏrĭor, mŏri, v. dep. n., to die upon, Plin. 10, 2, 2, § 4.

superenato.full: sŭpĕr-ēnăto, āre, v. a., to swim over: amnem, Luc. 4, 133 Cort.: fluctus omnes, Alcim. Diluv. 4, 240.

supererectus.full: sŭpĕr-ērectus, a, um, Part. [erigo], standing overhead: sol, vertical, Amm. 20, 3, 10 dub.

supererogatio.full: sŭpĕr-ērŏgātĭo, ōnis, f., a payment in addition (late Lat.), Ps. Quint. Decl. 3; 6.
supererogatio.short: sŭpĕr-ērŏgātĭo, ōnis, f., a payment in addition (late Lat.), Ps.

supererogo.full: sŭpĕr-ērŏgo, āvi, 1, v. a., to spend or pay out over and above: si quid forte supererogasti, Cod. Just. 2, 19, 14; Vulg. Luc. 10, 35.

superevolo.full: sŭpĕr-ēvŏlo, āre, 1, v. a., to fly away over: Alpem, Luc. 3, 299.

superexactio.full: sŭpĕrexactĭo, ōnis, f. superexigo, a demanding over and above, an excessive demand, Cod. Just. 10, 20, De superexactionibus.

superexalto.full: sŭpĕr-exalto, āre, 1, v. n., to exalt above others, Vulg. Jacob. 2, 13. — Part.: superexaltatus deus, Aug. Conf. 3, 2.

superexcedo.full: sŭpĕr-excēdo, ĕre, 3, v. a., to surpass (late Lat.), Aug. Specul. 6.

super7.full: sŭpĕr-excellens, entis, adj., very excellent, superexcellent, Salv. adv. Avar. 3, 18.
super7.short: sŭpĕr-excellens, entis, adj., very excellent, superexcellent, Salv.

superexcurro.full: sŭpĕr-excurro, ĕre, v. n., to run or stretch over, to spread over, Dig. 43, 27, 1, § 2.

superexeo.full: sŭpĕr-exĕo, īre, v. n., to extend over, Aus. Idyll. 18, 1.

superexigo.full: sŭpĕr-exĭgo, ĕre, v. a., to demand or exact over and above, i. e. to excess: damna, Cod. Just. 1, 55, 4.

super8.full: sŭpĕr-exsulto, āre, 1, v. n., to leap up, exult greatly, Symm. Ep. 5, 92; Cassiod. Complex. ad Ep. Jacob. 5.

superextendo.full: sŭpĕr-extendo, ĕre, 3, v. a., to stretch over, cause to cover: in aliquo cutem, Vulg. Ezek. 37, 6. — To stretch excessively: nos, Vulg. 2 Cor. 10, 14.

superextollo.full: sŭpĕr-extollo, ĕre, v. a., to raise or exalt above others, Tert. Res. Carn. 24; Vulg. Psa. 71, 16.

superfero.full: sŭper-fĕro, ferre, v. a. To carry over or beyond, to place or put over (postAug.): pedem parturienti, Plin. 28, 8, 27, § 103. — Pass., to go, ride, fly, swim, etc., over: pisces, Plin. 9, 16, 25, § 58; App. de Mundo fin.; Tert. Bapt. 4; Mart. Cap. 8, § 882. — To carry over or beyond the time: periclitari partus, si superferatur, Plin. 32, 10, 46, § 133. — To raise high, carry over the head: aurum, Plin. 33, 4, 25, § 84.—Hence, sŭperlātus, a, um, P. a., extravagant, excessive, exaggerated: verba

super9.full: sŭper-fēto, āre, v. n., to conceive anew while still with young, to superfetate, Plin. 10, 63, 83, § 179; 7, 11, 9, § 48; 8, 55, 81, § 219.

superficialis.full: sŭperfĭcĭālis, e, adj. superficies, of or belonging to the surface, superficial (late Lat.). Lit.: numerus, denoting the superficial contents, Cassiod. Arithm. p. 555; Isid. 3, 7, 4.— Trop., superficial: officia, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 28.

superficiarius.full: sŭperfĭcĭārĭus, a, um, adj. id., situated on another man's land, superficiary (jurid. Lat.). Adj.: praedia, Dig. 10, 2, 10: aedes, ib. 43, 18, 2: mathematice, ut ita dicam, superficiaria est: in alieno aedificat, Sen. Ep. 88, 28. — Subst.: sŭper-fĭcĭārĭus, ii, m., one who has a house on another man's land, a superficiary, Dig. 6, 1, 74; 39, 2, 18; 43, 17, 3 med. al.

superficiens.full: sŭper-fĭcĭens, entis, P. a. super-facio, superfluous, Dig. 39, 3, 1, § 11.

superficies.full: sŭperfĭcĭes, ēi, f. super-facies, the upper side of a thing, the top, surface. In gen. (post-Aug.): testudinum, the upper shell, Plin. 6, 22, 24, § 91; 6, 24, 28, § 109; 9, 10, 12, § 35: sardonychum, id. 37, 6, 23, § 89: aquae, the surface, Col. 8, 15, 3: arborum, the part that grows above ground, id. 4, 11, 1; Plin. 16, 31, 56, § 130; 19, 4, 19, § 56; Col. 11, 3, 21: vitis, id. Arb. 10, 2; 4, 29, 13; 4, 11, 2: aedis, the roof, Plin. 34, 3, 7, § 13: Ὑπερῷον superficies, cenaculum, percula, Gloss

superficium.full: sŭperfĭcĭum, ii, v. superficies, II. A.

superfigo.full: sŭper-fīgo, ĕre, fixus, 3, v. n., to fasten up, fasten thereupon: superfixa capita hostium portantes redierunt, Liv. 42, 60, 2; Treb. Pol. Claud. 3, 5.

super10.full: sŭper-fīo, fĭĕri, v. n., to be over and above, to be left, to remain (very rare; not in Cic.): edepol te vocem (ad cenam) libenter, si superfiat locus, Plaut. Ep. 3, 2, 10; id. Mil. 2, 4, 3; id. Stich. 4, 2, 12; id. Trin. 2, 4, 108: quae superfieri possunt, Col. 12, 1, 5.

superflexus.full: sŭper-flexus, a, um, Part. [flecto], bent over: crates, Sid. Ep. 8, 12 med.

superflorescens.full: sŭper-flōrescens, entis, Part. [floresco], blossoming all over: sibi cucumis, Plin. 19, 5, 24, § 70.

super11.full: sŭper-flŭo, ĕre, v. n. and a. Neutr., to run over, overflow (mostly postAug.; only once in Cic.; syn. redundo). Lit.: in aeneo vase leniter coquuntur, ne superfluant, Cels. 6, 18, 2: fons superfluit, Plin. 31, 4, 28, § 51: superfluentis Nili receptacula, Tac. A. 2, 61: si (Nilus) immodicus superfluxit, Sen. Ben. 6, 7, 3. — Trop. To be superabundant, to superabound: pecunia non superfluens, Sen. Ben. 1, 11, 5: virgines, id. Contr. 1, 3, 4: populus, id. ad Helv. 6, 11: claritas, Plin. 4, 7, 11, §

superfluus.full: sŭperflŭus, a, um, adj. superfluo, running over, overflowing (post-Aug.). * Lit.: flumina campis, Plin. Pan. 82, 5. — Trop. Superfluous, unnecessary: invenissent forsitan necessaria, nisi et superflua quaesissent, Sen. Ep. 45, 4; Mamert. Grat. Act. ad Jul. 30: leges, Eutr. 10, 8: cura, Vulg. Eccl. 2, 26: superfluum et vanum orare pro mortuis, id. 2 Macc. 12, 44: multa superflua legisse memini, Vop. Aur. 5: species, Capitol. Ant. 8, 7.— That is left over, remaining: fructus superfluos restituere,

superforaneus.full: sŭperfŏrānĕus, a, um, adj. superforum, superfluous, unnecessary (late Lat.): labor, Symm. Ep. 3, 48 (al. supervacaneus): super his plura replicare, superforaneum puto, Sid. Ep. 4, 11 med.

superforo.full: sŭper-fŏro, āre, 1, v. a., to bore from above (late Lat.), Scrib. Comp. 84.

superfrutico.full: sŭper-frŭtĭco, āre, v. n., to sprout forth again; trop.: talia ingenia, Tert. adv. Valent. 39.

superfugio.full: sŭper-fŭgĭo, gĕre, v. a., to flee away over a thing: intactas levis ipse superfugit undas, Val. Fl. 3, 554.

superfulgeo.full: sŭper-fulgeo, ēre, v. a., to shine over a thing, to shine forth: templa superfulgens, Stat. S. 1, 1, 33.

superfundo.full: sŭper-fundo, füdi, fūsum, 3, v. a. To pour over or upon (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; not in Cic. or Cæs.). Lit.: hanc misturam cum composueris, oleum superfundito, Col. 12, 57, 1; 4, 8, 3: unguentum, Plin. Ep. 9, 33, 9: magnam vim telorum, Tac. Agr. 36.—Absol.: potius mare superfunderet adversus terrarum ereptores, Tac. A. 13, 55 fin.— Mid., to pour itself out, overflow; to spread out, scatter, extend: Tiberis ripis superfunditur, Plin. Ep. 8, 17, 1: Circus Tiberi superfuso irrigatus, L

superfusio.full: sŭperfūsĭo, ōnis, f. superfundo, a pouring or spreading over or upon (late Lat.): aquarum caelestium, Amm. 17, 7, 12: pavimenti, Pall. 1, 17, 1.— An overflowing: haec, Ambros. Hexaëm. 3, 3, 14: aquarum, id. ib. 3, 2, 7.

superfusus.full: sŭperfūsus, a, um, Part. of superfundo.

supergaudeo.full: sŭper-gaudĕo, ēre, 2, v. n., to rejoice over (late Lat.): alicui, Vulg. Psa. 34, 19; Ambros. Ep. 70, 20 fin.

supergenero.full: sŭper-gĕnĕro, āre, 1, v. a., to produce more and more (late Lat.): generatur et supergeneratur usura, increases by compound interest, Ambros. Tob. 13, 43.

super12.full: sŭper-gestus, a, um, Part. [gero]. * Carried or heaped upon or over: terra, Col. 11, 3, 6. — * Covered over, covered up: orificium, App. M. 9, p. 237.

supergloriosus.full: sŭper-glōrĭōsus, a, um, adj., exceedingly glorious, Vulg. Dan. 3, 53.
supergloriosus.short: sŭper-glōrĭōsus, a, um, adj., exceedingly glorious, Vulg.

super13.full: sŭper-grĕdĭor (sŭpergrădĭor, Plin. 27, 12, 68, § 110), gressus, 3, v. dep. a. and n. gradior, to step, walk, or go over (post-Aug.). Lit.: limen, Col. 7, 9, 13; Plin. 32, 10, 46, § 133: capram alteram decubuisse atque ita alteram proculcatae supergressam, Plin. 8, 50, 76, § 201.— Trop., to pass over, get over, surmount; to surpass, exceed, excel: aetatis suae feminas pulchritudine, Tac. A. 13, 45: omnem laudem supergressa, Quint. 6, prooem. § 8: claritatem parentum animi magnitudine, Just. 42, 2

supergressus1.full: sŭpergressus, a, um, Part. of supergredior and supergredio.

supergressus2.full: sŭpergressus, ūs, m. supergredior, a surpassing, exceeding: per supergressum, beyond measure, exceedingly, Tert. Res. Carn. 40.

superhabeo.full: sŭpĕr-hăbĕo, ēre, v. a., to have over or upon a thing: superhabendum cataplasma, Cels. 7, 20, § 7 (perhaps it should be written separate, super habendum).

superilligo.full: sŭpĕr-illĭgo, āre, v. a., to bind over or upon, Plin. 29, 3, 11, § 40; 30, 6, 17, § 51.

superillino.full: sŭper-illĭno (-inl-), no perf., lĭtum (collat. form superillinītum, App. Herb. 74), 3, v. a. To smear over, besmear, anoint with a thing: totum corpus bulbis contritis, Cels. 3, 19, 19.— To smear or spread a thing over another: idque superillitum panniculo imponendum est, Cels. 6, 18, 9: superinlito butyro ovillo cum melle, Plin. 30, 12, 37, § 111: sucus, App. Herb. 74.

superillitus.full: sŭperillĭtus, a, um, Part. of superillino.

super14.full: sŭper-immĭnĕo, ēre, v. n., to hang over, overhang (very rare): pastorem Ense sequens nudo superimminet, Verg. A. 12, 306: terrā superimminente, Sen. Q. N. 5, 15, 1: virgineusque pudor zonae superimminet artus, Avien. Arat. 962: mons superimminens, Hilar, in Psa. 124, 3.

superimmitto.full: sŭper-immitto, ĕre, v. a., to throw over or upon: jecur, Apic. 2, 1.

super15.full: sŭper-impendens, entis, Part. [impendeo], overhanging: silvae, Cat. 64, 287.

superimpendo.full: sŭpĕr-impendo, ĕre, 3, v. n., to spend or exhaust upon any thing, Vulg. 2 Cor. 12, 15 (transl. of ἐκδαπανάω).

superimpleo.full: sŭpĕr-implĕo, ēre, falsely assumed as v. a.: implenturque super puppes, Verg. A. 5, 697; v. super, I. A.
superimpleo.short: sŭpĕr-implĕo, ēre, falsely assumed as v.

superimpono.full: sŭpĕr-impōno (-inpōno), no perf., pŏsitum, 3, v. a., to put, place, or lay upon (not ante-Aug.): saxum ingens, Liv. 39, 50, 3: statua superimposita, id. 38, 56, 3: manum, Quint. 1, 1, 27: allium, Cels. 5, 27, 6: cataplasmata, id. 3, 10: radicem arundinis, id. 5, 26, 35: superinposito linteolo, Plin. 31, 9, 45, § 103; Stat. S. 1, 1.

superimpositus.full: sŭpĕrimpŏsĭtus, a, um, Part. of superimpono.

superincendo.full: super-incendo, ĕre, v. n., to inflame more or greatly: hanc (Venus), Val. Fl. 2, 124.

superincerno.full: sŭpĕrincerno, ĕre, 3, v. a. super-incerno, to sift upon, Plin. 17, 10, 14, § 74.

superincidens.full: sŭpĕr-incĭdens, entis, Part. [incido], falling from above, falling down: tela, Liv. 2, 10, 11: viri, id. 23, 15, 13: caelestis aqua, Col. 4, 9, 1.

superincido.full: sŭpĕr-incīdo, ĕre, v. a., to cut into above: cutem, Cels. 7, 31, 7.

superincresco.full: sŭpĕr-incresco, ĕre, v. n., to grow over or upon: nimius callus, Cels. 8, 19 fin.

superincubans.full: sŭpĕr-incŭbans, antis, Part. [incubo], lying over or upon: Romanus, Liv. 22, 51.

superincumbo.full: sŭpĕr-incumbo, cŭbŭi, 3, v. n., to lay or cast one's self upon, Ov. H. 11, 57; 11, 117.

superincurvatus.full: sŭpĕr-incurvātus, a, um, adj., bent or stooping over, App. M. 9, p. 220, 13.
superincurvatus.short: sŭpĕr-incurvātus, a, um, adj., bent or stooping over, App.

superindictum.full: sŭpĕr-indictum, i, n., an extraordinary impost (jurid. Lat.): de superindicto, Cod. Just. 10, 18; 10, 17, 1; 11, 74, 1.
superindictum.short: sŭpĕr-indictum, i, n., an extraordinary impost (jurid.

superinduco.full: sŭpĕr-indūco, xi, ctum, 3, v. a. Lit., to draw over, cover over (post-Aug.): corpus, Quint. 5, 8, 2 N. cr.: terram, Plin. 15, 17, 18, § 61: tabellas cerā delitā, Just. 2, 10, 14.— To cause to come upon, to bring upon: eis principes, Vulg. 2 Par. 33, 11: in nos magnum malum, id. Dan. 9, 12.— Trop., to mention afterwards, to add: dispositionem caeli, Tert. adv. Herm. 26.

superinducticius.full: sŭpĕrinductīcĭus or -tĭus, a, um, adj. superinduco, supposititious: fratres (with falsi), Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 3.

superinductio.full: sŭpĕrinductĭo, ōnis, f. id., an erasing any thing written, Dig. 28, 4, 1, § 1.

superinductus.full: sŭpĕrinductus, a, um, Part. of superinduco.

superindumentum.full: sŭpĕrindūmentum, i, n. superinduo, an ouler garment (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Res. Carn. 42; id. adv. Marc. 5, 12 al.

superinduo.full: sŭpĕr-indŭo, ŭi, ūtum, 3, v. a., to put on over other clothes (post-Aug.). Lit.: paenulam, Suet. Ner. 48; Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 12.— Trop.: superinduti substantiā aeternitatis, clothed with, Tert. Apol 48 fin.: in hac carne domicilium indui solet, id. Res. Carn. 42.

superindutus.full: sŭpĕrindūtus, a, um, Part. of superinduo.

superinfundo.full: sŭpĕr-infundo, no perf., fūsum, 3, v. a., to pour over or upon: aquam, Cels. 5, 25, 4; 3, 20: mel, id. 8, 4 fin.

superinfusus.full: sŭpĕrinfūsus, a, um, Part. of superinfundo.

superingero.full: sŭpĕr-ingĕro, no perf., gestum, 3, v. a., to bring upon, to casl or heap upon: acervos leguminum, Plin. 18, 30, 73, § 308: montem, Stat. S. 1, 1, 59: illapsae superingeruntur escae, Prud. Cath. 4, 87.—Poet.: ubi non umquam Titan superingerit ortus, i. e. does not pour down his morning beams, does not shine, Tib. 4 (5), 1, 157 (al. super egerit).

superingestus.full: sŭpĕringestus, a, um, Part. of superingero.

superinicio.full: sŭpĕr-īnĭcĭo, no perf., jectum, 3, v. a., to throw on or above, to cast over or upon (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): raras frondes, Verg. G. 4, 46: textum rude, Ov. M. 8, 640: terram, id. F. 5, 533: togas, id. ib. 6, 570: folia contrita et illita, Cels. 5, 26, 33: fimum, Plin. 17, 9, 6, § 53.

superinjectus.full: sŭpĕrinjectus, a, um, Part. of superinicio.

superinspicio.full: sŭpĕr-inspĭcĭo, cĕre, v. a., to oversee, to superintend (eccl. Lat.): sacra ecclesiae, Sid. Ep. 9, 3 med.; 6, 1.

superinsterno.full: sŭpĕr-insterno, strāvi, 3, v. a., to spread or lay over: tabulas, Liv. 30, 10, 5; Sil. 7, 28; cf. Verg. A. 2, 722.

superinstillo.full: sŭpĕr-instillo, āre, v. a., to drop upon: olei modicum, Apic. 4, 2 fin.

superinstrepo.full: sŭpĕr-instrĕpo, ĕre, v. n., to sound above: axis perfractis ossibus, Sil. 2, 186.

superinstructus.full: sŭpĕrinstructus, a, um, Part. of superinstruo.

superinstruo.full: sŭpĕr-instrŭo, no perf., ctum, 3, v. a., to build over or upon; to arrange over one another: ut concameratis superinstruas, Cod. Just. 8, 10, 1: ordines vasorum in altitudinem, Col. 9, 7, 3.

superinsultans.full: sŭpĕr-insultans, antis, Part. [insulto], leaping about upon, Claud. Gigant. 83.

superintego.full: sŭpĕr-intĕgo, ĕre, v. a., to cover over: ora fossarum, Plin. 18, 6, 8, § 47.

superintendo.full: sŭper-intendo, ĕre, v. n., to have the oversight of, to superintend (eccl. Lat.): ut ipsi superintendant et quasi custodiant populum, Aug. in Psa. 126, n. 3; id. Civ. Dei, 19, 19; Hier. Ep. 146, 1.

superintentor.full: sŭpĕrintentor, ōris, m. superintendo, an overseer, superintendent, Aug. in Psa. 126, n. 3.

superinundo.full: sŭpĕr-ĭnundo, āre, v. a., to overflow; trop.: ejusmodi eloquiis, Tert. Res. Carn. fin.

superinungo.full: sŭpĕr-ĭnungo, ĕre, v. a., to smear over, to besmear, anoint with any thing: oculos collyrio, Cels. 7, 7, 1; 7, 7, 2; 7, 7, 8; 6, 6, 1.

superinveho.full: sŭpĕr-invĕho, ĕre, v. a., to carry above or over: speciem monstri, Avien. Arat. 1157.

superirruo.full: sŭpĕr-irrŭo, ĕre, 3, v. n., to fall in upon or over: igni, Mar. Vict. Fratr. Machab. 263.

superius.full: sŭpĕrĭus, comp. Neutr. of superior, v. superus.— From supra, adv., q. v.

superjaceo.full: sŭper-jăcĕo, ēre, v. n., to lie over or upon: cataplasma, Cels. 8, 9, 18.

superjacio.full: sŭper-jăcĭo, jēci, jectum (superjactus, Sall. Fragm. ap. Non 503, 33; Tac. H. 5, 6), 3, v. a. To cast or throw over or upon (mostly post-Aug.; not in Cic. or Cæs.). Lit.: membra superjectā cum tua veste fovet, Ov. H. 16, 222: semina de tabulato, Col. 2, 17, 2: folia, id. 2, 1, 6: aggerem, Suet. Calig. 19: se rogo, Val. Max. 1, 8, 10; 6, 6, 1 fin.: ut ille ardentibus tectis superjaceretur, id. 3, 2, ext. 7: et superjecto pavidae natarunt Aequore damae, i. e. spread over the earth, overwhelming, H

superjacto.full: sŭper-jacto, āre, v. a. * To fling or toss up: infantes, Val. Max. 9, 2, 4.—* To spring over a thing: mugiles transversa navigia superjactant, Plin. 9, 15, 21, § 54.

superjactus.full: sŭperjactus, a, um, v. superjacio init.

superjectio.full: sŭperjectĭo, ōnis, f. superjacio. * Lit., a throwing over or on: vestium, Arn. 3, 108.— Trop., in rhet., an exaggeration, hyperbole, Quint. 8, 6, 67.

superjectus1.full: sŭperjectus, a, um, Part. of superjacio.

superjectus2.full: sŭperjectus, ūs, m. superjacio, a leaping upon, covering, Col. 6, 36, 4.

superjumentarius.full: sŭper-jūmentārĭus, ii, m., a superintendent of the drivers of beasts of burden, Suet. Claud. 2.
superjumentarius.short: sŭper-jūmentārĭus, ii, m., a superintendent of the drivers of beasts of burden, Suet.

superjungo.full: sŭper-jungo, ĕre, 3, v. a., to subjoin, add (late Lat.), Inc. Quaest. ex. Nov. Fest. 95.

superlabor.full: sŭper-lābor, bi, v. n. dep., to glide or run over (very rare): in aperto jacentes sidera superlabebantur, Sen. Ep. 90, 42; Sid. Ep. 1, 2 med.; Liv. 30, 25, 6 (dub.).

superlacrimo.full: sŭper-lăcrĭmo, āre, v. n., to weep or drop upon: vitis, Col. 4, 24, 16.

superlatio.full: sŭperlātĭo, ōnis, f. superfero. In rhet., an exaggerating, hyperbole: veritatis superlatio atque trajectio, Cic. de Or. 3, 53, 203; cf. Auct. Her. 4, 33, 44; Quint. 9, 2, 3; 9, 1, 29; 12, 10, 62: malignitatis, the highest degree, App. Dogm. Plat. 2, p. 20, 40.— In gram., the superlative: (soloecismus) per comparationes et superlationes, Quint. 1, 5, 45; Charis. p. 88 sq. P.

superlativus.full: sŭperlātīvus, a, um, adj. superlatus; in gram.: nomen, superlative, in the superlative degree, Charis. p. 87 P.; Prisc. p. 605 ib.— Hyperbolic, exaggerated: sententiae, Isid. 2, 21, 16. — Hence, adv.: sŭperlātīvē, superlatively, in the superlative, Charis. p. 87 P.

superlatus.full: sŭperlātus, a, um, Part. and P. a. of superfero.

superlaudabilis.full: sŭper-laudābĭlis, e, adj., extremely to be praised, Vulg. Dan. 3, 53; 3, 54.
superlaudabilis.short: sŭper-laudābĭlis, e, adj., extremely to be praised, Vulg.

superlimen.full: sŭperlīmen, ĭnis, n. super-limen, a lintel, Plin. 29, 4, 26, § 83: LAPIDEVM, Inscr. Marin. Fratr. Arv. p. 324.

superliminare.full: sŭperlīmĭnāre, is, n. superlimen, a lintel, Vulg. Exod. 12, 23.— Plur., Vulg. Amos, 9, 1 (transl. of the Heb. ); id. Exod. 12, 7.

superlino.full: sŭper-lĭno, no perf., lĭtum, 3, v. a., to daub or smear over (post-Aug.). To daub or smear a thing over something: radicem in vino decoctam, Plin. 27, 6, 24, § 42. — To smear over, besmear with something: laser visco, ut haereat, Plin. 22, 23, 49, § 103: dolium, Pall. Oct. 14, 5.

superlitio.full: sŭperlĭtĭo, ōnis, f. superlino, a smearing over, Marc. Emp. 8 med.

superluceo.full: sŭper-lūcĕo, ēre, 2, v. n., to shine (late Lat.), Hier. in Psa. 89.

superlucror.full: sŭper-lucror, āri, 1, v. a., to gain in addition: talenta, Vulg. Matt. 25, 20.

superlugeo.full: sŭper-lūgĕo, ēre, 2, v. n., to mourn over in addition (late Lat.), Aug. in Job, 27.

supermando.full: sŭper-mando, ĕre, v. a., to chew or eat after something else: raphanos, Plin. 31, 6, 33, § 65.

supermeo.full: sŭper-mĕo, āre, v. n. and a., to go, glide, or flow over: aquae, Plin. 2, 103, 106, § 224; Amm. 24, 1, 7; Sol. 37 med.

supermetior.full: sŭper-mētĭor, mensus, 4, v. dep. a., to mete out abundantly: alimenta, Tert. Anim. 38.

supermico.full: sŭper-mĭco, āre, v. a., to leap over or beyond: austrum, Avien. 845.

supermitto.full: sŭper-mitto, mīsi, 3, v. a., to throw or pour over or upon; to put in afterwards, add, etc (post-class.): aquam, Just. 12, 14, 9; Curt. 10, 4, 20; Apic. 5, 3, § 194; 2, 1, § 40.

supermolaris.full: sŭper-mŏlāris, e, adj.: lapis, the upper millstone, Ambros. Tob. 21, 83.
supermolaris.short: sŭper-mŏlāris, e, adj.: lapis, the upper millstone, Ambros.

supermundialis.full: sŭper-mundĭālis, e, adj., that is above the world, supermundane: substantiae, Tert. Anim. 18.
supermundialis.short: sŭper-mundĭālis, e, adj., that is above the world, supermundane: substantiae, Tert.

supermunio.full: sŭper-mūnĭo, īre, v. a., to fortify or protect above: alvearia porticibus, Col. 9, 7, 4.

supernans.full: sŭper-nans, nantis, Part. [no], swimming above or at top, Macr. S. 7, 12.

supernas.full: sŭpernas, ātis, adj. supernus, of or belonging to the upper country, upper or northern, as regards Rome (post-Aug.): Caretini (opp. infernates), Plin. 3, 12, 17, § 106: abies, i. e. growing on the Upper or Adriatic Sea (opp. infernas, of the Tyrrhene Sea), id. 16, 39, 76, § 197: persica e Sabinis, id. 15, 12, 11, § 40: VINVM, Inscr. Rein. cl. 3, n. 88; cf. Inscr. Orell. 995: ventus, the northeast-by-north wind, Vitr. 1, 6.—Augustus jestingly called Maecenas adamas supernas (as the Adriatic produ

supernato.full: sŭper-năto, āre, v. n., to swim above or on top, to float (post-Aug.), Col. 12, 9, 2; Plin. 7, 15, 13, § 65; 28, 9, 35, § 134; App. M. 6, p. 180, 36; Paul. Nol. Carm. 21, 179.— With dat.: arieti (Phryxum), App. M. 6, p. 185, 33.

supernatus.full: sŭper-nātus, a, um, Part. [nascor], growing over or above: gravia ulcera, Cels. 8, 2: caule, Plin. 19, 3, 15, § 45.

supernitas.full: sŭpernĭtas, ātis, f. supernus, highness, height: supernitatum, Tert. adv. Val. 7

supernomino.full: sŭper-nōmĭno, āre, v. a., to surname: quem Philadelphum, Tert. Apol. 18.

supernumerarius.full: sŭper-nŭmĕrārĭus, a, um, adj., supernumerary (post-class.): accensi, hoc est postea additi, quam fuisset legio completa, quos nunc supernumerarios vocant, Veg. Mil. 2, 19 fin.; Aug. in Psa. 146, 9.
supernumerarius.short: sŭper-nŭmĕrārĭus, a, um, adj., supernumerary (post-class.): accensi, hoc est postea additi, quam fuisset legio completa, quos nunc supernumerarios vocant, Veg.

supernumero.full: sŭper-nŭmĕro, āre, 1, v. a., to count in over and above (late Lat.), Primas ad Apoc. 3, ad. 9, 16.

supernus.full: sŭpernus, a, um, adj. super, that is above, on high, upper; celestial, supernal (mostly post-Aug.; not in Cic. or Cæs.): pars oris, Plin. 7, 16, 15, § 69: vulnera, id. 2, 56, 57, § 147: Tusculum, lofty, i. e. standing on high ground, Hor. Epod. 1, 29; cf.: ballistae in humiliora ex supernis valentes, Amm. 19, 7, 5: superna (opp. inferna), Lucr. 5, 647: jactus ex supernis in infima, Gell. 9, 1, 2: album mutor in alitem Superna, above, Hor. C. 2, 20, 11 Muret. (al. superne): aquilones, qui alti su

supero.full: sŭpĕro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a. [id.]. Neutr., to go over, to rise above, overtop, surmount. Lit. (very rare; syn. transcendo): maximo saltu superabit gravidus armatis equus, surmounted, leaped the wall, Enn. ap. Macr. S. 6, 2 (Trag. v. 97 Vahl.): sol superabat ex mari, Plaut. Stich. 2, 2, 41: ripis superat mihi atque abundat pectus laetitia meum, id. ib. 2, 1, 6: jugo superans, passing over the summit, Verg. A. 11, 514: superat agger ad auras, Stat. Th. 4, 458: (angues) superant capite et ce

superobductus.full: sŭpĕr-obductus, a, um, Part. [obduco], drawn over: pallium, Paul. Nol. Carm. 22, 110.

superobruo.full: sŭpĕr-obrŭo (usually separate, sŭ-per obrŭo), ŭi, ŭtum, 3, v. a., to cover over, overwhelm (very rare): Tarpeiam ingestis armis, Prop. 4 (5), 4, 91. Hecubam injectis saxis, Aus. Epit. 25.
superobruo.short: sŭpĕr-obrŭo (usually separate, sŭ-per obrŭo), ŭi, ŭtum, 3, v.

superobrutus.full: sŭpĕrobrŭtus, a, um, Part. of superobruo.

superobumbro.full: sŭpĕr-ŏbumbro, āre, 1, v. a., to overshadow (late Lat.), Mar. Merc. Cyrill. Incarn. Unigen. 14.

superoccidens.full: sŭpĕr-occĭdens, entis, Part. [occido], setting just after: luna soli antecedenti, Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 18 med.

superoperio.full: sŭpĕr-ŏpĕrĭo, īre, 4, v. n., to cover over (late Lat.), S. S. Psa. 105, 17, ap. Aug. ad loc.

superordinatio.full: sŭpĕr-ordĭnātĭo, ōnis, f., the choice of a bishop's successor, Ambros. Ep. 12, 5.
superordinatio.short: sŭpĕr-ordĭnātĭo, ōnis, f., the choice of a bishop's successor, Ambros.

superordino.full: sŭpĕr-ordĭno, āre, 1, v. a., to appoint in addition, to add something to: testamentum, Vulg. Gal. 3, 15; Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 4.

superparticularis.full: sŭper-partĭcŭlāris, e, adj.: numerus, containing a number and an aliquot part of it besides, superparticular, Mart. Cap. 7, § 761.
superparticularis.short: sŭper-partĭcŭlāris, e, adj.: numerus, containing a number and an aliquot part of it besides, superparticular, Mart.

superpartiens.full: sŭper-partĭens, entis, Part. [partio]: numerus, containing a number and several aliquot parts of it besides, Mart. Cap. 7, § 762.

superpendens.full: sŭper-pendens, entis, Part. [pendeo], overhanging: saxa, Liv. 37, 27, 7.

superperspicio.full: sŭpĕr-perspĭcĭo, cĕre, 3, v. n., to look away over, Sol. 6.

superpeto.full: sŭper-pĕto, ĕre, 3, v. a., to ask further (late Lat.), Ven. Fort. Vit. Leob. 6.

superpictus.full: sŭperpictus, a, um, Part. of superpingo.

superpingo.full: sŭper-pingo, no perf., pictus, 3, v. a., to paint above or over (late Lat.), Sol. 17; Avien. Arat. 906.

superplaudo.full: sŭper-plaudo, ĕre, v. n., to clap or flap over or at a thing: pinnulis, Sol. 2 fin.

superpolluo.full: sŭper-pollŭo, ŭi, 3, v. a., to cover with pollution: omnem terram (iniquitas), Vulg. Esd. 4, 15, 6.

superpondium.full: sŭperpondĭum, ii, n. super-pondus, an overweight, App. M. 7, p. 196, 2.

superpono.full: sŭper-pōno, pŏsŭi, pŏsĭtum, 3, v. a., to put or place over or upon, to set up (perh. not ante-Aug.). Lit. In gen.: superpositum capiti decus (i. e. pileus), Liv. 1, 34: altissimam turrim congestis pilis, Suet. Claud. 20 fin.: statuam marmoream Jano, id. Aug. 31: villam profluenti, Col. 1, 5, 4; cf.: villa colli superposita, Suet. Galb. 4: ut omnis materia jugo superponatur, Col. 4, 25, 4: vitis, quae uno jugo superponatur, id. 5, 5, 15: aegra superpositā membra fovere manu, Ov. H. 21, 190: deser

superpositio.full: sŭperpŏsĭtĭo, ōnis, f. superpono, a paroxysm in disease, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 13, 179 al.

superpositus.full: sŭperpŏsĭtus, a, um, Part. of superpono.

superpostulatio.full: sŭper-postŭlātĭo, ōnis, f., an additional demand, Cod. Th. 7, 4, 28.
superpostulatio.short: sŭper-postŭlātĭo, ōnis, f., an additional demand, Cod.

superquartus.full: sŭper-quartus, a, um, adj.; of a number, one fourth as much more (i. e. that bears to another the ratio of 5 to 4): numerus, Mart. Cap. 7, § 761 sq.

superquatio.full: sŭper-quătĭo, ĕre, v. a., to shake above, or over and above, Avien. Arat. 1205.

superquintus.full: sŭper-quintus, a, um, adj.; of a number, one fifth as much more (i. e. which bears to another the ratio of 6 to 5): numerus, Boëth. Arithm. 1, 24; Mart. Cap. 7, § 761 sq.

superrasus.full: sŭper-rāsus, a, um, Part. [rado], scraped over: clavi pedum, Plin. 22, 23, 49, § 104.

superruo.full: sŭper-rŭo, ere, v. a. and n., to fall or rush upon; act.: Socratem, App. M. 1, p. 109, 31. — Neutr.: corpori, App. M. 2, p. 126.—Absol., Amm. 16, 12, 53.

supersapio.full: sŭper-săpĭo, ĕre, v. n., to possess very good taste, Tert. Anim. 18.

superscando.full: sŭper-scando (sŭperscendo), ĕre, v. a., to climb or step over (rare; not anteAug.): somno strata corpora, Liv. 7, 36, 2: sentes, Col. 11, 3, 7: ubi prostrato superscenditur, Tert. Poen. 10.

superscendo.full: sŭperscendo, ĕre, v. the preced. art.

superscribo.full: sŭper-scrībo, psi, ptum, 3, v. a., to write upon or over, to superscribe (postAug.), Dig. 28, 4, 1; 50, 10, 4; Schol. Juv. 6, 123.— Esp., to write over as a correction, Suet. Ner. 52 fin.; Gell. 20, 6, 14.

superscriptio.full: sŭperscriptĭo, ōnis, f. superscribo, an inscription, superscription, Vulg. Matt. 22, 20; id. Luc. 23, 38; Schol. Juv. 5, 34; Hilar. in Psa. 63, 1.

supersedeo.full: sŭper-sĕdĕo, sēdi, sessum, 2, v. n. and a., to sit upon or above. Lit. (very rare; not in Cic. or Cæs.): eques Romanus elephanto supersedens, Suet. Ner. 11: tentorio (aquila), id. Aug. 96: corio (damnati), Amm. 23, 6, 82: utribus, id. 25, 8, 2.—With acc.: ansam (aspis), App. M. 11, p. 262, 29. — Trop. * To preside over: vilicus litibus familiae supersedeat, i. e. decide them, Cato, R. R. 5, 1.— To be above or superior to, to forbear, to refrain or desist from, to pass, omit (the predom. and clas

supersellium.full: sŭpersellĭum, i, n., a shabrack: quod sellam tegebat, Vita Caes. 2, 2, 20.
supersellium.short: sŭpersellĭum, i, n., a shabrack: quod sellam tegebat, Vita Caes.

superseminator.full: sŭpersēmĭnātor, ōris, m. supersemino, one who sows upon or in addition, Tert. Anim. 16 fin.

supersemino.full: sŭper-sēmĭno, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a., to sow upon or over (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Prax. 1 med.; Hier. Ep. 30, 14.

supersero.full: sŭper-sĕro, sēvi, 3, v. a., to sow over or upon, to sow in addition, Hilar. in Psa. 127, 11; Arn. ib. 55.

supersessus.full: sŭpersessus, a, um, Part. of supersedeo.

supersiliens.full: sŭper-sĭlĭens, entis, Part. [salio], leaping or alighting upon: volucris, Col. 8, 3, 7.

supersisto.full: sŭper-sisto, stĭti, 3, v. a., to place one's self upon or over, to stand upon or over (post-class.): tribunal ligneum, App. M. 11, p. 269, 9: sicarium, id. ib. 8, p. 206, 20: caeremoniali scientiae, Amm. 29, 1, 31.

superspero.full: sŭper-spēro, āvi, 1, v. n., to hope exceedingly, Vulg. Psa. 118, 43; 118, 74.

superspersus.full: sŭper-spersus, a, um, Part. [spargo], strewn or sprinkled over (late Lat.): gemma stellis puniceis, Sol. 27 med.: camelopardalis candidis maculis, id. 30 med.; Arn. 7, p. 280.

superstagno.full: sŭper-stagno, āvi, 1, v. n., to spread out into a lake: si amnis Nar in rivos deductus superstagnavisset, Tac. A. 1, 79.

superstatumino.full: sŭper-stătūmĭno, āre, v. a., to place above as a foundation: rudus, Pall. 1, 9, 4.

supersterno.full: sŭper-sterno, no perf., strātum, 3, v. a., to strew or spread upon, to spread over, cover over (very rare): pavimenta testacea, Col. 1, 6, 13: superstrati cumuli, Liv. 10, 29, 19: fossam ponte solubili, Amm. 16, 8, 10.

superstes.full: sŭperstĕs, ĭtis, adj. super-sto. One who stands by or is present at any thing, a by-stander, witness (only in the foll. passages): superstites testes praesentes significat, cujus rei testimonium est, quod superstitibus praesentibus ei, inter quos controversia est, vindicias sumere jubentur. Plautus in Artemone: nunc mihi licet quidvis loqui, nemo hic adest superstes, Fest. p. 305 Müll.; cf. Serv. Verg. A. 3, 339: suis utrisque superstitibus praesentibus istam viam dico: inite viam, an old legal

superstillo.full: sŭper-stillo, āre, v. a., to drop upon, pour on drop by drop: oleum, Apic. 8, 7 fin.; 9, 13; Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 1, 18.

superstitio.full: sŭperstĭtĭo, ōnis, f. super-sto; orig a standing still over or by a thing; hence, amazement, wonder, dread, esp. of the divine or supernatural. Excessive fear of the goas, unreasonable religious belief, superstition (different from religio, a proper, reasonable awe of the gods; cf.: religio veri dei cultus est, superstitio falsi, Lact. 4, 28, 11): horum sententiae omnium non modo superstitionem tollunt, in quā inest timor inanis deorum, sed etiam religionem, quae deorum cultu pio continetur, Cic

superstitiosus.full: sŭperstĭtĭōsus, a, um, adj. superstitio, full of superstition, superstitious. Lit.: ita factum est in superstitioso et religioso alterum vitii nomen alterum laudis, Cic. N. D. 2, 28, 72: nimium esse superstitiosum non oportere, id. Dom. 40, 105: isti philosophi superstitiosi et paene fanatici, id. Div. 2, 57, 118: principes, Liv. 6, 5, 6: nimiā et superstitiosā religione sese alligaverat, Nigid. ap. Gell. 4, 9, 2: sollicitudo, Cic. Div. 2, 41, 86: in omni divinatione imbecilli animi facile super

superstito.full: sŭperstĭto, āre, v. a. and n. superstes. * Act., to keep alive, preserve: regnumque nostrum ut sospitent superstitentque, Enn. ap. Non. 170, 14; 176, 3 (Trag. v. 331 Vahl.).—* Neutr., to be over or remaining: ut mihi supersit, suppetat, superstitet, Plaut. Pers. 3, 1, 3.

supersto.full: sŭper-sto, āre, v. n. and a., to stand upon or over (perh. not ante-Aug.): signa cum columnis, quibus superstabant, Liv. 40, 2, 2: columnae (statua), Suet. Galb. 23: essedis carrisque (hostis), Liv. 10, 28, 9: ruinis (armati), id. 38, 7, 5: corporibus hostium, id. 7, 24, 5: cumulus caesorum, id. 22, 59, 3: rupibus, id. 37, 27, 8: superstantes propugnaculis celsis, Amm. 20, 6, 4: (quem) lapsum superstans Immolat, Verg. A. 10, 540: ossa inhumata (volucres), Ov. H. 10, 123: corpora atque arma simul

superstratus.full: sŭperstrātus, a, um, Part. of supersterno.

superstrictus.full: sŭperstrictus, a, um, Part. of superstringo.

superstringo.full: sŭper-stringo, xi, strictum, 3, v. a., to bind or draw together above or over (postclass. and very rare): manus accurate, App. M. 11, p. 263, 31: latera, Sid. Ep. 4, 20.

superstructus.full: sŭperstructus, a, um, Part. of superstruo.

superstruo.full: sŭper-strŭo, xi, ctum, 3, v. a., to build upon or over, to superstruct (postAug. and very rare): ligneam compagem, Tac. A. 4, 62: moles, Sen. Contr. 1 prooem. fin.: quidquid his (fundamentis) superstruxeris, corruet, Quint. 1, 4, 5: desuper pulvillis superstruunt, App. M. 10, p. 248, 27.

supersubstantialis.full: sŭpersubstantĭālis, e, adj. supersubstantia, necessary to support life: panis, Vulg. Matt. 6, 11.

supersubstantivus.full: sŭpersubstantīvus, a, um, adj., supermaterial (eccl. Lat.): Christus nec substantiva nec insubstantiva, sed supersubstantiva res est, Rustic. c. Aceph. p. 1184.

supersum.full: sŭper-sum, fui, esse (old collat. form of the pres. superescit, Enn. and Att. ap. Fest. p. 302 Müll.; per tmesin: jamque adeo super unus eram, Verg. A. 2, 567: nihil erat super, Nep. Alcib. 8, 1), v. n. To be over and above, either as a remainder or as a superfluity (class. and very freq.; cf. supero, B. 3.). As a remainder, to be left, to remain, to exist still. In gen.: dum quidem unus homo Romanus toga superescit, Enn. ap. Fest. p. 302 Müll. (Ann. v. 486 Vahl.): inde sibi memorat, unum supere

supertectus.full: sŭpertectus, a, um, Part. of supertego.

supertego.full: sŭper-tĕgo, xi, ctum, 3, v. a., to cover above, cover over: candidaque ossa super nigra favilla tegit (per tmesin), Tib. 3, 2, 10: vasa congestu culmorum et frondium, Col. 9, 14, 14: aliquid testa, Pall. Mart. 9, 3: me tunicā, App. M. 11, p. 263, 34: plures frondibus, Just. 43, 4, 6; Veg. Mil. 2, 25.

supertendo.full: sŭpĕr-tendo, ĕre, 3, v. n., to stretch or strain above (late Lat.): in augmento tumores supertendunt, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 9.

superterrenus.full: sŭper-terrēnus, a, um, adj., that is above the earth, superterrene, Tert. Res. Carn. 49.
superterrenus.short: sŭper-terrēnus, a, um, adj., that is above the earth, superterrene, Tert.

supertertius.full: sŭper-tertĭus, a, um, adj.; of a number, one third as much more (i.e. that bears to another the ratio of 4 to 3): numerus, a transl. of the Gr. ἐπίτριτον, Censor. de Die Nat. 10, 8; 10, 11; Mart. Cap. 7, § 761 sq.

supertextor.full: sŭper-textor, ōris, m., a chief-weaver (late Lat.), Mar. Merc. Procli. Hom. Sect. 3.
supertextor.short: sŭper-textor, ōris, m., a chief-weaver (late Lat.), Mar.

supertollo.full: sŭpĕr-tollo, ĕre, 3, v. a., to raise above, Commod. Instr. 61, 2.

supertraho.full: sŭper-trăho, ĕre, v. a., to draw over: crates dentatas, Plin. 18, 18, 48, § 173.

supertranseo.full: sŭper-transĕo, īre, v. n., to pass over (late Lat.), Ambros. in Psa. 37, 29.

superumerale.full: sŭpĕr-umerale (-humer-), is, n. umerus, the upper garment of a Jewish priest, a transl. of Heb. , an ephod, Vulg. Exod. 28, 4; Hier. Ep. 29, 4; 64, 15.

superunctio.full: sŭpĕrunctĭo, ōnis, f. superungo, a smearing or anointing over, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 4, 34.

superunctus.full: sŭpĕrunctus, a, um, Part. of superungo.

superundo.full: sŭpĕr-undo, āre, v. n., to overflow; trop.: gratia, Paul. Nol. Carm. 18, 183.

superungo.full: sŭpĕr-ungo, xi, ctum, 3, v. a., to smear or anoint over (medical), Cels. 7, 7, 1; Scrib. Comp. 29; Ambros. Ep. 80, 4.

superurgens.full: sŭpĕr-urgens, entis, Part. [urgeo], pressing from above: fluctu superurgente, Tac. A. 2, 23 fin.

superus.full: sŭpĕrus, a, um (ante-class. collat. form of the nom. sing. sŭpĕr in two passages: super inferque vicinus, Cato, R. R. 149, 1: totus super ignis, Lucr. 1, 649; gen. plur. in signif. I. B. 1. infra, superūm, Verg. A. 1, 4; Ov. M. 1, 251 et saep.), adj. super. Posit. Adj. In gen., that is above, upper, higher: inferus an superus tibi fert deus funera, Liv. And. ap. Prisc. p. 606 P.: at ita me di deaeque superi atque inferi et medioxumi, Plaut. Cist. 2, 1, 36: omnes di deaeque superi, inferi, Ter. P

supervacaneus.full: sŭper-văcānĕus, a, um, adj. vacuus, over and above what is necessary, needless, unnecessary, superfluous, supervacaneous (class.): vasa, supernumerary, extra, Cato, R. R. 12: opus, i. e. done at leisure hours, Cic. Sen. 16, 56: litterae, id. Att. 16, 2, 5: commemoratio officiorum, id. Fam. 3, 5, 1: oratio, Liv. 22, 39: defensio Pauli, id. 45, 37: iter, id. 21, 13: actio, Just. 11, 12 fin.: instituta (opp. necessaria), Suet. Rhet. 1: quicquid supervacaneum sit, aut usum non habeat, obstare, Cic.

supervaco.full: sŭper-văco, āre, v. n., to be superfluous, Gell. 1, 22, 3.

supervacue.full: sŭpĕrvăcŭē, adv., v. supervacuus, fin. b.

supervacuitas.full: sŭpervăcŭĭtas, ātis, f. supervacuus, vainglory, Vulg. Sap. 14, 14.

supervacuo.full: sŭpervăcŭō, adv., v. supervacuus, fin. a.

supervacuus.full: sŭper-văcŭus, a, um, adj., useless, needless, unnecessary, superfluous, redundant (not ante-Aug.; while supervacaneus is class.): omne supervacuum pleno de pectore manat, Hor. A. P. 337: non tam obest audire supervacua quam ignorare necessaria, Quint. 12, 8, 7: carnes, Plin. 32, 7, 24, § 69: coma, id. 16, 36, 64, § 158: radix, id. 25, 9, 64, § 111: frondes, Col. 5, 5, 19: mihi Baias Musa supervacuas Antonius facit, of no benefit, Hor. Ep. 1, 15, 3: sepulcri honores, id. C. 2, 20, 24: metus, Ov.
supervacuus.short: sŭper-văcŭus, a, um, adj., useless, needless, unnecessary, superfluous, redundant (not ante-Aug.;

supervado.full: sŭper-vādo, ĕre, v. a., to go or climb over, to surmount (very rare): omnes asperitates, Sall. J. 75, 2: ruinas muri, Liv. 32, 24, 5: munimenta, id. 31, 38, 4.

supervaganea.full: sŭpervăgānĕa dicebatur ab auguribus avis quae ex summo cacumine vocem emisisset, dicta ita, quia super omnia vagatur aut canit, Fest. pp. 304 and 305 Müll.
supervaganea.short: sŭpervăgānĕa dicebatur ab auguribus avis quae ex summo cacumine vocem emisisset, dicta ita, quia super omnia vagatur aut canit, Fest.

supervagor.full: sŭper-văgor, ātus, 1, v. dep. n., to wander too far, spread too much, of vine creepers, Col. 4, 21, 1; 4, 22, 4.

supervaleo.full: sŭper-vălĕo, ēre, 2, v. n., to surpass greatly (eccl. Lat.), Vulg. Ecclus. 43, 32.

supervector.full: sŭper-vector, āri, v. dep. n., to pass or hover over: spiritus ab initio, Tert. Bapt. 4.

superveho.full: sŭper-vĕho, vexi, 3, v. a., to carry over: cumulis montibusque harenarum supervectis (i. e. by the wind), Gell. 16, 11, 7.

supervehor.full: sŭper-vĕhor, vectus, 3, v. dep. n., to go, ride, sail, etc., over or past (very rare): montem, Cat. 66, 43: promontorium Calabriae, Liv. 42, 48, 7: arma tua, Aus. Epigr. 24, 2: eos universos montibus harenarum supervectis operuisse, Gell. 16, 11, 8.— To ride, ride upon: pullo asinae, Ambros. in Luc. 8, 59.

supervenio.full: sŭper-vĕnĭo, vēni, ventum, 4, v. n. and a., to come over or upon, to come to or in addition to, to overtake, to come up, arrive, come upon, fall upon (not ante-Aug.). Lit. In gen. Act.: et heres Heredem alterius, velut unda supervenit undam, follows after, presses upon, Hor. Ep. 2, 2, 176: crura loquentis Terra supervenit, closed over, covered, Ov. M. 10, 490: vineae superveniunt jugum, Col. 4, 22. 1: planitiem supervenit umor, id. 2, 17 fin.: si festinaret sequi, palantes superventurum, Curt. 5

superventio.full: sŭperventio, ōnis, f. supervenio, a coming up (late Lat.), Petr. Chrysol. Serm. 12.

superventores.full: sŭperventōres, um, m. supervenio, a kind of soldiers (perh. employed in sudden attacks), Amm. 18, 9, 3.

superventus.full: sŭperventus, ūs, m. id., a coming up or upon, an arrival (post-Aug.). In gen., Plin. 7, 15, 13, § 64; Tac. H. 2, 54.— In partic., in milit. lang., an attack, Veg. Mil. 3, 8; 3, 22.

supervestio.full: sŭper-vestĭo, ītus, 4, v. a., to clothe upon, clothe, Aug. Civ. Dei, 14, 3; Vulg. 2 Cor. 5, 4: maleficos homines taedā et papyro, Schol. Juv. 1, 156; Arn. in Psa. 38.

supervinco.full: sŭper-vinco, ĕre, v. a., to overcome, conquer (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Gnost. 13; Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 6, 46.
